scope.summary: The outer layer is the author's catalogue of causal arisings in complexity levels and phases, joined by causes that remain author hypotheses until evidence supports them; every technical record belongs to the subgraph of exactly one arising. Partial reconstruction of Level-0 definitions and scoped physical, chemical, biochemical, cellular, organismal, optical, retinal, visual and neural evidence. Levels organize the display; they do not establish a universal emergence order. Formal specifications, computational models, experimental preparations, observations and conditional interpretations have distinct roles. Each scientific claim retains its reviewed sources, selected system, observable, uncertainty, shared inputs and unresolved limitations. Field and particle models remain distinct from detector response, lattice calculations and conditional parameter extraction. Nuclear and atomic masses, primordial abundances and cosmological spectra retain their source-specific calibration, model and covariance limits. Atomic and molecular binding, prepared-state spectroscopy, charge production, electrolyte screening and stationary electronic representations address different questions; their energy comparisons do not by themselves establish formation kinetics, universal stability or a unique ancestry. Optical and neural records distinguish measured response from anatomy, intervention and theoretical interpretation. Cellular organization, state regulation, fate and immune responses retain preparation-specific perturbations, finite persistence, partial rescue, contrary outcomes and corrected controls. Model-derived metabolic flux and inferred immune networks remain distinct from measured readouts. Tissue morphogenesis, repair, extracellular mechanics, physiological coordination, retinal organization and inflammatory states retain their distinct preparation, timing, resource and endpoint boundaries. Adult observations and finite perturbations do not establish universal developmental generators, immune allocation optima, organism-wide set-points or hysteresis. Behavioral success and fitted models do not identify a unique mechanism. Finite checks reproduce only their declared data or mathematical witnesses, not entire experiments. Cross-domain construction, downward causation and a derivation of quantum theory from Level 0 remain unestablished. Reviewed descriptive bridges record the definitions, measurement principles, interpretation boundaries and topic scopes that records share across evidence islands and levels; they establish no construction, causation or level order. Source discrepancies and unreproduced stages remain explicit. No whole-graph scientific validation is claimed. Neural-system topics have explicit source-bound scope decisions: anatomy, effective signaling, memory tasks, glial/molecular/vascular interfaces and subjective reports retain distinct observables. Contextual treatment and conditioning contrasts do not establish universal psychosomatic pathways, healing, physical minima or a unique conscious mechanism. Social-system topics have explicit source-bound scope decisions. Animal interactions, human tasks, observed population associations, formal models and constitutive documents retain distinct evidence roles. Collective labels, laboratory effects and documentary rules do not establish universal social minima, weighted necessary chains, irreducibility or a measured society-wide neural mechanism.

review.limit: The released ratios are a fitted-normalization data product, with spline-derived error scaling; they are not a temporally prior independent input to that same fit. The cross-section ratios already incorporate acceptance and radiation modeling, Feshbach Coulomb correction and spline-fit normalization. They are not raw counts or independently measured absolute Born cross sections. Standard-dipole normalization is a model input. The 31 normalization parameters enter shared products. Equation 48 multiplies data and error by their product; ancillary Section 4 uses the reciprocal nuisance-parameter convention on the model. Their numerical parameter values are not interchangeable. Column 6 contains already-scaled point-to-point errors, not counting errors to scale a second time. The 315-MeV acquisition uses the current-based luminosity estimate after a monitor-setting problem. Kinematics must use the acceptance-averaged Q^2 and beam energy, not the central spectrometer angle. Multiplying columns 5-8 by column 9 undoes the applied Coulomb correction. Columns 12-18 change model normalization; the systematic variations in column 10 require new fits, not new observations.

sources.title: On Quantum-Electrodynamics and the Magnetic Moment of the Electron

review.limit: The actual two-page scan was read and visually inspected only for the Schwinger letter beginning on page 416 and ending on page 417. The neighboring letters on calcium and silver are excluded. The letter is dated 30 December 1947 and was published in 1948. Schwinger's two-page 1948 letter announces a leading perturbative magnetic correction with renormalized experimental mass and a separate discussion of charge renormalization. In its Gaussian-unit convention alpha=e^2/(hbar*c), the displayed correction becomes a_e^(1)=alpha/(2*pi). The historical decimal 0.001162 is not a modern precision prediction; no undocumented alpha input or loop calculation is reconstructed. Atomic-moment and atomic-energy examples mentioned in the letter are not admitted as separately reviewed experiments. The leading anomalous moment is not a statement that all radiative effects are vacuum polarization, that virtual excitations are an observed particle population, or that the vacuum is a material substance. The low-order formula does not reproduce modern higher-order QED, lepton, hadronic or weak contributions, nor does Fan's experimental extraction require the Schwinger term as a calibration input.

sources.title: Finite free-mode evolution and stationary-vacuum algebra

locators: verify(), flow(), vacuum_word() and correlation(): exact rational positive-frequency oscillator flow, formal commutator and Hamiltonian identities, vacuum moments, common time shifts and unequal-time controls
review.limit: The local oscillator has unit mass, positive omega, and an adopted infinite Fock representation with a|0>=0. The massless zero-frequency mode is excluded. Its 2 by 2 matrices act on coefficients of q and p, not on a finite-dimensional quantum state space; no finite matrix representation of [q,p]=i is claimed. Two rational positive frequencies and five rational unit-circle phases give ten exact mode checks and fifty composition/common-shift checks. A phase pair denotes cos(omega*t), sin(omega*t); no rational elapsed time is assigned and no arbitrary-time numerical integration or continuum field evolution is reproduced. A symplectic squeeze preserves the canonical commutator but changes this Hamiltonian and vacuum covariance. Attenuation without added operators fails a closed canonical map; this does not exclude physical open-system channels with environmental or noise degrees of freedom. A one-mode unequal-time commutator proves no spacelike microcausality or signal-propagation theorem.

limitations: Bilateral hippocampal antisense injections reduce the named transporter in tissue. They are not genetically restricted to a cell class. Astrocytic MCT4 and neuronal MCT2 attribution uses expression evidence; direct cell-to-cell lactate flux was not measured in these behavioral assays.

ODNs were injected 1 h before training; rescue L-lactate (100 nmol) or equicaloric glucose (50 nmol) was injected 15 min before training. Retention was tested at 24 h and 7 days, with 1 h short-term testing in a separate MCT2 assay.

The behavioral endpoint is inhibitory-avoidance entry latency. Supplementary animal, surgical and task procedures and Tables S4-S5 remain unread: age, sex, shock protocol and exact group statistics are not independently established here.

Figure 6 and the MCT2 Results report no lactate rescue; a Discussion sentence inconsistently lists MCT2 among rescued knockdowns. Other Results sentences pair significant impairment with p > 0.05. No numerical inference is derived from those inconsistent passages.

Rescue does not uniquely establish lactate as an exclusive energy substrate; redox, signaling and other metabolic explanations remain possible. The failed equicaloric glucose rescue is dose- and protocol-specific, not proof that glucose can never support retention.

The behavioral endpoint is inhibitory-avoidance entry latency. Supplementary animal, surgical and task procedures and Tables S4-S5 remain unread: age, sex, shock protocol and exact group statistics are not independently established here.

limitations: The preparation is the developing mouse retinogeniculate system. Engulfment is assayed at P5, segregation at P10/P30 and synaptic puncta at P32-35. Adult maintenance, immune surveillance, disease and all brain regions are not established by these developmental endpoints.

TTX/forskolin are intraocular pharmacological manipulations; CTB labeling follows 4-5 h later. Left-eye drug and right-eye vehicle inputs are compared within selected dLGN regions. Relative labeled-input engulfment is not a direct measurement of every synapse firing rate.

CR3/CD11b and C3 knockouts are developmental whole-animal genotypes. Local attribution to microglia is supported by CR3 expression and absence of other CR3-positive cells in the inspected P5 dLGN; the manipulation is not a microglia-restricted inducible knockout.

CTB-positive volume inside reconstructed microglia, projection overlap and juxtaposed VGlut2/GluR1 puncta are distinct anatomical observables. They do not directly measure synaptic efficacy or prove one exclusive sequence of activity, complement tagging and engulfment.

Engulfment is reduced, not abolished, in CR3/C3 knockouts. Complement-independent and nonphagocytic mechanisms remain possible. Raw images, complete supplementary methods and the updated supplementary document remain unread; sex is not established by the selected main methods.

limitations: Both male and female mice at least seven weeks old were used; exact age and sex distributions per assay group are not supplied. No randomized animal allocation, blinded investigation or prospective statistical sample-size calculation is reported. The reporting summary discusses stimulus ordering separately; it does not establish randomized animal groups.

FOS labeling is an activity-associated marker; Vglut2-cre bulk GCaMP6s is a population calcium signal, not a DBH-specific spike recording. Photometry uses saline on day 4 and LPS on day 5 in the same animals. Vagotomized mice form a separate group after two weeks of recovery; a matched abdominal sham is not explicitly specified in the reviewed procedure. Figure 1c reports residual responses after an approximately 80% reduction.

LPS doses differ across assays: 50 micrograms/kg for FOS and TRAP, 0.5 mg/kg for the main photometry comparison, 0.1 mg/kg for cytokine chemogenetics and 12.5 mg/kg for survival. These exposures are not interchangeable. LPS endotoxaemia is distinct from viable bacterial infection.

Descending efferent routes and immune effector cells remain unresolved. A whole-animal Myd88 knockout does not isolate immune-cell-specific mediation. Lower circulating inflammatory cytokines do not imply universally better defense: sustained TRPA1-population activation increased Salmonella tissue burden in the separate live-infection assay.

Raw measurements, animal identifiers and custom code have not been obtained or replayed. Exclusion criteria include unsuccessful targeting/expression/ablation, but counts and operational thresholds are incomplete. Extended Data 9c reports Gpr65 IL-6 P=0.03 despite a broad no-appreciable-effect conclusion; its small plotted decrease must not be turned into an all-population null. No numerical edge weight or universal carrier count is assigned.

claims.statement: The main 0.5 mg/kg LPS challenge increased bulk Vglut2-cre cNST calcium-response area relative to the preceding saline session. Fixed session order and a population fluorescence measurement limit causal and cellular interpretation.

limitations: Female C57BL/6 mice were four to five weeks old at housing allocation and received virus one week later. Of 58 recorded GFP-positive cells, 13 from 13 mice had neuronal physiology; 45 were nonexcitable and not all individually identified. The 13/58 fraction is a selected recording yield, not an unbiased neuronal differentiation probability. Unlabeled comparison neurons were not birthdated.

The SA immature-cell comparison is significant against HA and AD, but not against YA or PCI at the table adjusted-P threshold of 0.05. These distinct contrasts neither prove no difference nor establish that generating neurons preserves memory.

The study measures morphology and output transmission, not behavior. Proposed recruitment of existing spines is a cross-sectional interpretation, not an observed minimal construction rule or proof of memory necessity.

The manipulation reduces Bax-dependent cell death in the Nestin stem/progenitor lineage; it is not a selective increase in birth rate or a dentate-newborn-neuron-only intervention. Olfactory-bulb survival also changes. Reporter recombination is a proxy, and altered cell properties or other lineage effects remain alternative mediators.

Main Figure 2c alternates the order of contexts across days, whereas the discrimination Methods describe training context A followed one hour later by similar context B. The exact per-animal schedule requires reconciliation. The nine-day ratio analysis reports treatment P=0.023; its day F/degree-of-freedom/P combination also needs correction. Handling of a zero sum of freezing scores is unspecified.

Contextual freezing discrimination is a behavioral proxy for pattern separation, not a direct measurement of DG neural population codes or general memory improvement. Supplementary protocol variants have treatment P=0.38 and P=0.06 despite interactions or day-specific differences; they cannot be pooled as uniformly positive main effects.

Supplementary Figure 14 reports an overall discrimination-ratio treatment P=0.1 and interaction P=0.3. Late within-group differences are not a between-group necessity test. Its day-five F(1,14)=4.34/P=0.04 pair needs reconciliation; no replacement biological P value is calculated here.

The paper explicitly leaves functional significance untested. No electrical recording, identified synaptic output, behavioral mediation or selective birth-cell perturbation establishes functional integration in these human samples. Findings in mouse integration experiments cannot supply those missing human measurements.

Whole hippocampi were analyzed; the investigators could not separately radiocarbon-date hippocampal subdivisions. Dentate localization and absolute cell-number scaling rely on other histological and stereological studies. The approximately 700 neurons per day in each hippocampus and 0.004% of dentate neurons per day are model-dependent estimates, not directly counted daily births.

No human electrical, identified synaptic-output or selective behavioral assay is performed. Similar estimated rates across species do not supply human functional integration or a birth-to-cognition mechanism. Histology, isotope dating, molecular markers and rodent interventions remain distinct evidence.

No electrical, synaptic-output, learning or memory assay was performed. A possible cognitive role, stable-memory benefit or recovery mechanism remains untested. Labeling in this study does not require an injury or learning manipulation.

Specific rat learning protocols alter retained birth labels; a separate macaque study supplies age-limited neuronal colabels. Neither establishes a universal learning prerequisite or a selective newborn-neuron requirement for memory.

Rakic (1985) and Eckenhoff and Rakic (1988) propose that stable neurons preserve learned information. Their autoradiographic nulls contain no matched memory test and appear to share specimens. This proposed stability mechanism and later renewal-benefit hypotheses are not adjudicated by histology alone.

Pattern separation, temporal context and memory resolution remain nonexclusive interpretations. Behavioral discrimination, population-code decorrelation and temporal association require different measurements; review schematics cannot choose among them.

Main scientific text, Materials and Methods, and Figures 1-5 with captions are reviewed. Supplemental Figures 1-2 were not obtained or read. Animal-identified image stacks, custom IgorPro routines and the allocation/exclusion manifest were not obtained; no imaging or biological experiment was independently reproduced.

Photothrombosis used Rose Bengal 100 milligrams per kilogram intraperitoneally and 532-nanometer illumination, 17 milliwatts for fifteen minutes, under ketamine-xylazine. Sham controls omitted either dye or illumination. Per-assay sham composition, random allocation and group-specific age distributions are not supplied in the reviewed account.

Imaging under urethane was acute: hourly stacks over six, occasionally seven hours, after a one-, two- or six-week recovery interval, followed by terminal histology. Separate cohorts do not trace the same spine or dendritic arbor continuously from before injury through six weeks.

Only laterally projecting spines were scored. New spines had to protrude at least four pixels, approximately 0.55 micrometers, and remain present at the six-hour endpoint. Transient events, filopodium conversions, shifted segments and poor-quality images were excluded. The assay is not a census of all spine births, losses or synapses.

Turnover is reported as a percentage of the counted spine population over the imaging session; raw animal-level numerator/denominator assignments are unavailable. Spine density is a count per ten micrometers of dendrite. Neither measure is a neuron birth rate, a universal hourly turnover constant or a calibrated graph weight.

Turnover scoring was blinded to experimental condition, but movement, abnormal breathing and image deterioration could exclude experiments; exclusion counts and animal identifiers are not supplied. Axial optical resolution was about 5.3 micrometers, much poorer than lateral resolution, and six spine-appearance cases were pooled across animals for shaft-fluorescence controls.

Spine morphology and adjacent sensory-evoked reflectance do not measure the functional efficacy of each new synapse, selective memory content or behavioral recovery. The Discussion explicitly leaves the causal link between increased formation and recovered function unestablished.

The main text gives a 0.14 percent control formation mean and 1.37, 0.93 and 0.75 percent poststroke means. The abstract describes a five- to eight-fold peak increase; these rounded quantities do not define one exact fold estimate. Retain the reported assay means without calibrating a universal multiplier.

Nonsignificant outcomes are not equivalence or full recovery. Photothrombosis does not permit controlled reperfusion, and the paper does not directly establish the same time course in other stroke models, traumatic injury or humans.

limitations: Five cancer patients received diagnostic BrdU labeling; one patient with similar cancer and no BrdU served as a staining control. This is an observational autopsy series, not a randomized intervention on neurogenesis or a healthy-population survey.

A single intravenous infusion contained 250 mg BrdU in 100 ml saline. No anticancer therapy was given before or during labeling and no cerebral metastases were found at autopsy. Later treatment, full clinical histories, sex-specific sampling, postmortem intervals and selection or exclusion counts are not reconstructable from the report.

BrdU marks DNA synthesis and subsequent label retention. The neuronal-marker interpretation supports candidate adult-born cells under the labeling assumptions; the images do not continuously observe cell division, trace a clone or selectively exclude every nonmitotic DNA-synthesis mechanism.

NeuN, NSE and calbindin were alternative neuronal stains with BrdU and GFAP, not three independent birthdating assays or necessarily three labels on each same cell. Reported neuronal percentages use BrdU-positive cells as denominator, not all neurons. At least twenty BrdU-positive cells per patient were examined; exact marker-specific denominators and patient-level counts are unavailable.

BrdU/GFAP-positive cells and cells lacking the selected phenotype markers were also observed. Marker-negative cells cannot be assigned automatically to a quiescent stem-cell lineage, and fractions from different marker assays cannot be added as disjoint cell classes.

The paper explicitly leaves functional significance untested. No electrical recording, identified synaptic output, behavioral mediation or selective birth-cell perturbation establishes functional integration in these human samples. Findings in mouse integration experiments cannot supply those missing human measurements.

limitations: Five cancer patients received diagnostic BrdU labeling; one patient with similar cancer and no BrdU served as a staining control. This is an observational autopsy series, not a randomized intervention on neurogenesis or a healthy-population survey.

A single intravenous infusion contained 250 mg BrdU in 100 ml saline. No anticancer therapy was given before or during labeling and no cerebral metastases were found at autopsy. Later treatment, full clinical histories, sex-specific sampling, postmortem intervals and selection or exclusion counts are not reconstructable from the report.

BrdU marks DNA synthesis and subsequent label retention. The neuronal-marker interpretation supports candidate adult-born cells under the labeling assumptions; the images do not continuously observe cell division, trace a clone or selectively exclude every nonmitotic DNA-synthesis mechanism.

The paper explicitly leaves functional significance untested. No electrical recording, identified synaptic output, behavioral mediation or selective birth-cell perturbation establishes functional integration in these human samples. Findings in mouse integration experiments cannot supply those missing human measurements.

All main scientific text and Methods were read in the author-uploaded public full text; all five publisher figures and captions were inspected. The publisher full PDF was not obtained. Raw sections, image stacks, individual counts and analysis code have not been reproduced. The small clinical series does not establish an invariant rate, every adult age or a universal structural-construction rule.

Whole hippocampi were analyzed; the investigators could not separately radiocarbon-date hippocampal subdivisions. Dentate localization and absolute cell-number scaling rely on other histological and stereological studies. The approximately 700 neurons per day in each hippocampus and 0.004% of dentate neurons per day are model-dependent estimates, not directly counted daily births.

No human electrical, identified synaptic-output or selective behavioral assay is performed. Similar estimated rates across species do not supply human functional integration or a birth-to-cognition mechanism. Histology, isotope dating, molecular markers and rodent interventions remain distinct evidence.

Global neuronal 2POP fitting reports a renewing fraction near 0.35, with a reported 95% interval of 0.12-0.63. For nonneuronal cells the main text reports 0.51 with interval 0.22-0.88, accepted Table S2 gives 0.56, and individual fits fix 0.55. These summaries must not be treated as one exactly reproduced estimate.

The reported individual medians, 1.75% per year for neurons and 3.5% for nonneuronal cells, apply within fixed renewing fractions of 0.35 and 0.55 after the stated exclusions. Global-fit rates of about 12% and 4.9% per year in Tables S3 and S2 are different estimands. Unfittable samples were excluded from the individual 2POP analysis; Figure 2C/5A additionally states plot limits below 0.001 or above 1.5.

The accepted supplement distinguishes unpaired 2POP comparison (51 neuronal and 64 nonneuronal fractions, rank-sum P=0.005) from 40 matched pairs (signed-rank P=0.054; neuronal median 1.5%, nonneuronal 3.5% per year). The latter null does not establish equal rates. Comparing these tests without their populations and denominators would be misleading.

Age associations use cross-sectional, model-derived rates: reported neuronal r=-0.31, P=0.03 and nonneuronal r=-0.35, P=0.04. They do not trace the same people over time or identify an age intervention. The sex comparison P=0.41 does not establish equivalence. The DCX overlay uses an external Knoth cohort, not birthdating of the same cells.

The accepted supplement prints a heuristic labeled AIC, p + log2(SSE), and requires a halving of SSE per added parameter. Applying that printed rule to rounded Table S2 gives 0.31 > 0.51/2, so its nonneuronal 2POP preference does not follow from that rule. Table S3 has 0.17 < 0.49/2 for neurons. This arithmetic checks reporting consistency only; final supplementary methods, likelihood and code remain unverified.

The source says subjects born around 1955-1965 discriminate 2POP from homogeneous age-dependent alternatives; without them the scenarios could not be distinguished. MCMC explores bounded parameter sets, and fitting several scenarios does not prove a unique biological mechanism. Full numerical replay and out-of-sample discrimination have not been performed.

The fitting procedure assumes a one-year food lag and development beginning six months before birth. Its weighted SSE squares weights of 1 or 2 assigned around a 10-microgram carbon boundary. Table S1 has both estimated DNA carbon mass and reactor-measured mass, including ND entries. The exact mass choice, boundary treatment and missing-value policy require executable code before reproducing the fit.

The supplement explicitly does not explore population feedback: birth and death rates do not depend on the population state. Constant population size in replacement scenarios is imposed by their birth boundary, not observed emergence of a stabilizing rule. Population turnover does not identify one-for-one functional replacement, circuit topology or a universal minimal assembly.

limitations: BrdU and PCNA label DNA synthesis or cell-cycle-associated profiles; they do not continuously observe completed cytokinesis or a clone. PCNA was examined in sections from the same brains, not as a second independent animal cohort or a reported same-cell BrdU/PCNA lineage assay. Apposed doublets suggest, but do not identify, sibling relationships.

O4 or CNP double labeling used sequential black nuclear and brown cytoplasmic peroxidase signals in ethanol-fixed paraffin sections of 8 or 10 micrometres. Figure 3 shows 27-day single-injection examples. These preparations are distinct from the 32-day neuronal fluorescence assay; marker-positive morphology does not measure myelin formation or conduction.

Astrocyte generation is attributed to Eckenhoff and Rakic (1988) and Eriksson et al. (1998), not a newly reported GFAP assay in this experiment. Finding several phenotypes near one niche does not establish a shared multipotent founder, self-renewal or exclusive stem-cell lineage. The 1988 GFAP/autoradiographic assays are separately reviewed and do not trace a common founder.

Bipolar morphology and radial or tangential orientation support a migration interpretation but do not track displacement, origin or a radial-glial guidance interaction. Nearby cells are not a clone, and anatomical resemblance to developing neurons is not an executed construction rule.

No electrical, synaptic-output, learning or memory assay was performed. A possible cognitive role, stable-memory benefit or recovery mechanism remains untested. Labeling in this study does not require an injury or learning manipulation.

limitations: Adult male Sprague Dawley rats weighed 300-350 g; chronological age is not stated. Group sizes are generally five or six. The paper does not provide a complete animal manifest or randomized assignment procedure. Coded histology is reported, not complete blinding of every procedure.

BrdU was 200 mg/kg; the injection route is not specified. In the main experiments labeling occurred one week before four consecutive training days, with separate terminal cohorts 24 hours or seven days after training. The approximate three-week label-age wording does not exactly specify elapsed days. Separate sacrificed cohorts do not track individual cells longitudinally.

Trace conditioning used 200 trials per day for four days, an 83-dB 250-ms noise, a 500-ms gap and a 100-ms 0.7-mA shock. Unpaired rats received the same stimulus counts without explicit pairing. All paired animals reached 60% conditioned responses; none of the unpaired animals did. Complete naive-group electrode and handling matching is not specified.

Delay conditioning uses a 320-ms noise coterminating with an 80-ms shock and a different conditioned-response window. Trace and delay differ in stimulus durations and scoring as well as temporal gap. The reported F(1,19)=4.24, P=0.05 is called nonsignificant; this boundary result and final-day similarity are not statistical equivalence.

Hippocampal dependence is imported from prior lesion literature and, for the exact rat trace protocol, unpublished lesion data. No matched hippocampal lesion or selective newborn-cell manipulation is performed in this histology study. The graph links the specified task protocol to its measured outcome, not generic hippocampal necessity.

limitations: Twelve rhesus monkeys were labeled at reported ages of six months to eleven years; Table 1 gives ages at death of seven months to seventeen years. This is a mixed developmental and adult sample, not twelve animals labeled after puberty. Age at death cannot substitute for age at injection.

One to seven injections of tritiated thymidine were given at 10 mCi/kg. This is radioactivity per body mass, not the later BrdU mass dose. The injection route is not stated. The narrative survival range is three days to more than six years; the table includes 6.3 years. Repeated exposures and long retention windows are not independent animals or instantaneous birth rates.

Table 1 describes six-digit dates as day/month/year, although entries such as 013183 require month/day/year. Under that interpretation case 11 ends with injection 011976 and death 012376, four elapsed days rather than the printed fourteen. Case 7 gives 043069 to 050269, two elapsed days versus three printed; inclusive dating may matter. The original dates and intervals remain unreconciled.

Between 500 and 1000 sections per animal were screened across major brain regions and spinal cord, followed by brightfield or Nomarski examination with a 63x oil objective. The estimated million cells per specimen is not an exact neuronal denominator, random whole-brain census or statistical upper bound on rare births. Table 1 specifies 8-micrometre sections and every second to tenth section depending on region size.

Heavy labeling was calibrated separately in each case from glial, endothelial or peripheral cells, usually more than 15-30 silver grains per nucleus. Light-microscopic autoradiography exposure was 12-18 weeks and electron-microscopic exposure exceeded 24 weeks. A common fixed threshold cannot be imposed retrospectively. Occasional neuronal profiles with fewer than five or six grains were not classified as newborn; artifact or DNA repair was proposed without a repair assay.

Figure 1D-E and Figure 2 use a seven-month-old animal, with Figure 2 explicitly labeled at six months. These images are juvenile examples. Oligodendroglial labels were mostly reported at six and eighteen months, with only occasional postpubertal examples. Selected dentate GFAP and ultrastructural analysis is described without a complete case-by-assay manifest or independent neuronal-marker panel.

The memory and fixed-neuron-population interpretation has no behavioral, electrical, synaptic-output or selective neuron-replacement assay. The macaque null does not establish a general absence in humans or a necessary stable-neuron mechanism for memory.

Case identifiers and adult schedules in Eckenhoff and Rakic (1988) correspond to Table 1 death dates here. Publications and repeated injections cannot be counted as independent biological replications without reconciling specimen identity. The 1983 abstract and in-preparation work cited in reference 6 are not themselves the 1988 full article.

Table 1 contains four adult animals aged five, ten, ten and seventeen years at collection. Their seven, three, five and one injections total sixteen exposures, not sixteen independent animals.

Methods specifies six early developmental animals with one intravenous 5-10 mCi/kg tritiated-thymidine injection and one-hour survival. Table 1 instead prints one day for these rows. The eleven additional animals are described as surviving five weeks to two years, while Table 1 includes fourteen days, three years and six years. No adult one-hour cohort is documented; early developmental sampling cannot supply an adult short-interval null.

Left hemispheres were sectioned at 8 micrometres and exposed for 10-18 weeks. Heavy light-microscopic labeling is more than half the maximum grain count in the most intensely labeled cells of each case. Electron microscopy uses four nuclear grains under low-background conditions. These distinct assay thresholds must not be merged with each other or with the 1985 threshold.

Postnatal short-interval and longer-survival groups contain different animals. Approximately 150 sections across three longer-survival ages yielded eight profiles classified morphologically as definitive granule neurons, only one in P90-P155. These are sampled profiles, not eight animals, a clonal lineage or a daily birth rate; Nissl morphology has acknowledged identity limits.

No lineage tracing identifies whether phenotypes arise from separate committed founders or a common multipotent founder. The discussion allows other glial lines, undifferentiated cells and potential neuronal differentiation under other conditions. Regional co-occurrence and GFAP phenotype cannot close a precursor-to-neuron construction rule.

For adult cases 112883, 012980, 012376 and 021583, ages, injection counts and survival correspond to Rakic (1985) cases 12, 10, 11 and 8. A negative GFAP profile need not be a neuron; technical false negatives and other glial or precursor identities remain possible.

The five-year-old seven-injection animal has about two labeled profiles per ten sections at three months, all small SGZ profiles without typical neuronal morphology. The seventeen-year-old animal retains a label given six years earlier; collection age does not date a new division at seventeen.

The discussion calls sixteen injections to four adult animals equivalent to independent labeling experiments. Repeated exposures share animals and cumulative label windows. The eleven-of-twelve-month coverage is also pooled across animals and ages, not a matched adult seasonal experiment. No formal rare-neuron detection bound or exact cessation age is calculated.

Gliogenesis, replacement and stable-neuron memory roles are interpretations. No paired birth/death census identifies population feedback, and no functional or behavioral test establishes that neuron turnover impairs memory. The adult autoradiographic null remains distinct from a universal prohibition on adult neurogenesis.

The mass and continuum extrapolations are correlated. Two normalization methods, two chiral/Taylor strategies, three pion-mass ranges, two continuum forms linear in a or a^2, and eighteen time windows produce 432 analysis variants per hadron in each normalization set, not 432 experiments.

The central value is the fit-quality-weighted distribution median. The central 68% interval of that variant distribution estimates systematic uncertainty; 2000 bootstrap datasets supply the median distribution and its central 68% statistical interval. Statistical and systematic errors are combined in quadrature for final plotted bars.

The fit family estimates selected extrapolation and excited-state effects. Exact fit-quality weights, raw correlators, full covariances and independent fit replay are unavailable here; the paper's description of blind analysis does not establish a separately audited outcome-masking protocol.

Finite-volume image corrections use M_X(L)=M_X+c_X(M_pi)*exp(-M_pi*L)/(M_pi*L)^(3/2), with volume scans at about a=0.125 fm and M_pi=320 MeV. Resonance corrections additionally use a scattering model; no precise width determination is supplied.

The lightest pion-mass point at a about 0.085 fm is excluded for rho and Delta because the lowest level is dominated by a two-particle state and weakly sensitive to the resonance mass. All other mass-range cuts remain part of the analysis.

Table S2 fractions are correlated, non-Gaussian and averaged across Xi/Omega sets. Finite-volume terms are treated as corrections. The fractions must not be summed or normalized as independent probabilities or independent variances.

The comparison uses the paper's PDG 2006 isospin averages. QED and isospin breaking are absent; leading pion/kaon electromagnetic adjustments and the neglected residual effects remain approximations. The result does not resolve the proton-neutron mass difference.

A mass spectrum does not establish stability against weak decay, a neutron lifetime, a real-time hadron formation path, a universal three-constituent minimum, nuclear stability or downward causation. The introductory percentages about visible matter and mass origin are not calculated decompositions in this study.

Figure 3 shaded bands represent experimental decay widths, not mass-measurement uncertainties. Input symbols have no error bars because their values set model parameters; this is not evidence of exact independent prediction.

Rolling normalization uses short holds in overlapping blocks, typically fifteen runs within epochs. Its covariance and uncertainty are not independently reconstructed by dividing a printed yield error by the fitted correction factor.

limitations: These four runs are a subset of the 14 charged production ensembles, not an independent replication of the 41-ensemble result. The temporal extent changes with the spatial box and the QED_L large-time assumptions remain applicable.

The bare coupling e=1.00 is larger than the physical coupling. Figure 1 uses the approximate label bare alpha about 1/10; e^2/(4*pi), the renormalized flow coupling and physical alpha are distinct quantities.
The plotted kaon mass-squared difference is negative at this enhanced coupling. That sign is not the physical kaon mass ordering and is not evidence of a neutron-proton sign reversal.

No significant neutral-kaon volume dependence is resolved in this scan; that does not prove exactly zero corrections. The charged-neutral difference needs a fitted 1/L^3 term in addition to the universal leading terms.

These are reported computational results for the specified action, ensembles and fitting procedure. The 60 TB archive, correlators, covariance matrices and analysis code have not been independently replayed.

QED_L removes spatial photon zero modes on every time slice. QED_TL removes only the four-momentum zero mode and has an ill-defined T-to-infinity limit at fixed L for the conventional charged-particle mass extraction. This is a regulator distinction, not two experimental forces.

At order alpha, the leading mass correction is -q^2*alpha*kappa/(2*L)*(1+2/(m*L)), with kappa approximately 2.837297 in units hbar=c=1. Universality through 1/L^2 assumes the photon is the only massless asymptotic state and the charged particle is stable and nondegenerate with states sharing its quantum numbers.

Terms of order 1/L^3 can depend on internal structure and spin; a point-fermion coefficient cannot be imposed on every hadron. Vanishing leading q^2 terms for a neutral particle do not prove absence of all finite-volume effects.

In the full QCD+QED theory the paper's continuum prescription retains an extremely small nonzero cutoff because of QED triviality. Its practical extrapolation does not establish a nonperturbative interacting QED limit at exactly zero lattice spacing.

limitations: At the stated precision the recoil prescription is E_B approximately E_gamma + E_gamma^2/(2*m_d*c^2), so the energy-equivalent wavelength is shorter than the photon wavelength. It is not a second detected photon.

The recoil mass is the deuteron nuclear mass, not a deuterium atomic mass or the Kapton molecular mass. Thermal capture and the stated prompt-emission conditions limit this approximation; it is not an exact arbitrary-kinematics formula.

limitations: The five configuration groups are combined as two campaign sets because settings within a campaign share an angle calibration. They are not five independent mass experiments.
Each angle determination uses four profiles in the +,-,-,+ sequence. Bragg-angle counts, scan points, detected photons and independent calibration sets are distinct counting domains.

Profiles contain approximately 45 points with 60 or 90 seconds per point. A scan-specific summed pulse-height window precedes fitting dynamical diffraction profiles with Gaussian broadening; a profile width is not a direct neutron mass.

The approximately 6 g Kapton source in three graphite holders is exposed to about 5e14 neutrons per square centimeter per second. Its roughly 450 C environment and about 1.2 percent daily hydrogen loss do not describe isolated stationary free neutrons.

Four optical-polygon calibrations near the campaigns use the sum of 24 exterior angles, 2*pi. One serves 1995 and three serve March 1998; the 1998 humidity dependence is about 0.5e-6 per ten percentage points, with calibration relative uncertainty expanded to 1e-7.

Within each campaign the weighted-mean uncertainty is enlarged by sqrt(chi^2/dof), then the 1e-7 relative calibration uncertainty is added in quadrature. The two campaign means are combined before adding crystal-temperature and vertical-divergence contributions.

The final angle uncertainty includes relative contributions 0.1e-6 from crystal temperature and 0.05e-6 from vertical divergence. The 0.083202194(11) degree intermediate value excludes these final contributions; the final value is 0.083202194(14) degrees.
Table 2 prints final March 1995 result beneath the March 1998 configuration rows. Section 3 and the rows identify the second campaign as March 1998; the inconsistent printed label remains disclosed.
Repeatability across years and settings is an internal consistency check using the same facility and crystals, not independent replication or proof that every systematic effect has been removed.

These are published results for the stated capture source, spectrometer and calibration. Raw count profiles, fringe records, calibration runs and their covariance have not been independently replayed.

limitations: At the stated precision the recoil prescription is E_B approximately E_gamma + E_gamma^2/(2*m_d*c^2), so the energy-equivalent wavelength is shorter than the photon wavelength. It is not a second detected photon.

The recoil mass is the deuteron nuclear mass, not a deuterium atomic mass or the Kapton molecular mass. Thermal capture and the stated prompt-emission conditions limit this approximation; it is not an exact arbitrary-kinematics formula.

The paper reports a 5e-10 relative uncertainty contribution from recoil constants, negligible at its measurement precision. This does not make recoil itself negligible or set omitted kinematic effects identically to zero.

The 1999 inverse-meter conversions are 1.331025045(11)e-15 u and 1.239841870(54)e-6 eV per inverse meter. The first is a mass-equivalent conversion h/(m_u*c), the second is hc/e; energy and mass units are not interchangeable without c^2.

The conversions depend on the paper's electron relative mass, fine-structure constant, Rydberg constant and other adopted constants. Their uncertainties are different; changing to modern SI constants is a new calculation, not a silent correction of the published result.

limitations: The measured ion has three trap modes. The free cyclotron frequency is reconstructed from their squared frequencies; the trap cyclotron mode alone is not the free frequency.
The paper writes omega_c=q*B/(m*c) in Gaussian units. In SI the expression is omega_c=abs(q)*B/m for the frequency magnitude; an angular frequency differs from cycles per second by 2*pi.

For the same magnetic field, omega_2/omega_1=(m_1/abs(q_1))/(m_2/abs(q_2)). Equal charges permit a mass ratio; the Ar+/Ar++ entry requires the charge factor and is not a literal ratio of almost equal ionic masses.
The ions are loaded and measured alternately, not simultaneously. Removing a fitted magnetic drift does not make all residuals or adjacent ratios statistically independent.

limitations: PNP detects the ion after coherent radial-to-axial transfer. Its resonant voltages differ for N+ and N2+, changing equilibrium position in stray fields. The SOF protocol keeps the evolution voltage common and changes it only for detection.

limitations: PNP detects the ion after coherent radial-to-axial transfer. Its resonant voltages differ for N+ and N2+, changing equilibrium position in stray fields. The SOF protocol keeps the evolution voltage common and changes it only for detection.

The SOF signal is a classical cyclotron amplitude produced by two separated pulses, not a quantum-state amplitude or an entanglement measurement. Figure 1 uses evolution times up to 50 s for the precision estimate.

Figure 2 compares an N+ ion at approximately 5 V with the same species at 10 V and an N2+ ion at 10 V, with a 22.5 mV axial offset. The approximately 3 ppb unequal-voltage shift disappears at the reported precision with the common-voltage procedure.

Table I bounds residual magnetic, electrostatic and relativistic systematic terms at approximately 0.030, 0.025 and 0.020 ppb for the specified N+/N2+ settings. These are configuration-specific error estimates, not zero corrections or universal bounds.

The first two Table II(a) reference ratios depend on electron mass and binding energies. Their agreement near 0.15 ppb tests those controls; it does not prove absence of every systematic effect in all other ion comparisons.
These are reported measurements and conditional inferences. Raw phase records, drift fits, chemical-energy inputs and complete covariance have not been independently replayed.

A charged-ion frequency, neutral-atom mass and inferred neutron mass are different quantities. These results do not establish nucleon formation, lifetime, stability or a universal constituent minimum.

The 1993 and 1994 publications belong to the same MIT measurement program. Disjoint acquisition and cross-publication covariance are not established; the two papers cannot be treated as independent replications or averaged as independent results.

limitations: The 1994 result is a global least-squares solution of twenty pairwise comparisons. Its covariance matrix determines uncertainties of correlated atomic masses and mass differences; the short article does not provide that matrix or every input ratio.
For a mass difference, Var(D-H)=Var(D)+Var(H)-2*Cov(D,H). Adding printed marginal errors in quadrature assumes zero covariance and is not a reconstruction of the published fit.

The authors report reduced chi-square 0.74 and redundant routes to the mass table. These internal checks constrain the stated error model; they do not logically exclude every possible common systematic.

The quoted 2.6e-10 relative rms magnetic fluctuation applies to a single frequency measurement in the 1994 analysis. A typical one-night ratio error near 1e-10 and the final fitted mass uncertainties have different averaging domains.

The 1993 treatment describes approximately Gaussian residuals for its example; the 1994 robust estimator downweights non-Gaussian outliers. These are different analysis descriptions, not interchangeable procedures.

limitations: Schuh uses 120 cycles over 23 days, with 73 cycles at 40 s and the others at 20 s, and approximately 140 minutes per full cycle. Two 4.6 ms magnetron pulses and an intentionally deformed readout potential distinguish this experiment from proton-mass PnA acquisition.

limitations: COMSOL 5.2 with the AC/DC module represents a point charge and perfectly conducting grounded electrode surfaces. Twenty-one ion positions from -0.5 to +0.5 mm are fitted with odd polynomials to extract field gradients.

limitations: Neutral carbon-12 has mass exactly 12 u; C-12(6+) instead has mass 12 u minus six electron masses plus the six positive ionization energies divided by c^2. The sixfold charge factor in m_p=R*m_C/6 cannot be omitted.

limitations: Fink/Myers uses a separate FSU 8.5 T, 4.2 K trap with two simultaneously stored ions, alternated between the center and a 2 mm cyclotron orbit. Storage is simultaneous; the reported frequency readout is sequential.

Of 83 runs on 27 H2+ ions, the final analysis uses 33 runs on seven ions. The eight-Gaussian vibrational histogram is not the final mass fit. The supplement needed to audit selection and maximum-likelihood details was not obtained.

Vibrational v=0 does not imply rotational N=0. Long-lived rotational excitation is modeled, not directly measured. A 300 K parent-gas distribution and cascade calculation are assumptions, with uncertain desorption populations.
The adopted rotational correction is 15.8(16.4) ppt. The trend -5.1(12.4) ppt is not a detection of heating. Table III total correction is 65.2(19.0) ppt; the 19.0 includes statistical uncertainty.

The published final ratio uncertainty components are (7) statistical, (7) instrumental, (16) rotational and (19) total. The raw statistical entry is 6.3 ppt; the original weighting is not independently reproduced.

Conversion from H2+ to m_d/m_p uses electron and molecular binding inputs. The cited Olivares-Pilon/Baye and Yan/Zhang/Li binding calculations remain unreviewed upstream sources here; Korobov HD+ theory is not substituted for them.

claims.statement: In the ideal corrected beam model, R_p=epsilon_p*N_n/tau and R_monitor=epsilon_0*v_0*N_n/L, so tau=L*epsilon_p*R_monitor/(epsilon_0*v_0*R_p). R_p counts detected proton-producing decays, and epsilon_0 is the monitor efficiency at the reference speed v_0.

citations.locator: Published PDF pages 1-5, Sections I-II and Equations 3-8: publication identity, decay counting, neutron population, inverse-velocity monitor and trap-length slope
citations.note: Only the stated acquisition, monitor calibration or conditional inference is supported by this reviewed passage.

limitations: The measured beam observable is a proton-producing decay rate relative to the monitored neutron population in the trapping region. Identifying its inverse with the total free-neutron lifetime requires the stated decay-channel and detection assumptions. Storage disappearance and proton counting are distinct observables; no branching fraction or explanation of their difference is inferred here.

Cancellation of the neutron velocity distribution assumes a thin monitor with inverse-velocity response and unchanged beam between the trap and monitor. Finite absorption, spatial profiles, scattering and beam transport still require the original corrections.

The effective trap length is L=n*l+L_end. A fit of the proton-to-monitor count-rate ratio versus electrode number removes a constant end contribution only under the common-end-region assumption; the paper separately corrects nonlinearity from field, geometry and beam divergence. Proton trapping for milliseconds is not neutron storage for a lifetime.

The neutron-lifetime results do not establish neutron formation, proton stability, a universal constituent minimum or a present-day beam/bottle discrepancy. The 2013 historical world averages are not admitted without review of their components.

limitations: The 2014 author report describes the August 2006, November 2006 and May 2007 MAMI acquisition previously reported in 2010. The 2010 and 2014 publications, spline fits and Rosenbluth separation are dependent uses of this acquisition, not independent replications.

Unpolarized elastic scattering in the ultrarelativistic one-photon approximation determines epsilon*GE^2+tau*GM^2. Signs require normalization and continuity conventions. GE(0)=1 and GM(0)=mu_p are imposed reference values; this is not a new magnetic-moment measurement, a count of constituents or a formation law.

The released ratios are a fitted-normalization data product, with spline-derived error scaling; they are not a temporally prior independent input to that same fit. The cross-section ratios already incorporate acceptance and radiation modeling, Feshbach Coulomb correction and spline-fit normalization. They are not raw counts or independently measured absolute Born cross sections. Standard-dipole normalization is a model input.

The 31 normalization parameters enter shared products. Equation 48 multiplies data and error by their product; ancillary Section 4 uses the reciprocal nuisance-parameter convention on the model. Their numerical parameter values are not interchangeable. Column 6 contains already-scaled point-to-point errors, not counting errors to scale a second time. The 315-MeV acquisition uses the current-based luminosity estimate after a monitor-setting problem.

Kinematics must use the acceptance-averaged Q^2 and beam energy, not the central spectrometer angle. Multiplying columns 5-8 by column 9 undoes the applied Coulomb correction. Columns 12-18 change model normalization; the systematic variations in column 10 require new fits, not new observations.

The selected Mainz-only spline table tabulates GE, GM/mu_p and mu_p*GE/GM, with separate statistical, experimental systematic and Coulomb-variation columns. Its 1000 grid values are evaluations of one fit, not 1000 new measurements.

The fit errors describe 68 percent pointwise bands. They are not simultaneous bands, independent draws or the full covariance. The Coulomb-variation band varies a correction by 50 percent; it is not an independent Gaussian error to combine without a model.

The Mainz-only analysis applies Feshbach Coulomb correction but not a complete hard two-photon-exchange treatment. Limited epsilon coverage weakens GE/GM separation above Q^2 about 0.55 GeV^2; the single-energy endpoint does not separately identify both form factors without the fit model.

Sachs form factors describe elastic current response in a specified framework. A static three-dimensional charge-density interpretation is frame dependent; no literal three-quark geometry, unique pion-cloud mechanism, neutron form factor, hadronization dynamics or nuclear stability follows.

limitations: The 2014 author report describes the August 2006, November 2006 and May 2007 MAMI acquisition previously reported in 2010. The 2010 and 2014 publications, spline fits and Rosenbluth separation are dependent uses of this acquisition, not independent replications.

Unpolarized elastic scattering in the ultrarelativistic one-photon approximation determines epsilon*GE^2+tau*GM^2. Signs require normalization and continuity conventions. GE(0)=1 and GM(0)=mu_p are imposed reference values; this is not a new magnetic-moment measurement, a count of constituents or a formation law.

The released ratios are a fitted-normalization data product, with spline-derived error scaling; they are not a temporally prior independent input to that same fit. The cross-section ratios already incorporate acceptance and radiation modeling, Feshbach Coulomb correction and spline-fit normalization. They are not raw counts or independently measured absolute Born cross sections. Standard-dipole normalization is a model input.

The 31 normalization parameters enter shared products. Equation 48 multiplies data and error by their product; ancillary Section 4 uses the reciprocal nuisance-parameter convention on the model. Their numerical parameter values are not interchangeable. Column 6 contains already-scaled point-to-point errors, not counting errors to scale a second time. The 315-MeV acquisition uses the current-based luminosity estimate after a monitor-setting problem.

The selected Mainz-only spline table tabulates GE, GM/mu_p and mu_p*GE/GM, with separate statistical, experimental systematic and Coulomb-variation columns. Its 1000 grid values are evaluations of one fit, not 1000 new measurements.

The fit errors describe 68 percent pointwise bands. They are not simultaneous bands, independent draws or the full covariance. The Coulomb-variation band varies a correction by 50 percent; it is not an independent Gaussian error to combine without a model.

The Mainz-only analysis applies Feshbach Coulomb correction but not a complete hard two-photon-exchange treatment. Limited epsilon coverage weakens GE/GM separation above Q^2 about 0.55 GeV^2; the single-energy endpoint does not separately identify both form factors without the fit model.

Sachs form factors describe elastic current response in a specified framework. A static three-dimensional charge-density interpretation is frame dependent; no literal three-quark geometry, unique pion-cloud mechanism, neutron form factor, hadronization dynamics or nuclear stability follows.

limitations: The channel is an isolated ground-state bare deuteron with no supplied energy and asymptotically free p+p+e-+electron-antineutrino final particles. Its net charge is +1 on both sides. Neutral atoms, electronic bound final states, molecular ions and externally driven breakup are different state specifications.

Q0 neglects the antineutrino rest mass; any nonnegative final neutrino mass raises the required rest energy. Positive-energy on-shell final particles and four-momentum conservation make Q0<0 an exclusion for this channel. Q0>=0 alone would not establish a nonzero matrix element or rate.

The calculation uses the one Rau joint adjusted pair mp=1.007276466580(17)u and md=2.013553212537(16)u with correlation +0.26. These reuse the published mass measurements and molecular/reference inputs; the local adjustment, direct deuteron and earlier proton values are not substituted or pooled as independent replicas.

The adopted CODATA 2018 inputs are me=0.000548579909065(16)u and u*c^2=931494102.42(28)eV. They are external adjustment values, not new electron-mass or energy-conversion measurements; this calculation does not update them to a later adjustment.

The admitted neutron mass was inferred as mn=md-mp+Bd/c^2 using the same adjusted masses and capture binding. Substitution into (mn-mp-me)c^2-Bd cancels Bd identically. Capture-derived mn and Bd are not independent confirmation of the reduced Q and cannot be assigned independent errors in that expression.

Separately inserting printed mn=1.00866491604u and Bd/c^2=0.00238817008u gives a Q larger by 0.0027944823...eV than the reduced expression. The identity gives mn=1.008664916037u, compatible with the printed neutron rounding; the difference is not a source-analysis error or a second acquisition. The display-rounding box is not a confidence interval.

The published +0.26 mass-pair correlation enters var(md-2mp)=var(md)+4var(mp)-4cov(md,mp), giving about 0.0313eV standard uncertainty for this contribution alone. Electron/reference cross-covariances and the full adjustment are not reconstructed; no complete Q uncertainty, discovery significance or calibrated coverage is supplied.

Bare nuclear masses cannot be replaced by neutral hydrogen-isotope masses. For positive electronic binding energies IH and ID, Q0=[M(D)-2M(H)]c^2+ID-2IH. This identity retains the declared bare-particle channel; it does not import a neutral-atom decay or its final electronic states.

This is a new bounded calculation from published inputs, not a beta-decay measurement reported by Rau. It establishes neither all-channel deuteron permanence, a nuclear or individual bound-neutron lifetime, nor stability of arbitrary nuclei. No weak amplitude, phase-space rate, raw mass fit, instrument calibration or complete covariance is reproduced.

claims.statement: For the declared bare-deuteron channel, the local calculation gives Q0=(md-2mp-me)*c^2=-1.44223 MeV approximately. limitations: This admission concerns the 1993-1995 small-angle data near the Z resonance. The separate 1998 large-angle acquisition at 188.7 GeV is not imported. Four coordinate measurements weighted 0.25 belong to each event; seven year/energy data sets do not supply seven independent instruments or uncorrelated replicas.

Modified BHLUMI 4.04 varies the spacelike running about the nominal Eidelman-Jegerlehner prediction while keeping timelike running unchanged. Photon-Z interference and other radiative terms remain part of that model; S=0 means nominal running, not no running. The linear deformation is restricted to the stated small-angle interval.

The opposite detector sides give S=-6.7e-4 and -0.5e-4 GeV^-2. The authors attribute their discrepancy to incomplete beam-pipe material simulation and assign half the difference, 3.1e-4 GeV^-2, as a dominant systematic contribution. This is retained, not averaged into independent precision measurements.

The correction sample contains 2.6 million simulated and reconstructed BHLUMI events. Bin corrections differ from unity by at most 0.4 percent, with quoted statistical errors about 4e-4. Shared detector-correction errors are assumed fully correlated between corresponding bins of different data sets; prediction errors are correlated across parameter choices but uncorrelated between data sets.

No event-level acquisition, corrected bin table, BHLUMI prediction, detector/material simulation, multinomial likelihood, significance calibration, stochastic systematic propagation or covariance is independently reproduced. The paper's hypothesis-significance statement is not certified or admitted as a local result.

claims.statement: In the stated solar-neutrino weak-response model, nu_e+d->p+p+e-minus is the charged-current channel, nu_x+d->p+n+nu_x is the neutral-current channel and nu_x+e-minus->nu_x+e-minus is elastic scattering. CC is electron-flavor sensitive; NC has equal sensitivity to the three active flavors; ES has reduced muon/tau sensitivity. Reconstructed Cherenkov observables distinguish statistical response templates, not individually labeled incoming flavors.

The principal templates and flux inferences assume the standard undistorted B8 spectrum and adopted weak cross sections. claims.statement: For two effectively massless physical daughter four-momenta from a two-body decay, define mT^2 = 2 pT1 pT2 (1-cos(deltaPhi)); the exact parent invariant mass then obeys M >= mT. Replacing these quantities by reconstructed electron and missing transverse vectors defines an estimator under a single-invisible-daughter assignment. Response errors can make that estimator exceed the true mass, so the exact inequality is not an eventwise detector guarantee. The transverse recoil is the magnitude of the daughter transverse-vector sum; mT is not a fully reconstructed invariant mass.

limitations: Use c=1 and the (+,-,-,-) metric for the declared kinematic definitions. The exact transverse-mass inequality concerns physical daughter momenta under the two-body assumptions. Assigning the missing transverse vector to one effectively massless neutrino is an inference condition; missing energy alone does not identify a neutrino species or a W.

TASSO uses selected charged tracks, detector/fragmentation assumptions and a specified collinear two-jet comparison. Planarity and the hard-gluon interpretation do not provide a complete final-state census, a free stable gluon observation or a universal confinement theorem.

SLD neutral-hadron results reconstruct specified decay channels through acceptance, branching and background models. Full-range totals reuse the measured spectra with fragmentation-model extrapolation; their shared normalization and covariance are retained. Reconstructed parents and daughters are not disjoint stable end products or feed-down-subtracted primary populations.

Neither a selected hadron spectrum nor inclusive jet/decay yields uniquely identify a microscopic hadronization mechanism or prove the absence of all colored final states. Fractional electric-charge searches are a distinct inference and are not pooled with these hadronic records.

Hadronic consistency does not establish stable nuclear matter or atomic structures. The admitted nuclear capture, mass and deuteron-threshold records have separate calibration and channel limits. Their bounded results do not supply an all-channel stability proof; atomic electronic binding lies outside the QCD-only spectrum.

limitations: This is a literature synthesis of already admitted results. KamLAND reactor antineutrinos involve changing reactor histories and baselines. Super-Kamiokande uses atmospheric flux, zenith distributions and detector/kinematic proxies with a historical two-flavor fit. The 1998 disappearance analysis does not directly identify tau appearance or distinguish its tau interpretation from the stated sterile alternative. Its L/E cross-check reuses the sample and does not resolve an oscillation dip.

OPERA reconstructs tau candidates in a primarily muon-neutrino beam using channel-dependent efficiencies and backgrounds. Its calibrated channel-combination significance, signal strength and full-mixing mass-squared compatibility reuse the same candidate sample. Dividing five candidates by an interaction total does not produce an oscillation probability, and the Fisher-product statistic is not the calibrated tail probability.

Historical effective two-flavor parameters, confidence constructions and adopted external inputs retain their publication-specific meanings; no current three-flavor global fit is inferred. These results do not establish absolute neutrino masses, every individual mass to be nonzero, Dirac/Majorana character, a unique mass-generation mechanism or quantitative astrophysical/cosmological transport.

Residual bounds require a Hermitian transfer matrix and delimit a window containing some eigenvalue, not necessarily the ground state; for this improved action the source restricts Hermiticity to its low-energy sector, E much less than 1/a.

Tighter gap bounds require the stated no-missing-states threshold and negligible thermal effects. Estimates based on noninteracting NN level counts below NDelta or DeltaDelta thresholds can fail if extra low states are present. Source errors and bound widths are distinct; one-sided upper bounds cannot supply two-sided phase errors.

The selected phase comparison truncates to the lowest S wave, neglects lattice artifacts and does not determine a complete coupled-channel amplitude. Raw correlators, residual/gap calculations, operator completeness, continuum/infinite-volume extrapolations and physical-mass nuclear binding are not reproduced here.

claims.statement: The paired 2026 preprints leave the nature of the lowest I=1 and I=0 two-nucleon states at these heavy-mass action parameters unresolved without additional spectral assumptions. The authors find no positive I=1 bound-state evidence from those bounds, and the I=0 level is too near the bound-state threshold to settle its nature from this one volume. This does not exclude a missed bound state or validate the earlier binding assignment as consensus.

The spatially flat background is ds^2=dt^2-a(t)^2 dx^2, dt=a d_eta. claims.statement: For the declared infrared flow F(g), a fixed point g_* satisfies F_i(g_*)=0. Near it, d(delta g_i)/d ell=B_ij delta g_j+O(delta g^2), where B_ij=partial F_i/partial g_j at g_*. For an admitted eigen-direction with real eigenvalue y_a, its linear scaling field obeys u_a(ell)=exp(y_a ell)u_a(0). A nonredundant local operator of full fixed-point scaling dimension Delta_a coupled homogeneously in d dimensions has y_a=d-Delta_a. With ell increasing toward the infrared, y_a>0 is relevant, y_a<0 irrelevant and y_a=0 linearly marginal.

claims.statement: In a supplied closed unitary three-active-neutrino model, define U=R23 R13(delta) R12 P. Each real ij rotation acts on its plane with block [[cij,sij],[-sij,cij]] and as identity on the remaining direction, with cij=cos(thetaij) and sij=sin(thetaij); the 1-3 block is [[c13,s13 exp(-i delta)],[-s13 exp(i delta),c13]]. For generic three-mass mixing, charged-lepton and Dirac-neutrino rephasings leave three angles and one Dirac phase, with P=I. In the Majorana alternative use P=diag(exp(i eta1),exp(i eta2),1); these two extra column phases cancel from ordinary mass-induced flavor-oscillation probabilities.

A dimension-five operator built from the lepton and Higgs doublets can instead generate a Majorana mass after electroweak symmetry breaking. These are alternative model constructions; flavor-oscillation evidence alone does not select one.

claims.statement: Adopt the local gauge algebra su(3)c plus su(2)L plus u(1)Y, conventionally written SU(3)c x SU(2)L x U(1)Y, with Q=T3+Y. For each of three generations, the pre-Higgs-background chiral assignments are Q_L=(u_L,dprime_L)~(3,2,1/6), u_R~(3,1,2/3), d_R~(3,1,-1/3), L_L=(nu_L,l_L)~(1,2,-1/2) and l_R~(1,1,-1). The single complex Higgs scalar is phi~(1,2,1/2). Each tuple gives the color representation, weak representation and declared hypercharge: 3 means the color fundamental, 2 the weak doublet and 1 a singlet. The gauge potentials are G_mu^a (a=1,...,8), W_mu^i (i=1,2,3) and B_mu, with couplings gs, g and gprime. This is a chosen interacting field specification; the scalar is a boson without being a gauge vector mediator.
claims.scope: Declared minimal Standard Model sector and representation bookkeeping; no empirical selection or derivation of the field content.

limitations: Here Y=Y_PDG/2: the reviewed electroweak chapter writes Q=T3+Y_PDG/2. The tuples use Y=Q-T3, the adopted quark charges +2/3 and -1/3, lepton charges 0 and -1, and weak doublet T3=+1/2,-1/2 or singlet T3=0. They state the converted convention, not a verbatim PDG tuple table. Right-handed entries denote right-handed fermion fields, not their left-handed charge conjugates; dprime is a weak-interaction basis component.

Choose D_mu=partial_mu+i*gs*t^a*G_mu^a+i*g*T^i*W_mu^i+i*gprime*Y*B_mu, with generators in the representation of the field and zero action for a trivial factor. The Q_L multiplet is charged under all three factors; the Higgs doublet has weak and hypercharge interactions, and Yukawa terms couple the declared multiplets. Commuting gauge factors do not make the full interacting sectors dynamically isolated or independently generated systems.

The 8+3+1 vector-potential species count follows from the chosen generator dimensions; it is neither a total physical-polarization count nor an observed particle population. Gauge redundancy, physical free excitations, unstable W/Z resonances, confined colored fields and detector candidates have different meanings. The four real components of phi do not add four gauge-vector species.

claims.statement: Choose a nonrelativistic electron of mass m_e in the Coulomb field of a supplied static point nucleus with charge +e. In rationalized hbar=c=1 units define alpha=e^2/(4*pi) and H=-nabla^2/(2*m_e)-alpha/r. Rewriting the selected primary result in these conventions gives E_n=-m_e*alpha^2/(2*n^2), n=1,2,..., relative to the separated-particle threshold. These are discrete negative bound energies with positive binding energy -E_n. The source describes regular spatial solutions with exponentially decreasing radial tails; the eigenfunctions are not classical electron orbits or compact hard-edged objects.

claims.statement: Adopt the selected equilibrium continuum-solvent ion-atmosphere model in its original electrostatic-cgs units. Let n_i be bulk ion-species number density, z_i signed valence, D the dimensionless solvent dielectric constant, kT thermal energy and e the positive charge magnitude. For electroneutral bulk sum_i(n_i*z_i)=0, the Boltzmann density n_i(r)=n_i*exp[-z_i*e*psi(r)/(kT)] gives, after weak-potential linearization, nabla^2*psi=kappa^2*psi outside the tagged source, with kappa^2=4*pi*e^2*sum_i(n_i*z_i^2)/(D*kT). In the dilute point-ion limiting model the tagged-charge mean potential is psi(r)=q*exp(-kappa*r)/(D*r). The screening length 1/kappa depends on composition, temperature and solvent response; it represents statistical ion-atmosphere structure rather than an ion-formation event.

The icosahedral phase is metastable under the reported protocols: no detectable subsequent crystallization after 6 hours at 300 degrees C or 1 hour at 350 degrees C, and conversion to stable Al6Mn after 1 hour at 400 degrees C.

claims.statement: The reported two-dimensional hard-disk calculations support first-order liquid-hexatic coexistence over approximately eta=0.700 to 0.716, using coexistence patterns, the equilibrium equation of state and interface scaling. Near eta=0.720 the positional correlations become approximately algebraic, near r^-1/3 over the resolved range, and the source identifies a continuous hexatic-solid transition. Thus this specified entropic model has ordered regimes and two distinct transition characters.

claims.statement: For the selected ambient-water structure analysis, the oxygen-oxygen pair-distribution function g_OO(r) describes a radial spatial correlation of oxygen positions. claims.statement: Specify the dispersed material, continuous medium, interaction model, preparation and observation time when describing colloid stability or an interface. Persistence over an observation window, a thermodynamic phase preference and a kinetic barrier to a particular change are different propositions. For the source spherical-crystallite approximation, DeltaG(r)=4*pi*r^2*gamma-(4*pi/3)*r^3*n*DeltaMu, where gamma is crystal-liquid interfacial free energy per area, n is crystallite particle-number density and DeltaMu is liquid-minus-solid chemical potential. The positive surface cost competes with a bulk growth term when DeltaMu>0.

claims.statement: For a free nucleus of mass M, the leading nonrelativistic recoil energy is E_R=E_gamma^2/(2*M*c^2), displacing emission below and absorption above the nuclear transition energy. In the selected bound-solid oscillator account, a recoilless nuclear gamma event leaves the internal vibrational occupation state unchanged. Momentum is still transferred to the bound body; its whole-body translational recoil energy is negligibly small on the stated spectral scale. This zero-phonon channel is a fraction of events, not absence of binding vibrations, zero momentum transfer or a rule that every emitted gamma ray is resonant.

claims.statement: Orbital electron capture consumes a bound electron in a specified nuclear transition and emits an electron neutrino; in the selected 140Pr to 140Ce channel it converts a proton to a neutron, preserves mass number A=140 and lowers nuclear charge Z from 59 to 58. Initial bare 140Pr59+, hydrogenlike 140Pr58+ and heliumlike 140Pr57+ carry zero, one and two bound electrons respectively. EC removes one bound electron while lowering Z by one, so the daughter ionic charge remains the same. Changing the initial ionization state does not change which parent isotope is prepared; the subsequent nuclear decay does change the element.

claims.statement: For the source constant-rate fit in one consistent time frame, parent disappearance obeys N_Pr(t)=N_Pr(0)*exp(-lambda_all*t), with lambda_all=lambda_EC+lambda_betaPlus+lambda_loss. Stable EC-daughter growth obeys N_Ce(t)=N_Pr(0)*lambda_EC/(lambda_all-lambda_loss)*[exp(-lambda_loss*t)-exp(-lambda_all*t)]+N_Ce(0)*exp(-lambda_loss*t). Loss includes residual-gas collisions and electron pickup in the cooler; it is not nuclear decay. The source Table I rates are in the ion rest frame, while Figure 2 times are laboratory times: for a constant Lorentz factor gamma, t_lab=gamma*t_rest and lambda_rest=gamma*lambda_lab.

claims.statement: For a declared isotope and electronic state, let I be nuclear spin, J total electronic angular momentum and F the coupled total angular momentum. Define K=F(F+1)-I(I+1)-J(J+1). With A expressed in frequency units, the first-order magnetic-dipole contribution relative to the state centroid is E_F/h=A*K/2; allowed higher-rank terms have separate state-specific constants, including the electric-quadrupole B term. In the selected Cs133 7d 2D3/2 assignment, J=3/2 and F=2,3,4,5 correspond to supplied I=7/2. The first-order electric-quadrupole term is absent within a J=1/2 electronic level; the Cs ground-state clock is not evidence that every hyperfine transition has a nonzero quadrupole contribution.
claims.scope: Selected first-order angular-momentum/frequency convention, not an all-atoms precision Hamiltonian.

limitations: The measured A,B and optional C coupling constants combine nuclear multipoles with state-dependent electronic matrix elements and higher-order corrections. They are not direct independent measurements of bare nuclear magnetic dipole, electric quadrupole or magnetic octupole moments.

E_F/h is a frequency, with interval DeltaE/h in Hz or MHz, not angular frequency in rad/s. If A is instead quoted as an energy, the h conversion must be changed consistently; no extra 2*pi or equality of A with each measured interval is admitted.

A first-order parametrization is an approximation within the declared state and field regime. Nuclear spin and state assignments are supplied labels, not newly measured nuclear-spin values; external-field shifts and higher-order level mixing remain separate.

The multipole and angular-momentum conditions do not require every isotope/state to exhibit the same terms or any universal nonzero splitting. Nuclear-moment coupling is distinct from electronic fine structure, the Lamb shift and general radiative/QED corrections.

Neither a free-proton/neutron moment nor the leading static-nucleus Z=1 binding model supplies the composite Cs133 nuclear moments, many-electron wavefunction or a quantitative prediction of these constants.

claims.statement: The SI second fixes the unperturbed Cs133 electronic-ground-state hyperfine transition frequency Delta_nu_Cs to exactly 9,192,631,770 Hz, where Hz=s^-1. This exact assigned number is a normative unit definition; a finite apparatus realizes that reference through measurements, systematic corrections and nonzero uncertainty.
