claims.statement: Brett et al. measure vacuolar pH in 4,606 single-gene deletion strains of yeast at three external pH values with a calibrated fluorescent probe. Wild-type vacuolar pH stays between 4.81 and 5.41, median 5.27, and resists acid stress. Deletion of eleven subunits or assembly factors of the vacuolar proton-pumping ATPase gives prominent alkalinization of the vacuole under more than one external pH, and these deletions head the list of 30 gene losses that raise vacuolar pH. This is evidence for Ion Channels and Membrane Transport Structures → Regulation of pH and Ionic Balance in the arising role: the regulated internal pH is produced by a membrane transport structure that moves protons, and removing subunits of that structure loses control of the compartment's pH.

claims.statement: Su et al. map chromatin accessibility in adult mouse dentate gyrus before and one hour after synchronous neuronal activation. Activation opens 11,438 regions and closes 1,739, and the open regions carry the binding motif of the activity-induced factor cFos. Knocking cFos down with a virally delivered short hairpin attenuates the activity-induced opening at those sites and the upregulation of the associated genes, while expressing cFos without any stimulation partially reproduces the opening, 56 percent of the 647 regions it opens overlapping those opened by activity. This is evidence for Signal Transduction Pathways → Nucleosomal Chromatin Packaging and DNA Accessibility in the modulation role: signal transduction does not create nucleosomal packaging but shifts which sequences in an already packaged genome are accessible, through the factors it induces.

claims.statement: Jones et al. follow eight misfolded nuclear substrates in yeast by cycloheximide chase. Every one of them, three nuclear-targeted misfolded proteins, two truncations, a hydrophobic peptide fusion and two missense mutants, is stabilized in cells lacking the quality-control ubiquitin ligase San1, in four independent assays each. Loss of the Hsp70 chaperones Ssa1 and Ssa2 impairs the degradation of some of the same substrates and leaves the two missense substrates almost unaffected, and the stabilized substrates stay in the nucleus. This is evidence for Chaperones and Protein Quality Control Mechanisms → Selective Proteasomal Degradation of Tagged Proteins in the arising role: the recognition step that commits a damaged protein to the proteasome is carried out by a quality-control component, and no substrate is degraded when that component is missing.

claims.statement: Prakash et al. show that a ubiquitinated protein is destroyed only if part of it is unstructured. Truncating the unstructured region of the degradation tag stabilizes a tightly folded dihydrofolate reductase against the proteasome although the shortened substrate is ubiquitinated at the same rate and to the same extent; attaching either of two unrelated lysine-free unstructured tails to its other end restores rapid degradation. A substrate carrying four fused ubiquitins directly on the folded domain is degraded only inefficiently, and again rapidly once an unstructured extension is added, while stabilizing the folded domain with methotrexate leaves the protein intact and merely clips off the tail. This is evidence for Protein Folding and Functional Conformation → Selective Proteasomal Degradation of Tagged Proteins in the arising role: whether the proteasome can destroy a tagged protein is fixed by the protein's own folded conformation, which must present an unstructured segment for degradation to begin.

claims.statement: In the same system the covalent modification is what commits a protein to the proteasome. A circularly permuted dihydrofolate reductase carrying an unstructured tail is degraded rapidly, but is stabilized when the N-terminal residue of its degradation signal is changed from arginine to methionine, when the two ubiquitin-acceptor lysines of the signal are changed to arginine, or when the ubiquitination signal is deleted altogether. The same requirement holds for the substrates whose degradation is restored by unstructured tails, which are ubiquitinated on the signal's lysines. This is evidence for Post-Translational Modifications of Proteins → Selective Proteasomal Degradation of Tagged Proteins in the arising role: selective destruction follows a covalent post-translational mark, and removing the residue that receives it, or the signal that directs it, leaves the protein intact.

claims.statement: Brinley and Mullins dialyse the inside of squid giant axons against a defined medium containing cyanide and measure sodium movement with tracer. With fuel supplied, the resting sodium efflux averages 48 pmol per square centimetre per second against an inward leak of 57. Applying 10 micromolar strophanthidin outside, an inhibitor of the sodium pump of the membrane, reversibly lowers the efflux to 10-13 pmol per square centimetre per second, the same level reached when the fuel is withdrawn. This is evidence for Ion Channels and Membrane Transport Structures → Pump-Sustained Transmembrane Electrochemical Gradients in the arising role: the outward movement that maintains the ionic difference across the membrane is carried by a specific membrane transport structure, and blocking that structure leaves only the passive leak.
claims.scope: Cause 3.3 > 3.38 (arising): one axon preparation with a pharmacological block of the sodium pump; it shows the active flux depending on the transport structure, and measures fluxes rather than the gradient itself.

claims.statement: Prywes et al. measure, for all sixteen combinations of template base and activated monomer, how fast a primer is extended without any enzyme, using the same primer and the same activated downstream trimer. Matched additions run at 1, 6, 26 and 44 per hour for U on A, A on U, G on C and C on G; the fastest mismatch, G opposite U, runs at 0.3 per hour, about 5 percent of the matched rate on that template, and every other mismatch is at least two orders of magnitude slower than its match, giving an average fidelity of 98 percent over the four templates. This is evidence for Template Complementarity and Selective Pairing Rules → Non-Enzymatic Template-Directed Polymerization in the arising role: which monomer is added in non-enzymatic copying is set by the complementarity rules themselves, since the same chemistry proceeds a hundred times more slowly when the pair is not matched.
claims.scope: Cause 3.40 > 3.41 (arising): sixteen separate RNA primer-extension reactions with one monomer each at pH 8 with magnesium; it shows selective pairing governing the addition, not copying fidelity when all monomers compete.

claims.statement: Prywes et al. compare the same non-enzymatic primer extension with and without chemical activation of the reacting species. A single activated G monomer alone extends the primer very slowly, at about the rate of ligation; an unactivated downstream trimer bearing a 5'-hydroxyl or a 5'-phosphate raises that rate only modestly; the same trimer activated as a 5'-phosphoro-2-methylimidazolide raises it by over two orders of magnitude. With activated trimers present, all four activated monomers are added at least a hundred times faster than without, and a mixture of activated monomers extends a primer by four nucleotides where the helper-free lane shows little extension. This is evidence for Activated Monomers and Energy-Rich Intermediates → Non-Enzymatic Template-Directed Polymerization in the arising role: template-directed polymerization without enzymes proceeds only from energy-rich activated monomers, the leaving group being what makes the condensation fast enough to observe.

claims.statement: Exterkate et al. reconstitute the phospholipid synthesis pathway in preformed liposomes and follow what the synthesis does to them. Adding a large dose of oleic acid swells the vesicles from 30-100 to 60-200 nm; converting it enzymatically into phospholipid turns the preparation into stacked multilamellar membranes, which dissolve back into normal liposomes on adding EDTA. Feeding the fatty acid in small doses at lower magnesium instead yields larger vesicles with no stacking, and the dye-dilution assay puts the membrane expansion at 25-30 percent, the value expected from the fatty acid supplied. This is evidence for Enzymatic Lipid Biosynthesis and Membrane Growth → Amphiphile Self-Assembly into Bilayers and Vesicles in the modulation role: enzymatic lipid synthesis does not create the bilayer, which must already exist for the enzymes to work, but changes the size, lamellarity and amount of the assembled membrane.

claims.statement: Mansy et al. measure how fast solutes cross the boundaries of vesicles self-assembled from single-chain amphiphiles. The permeability belongs to the assembled bilayer and changes with what it is made of: ribose crosses myristoleate membranes at 24 and myristoleate:monomyristolein membranes at 87, in units of 10^-8 cm/s, with farnesol-containing membranes at 410, while the same series orders the permeability of the nucleotide UMP in the same way. Charged nucleotides are retained for 24 hours while singly charged activated nucleotides equilibrate with a half-time of about 12 hours. This is evidence for Amphiphile Self-Assembly into Bilayers and Vesicles → Selective Permeability in Protocellular Boundaries in the arising role: a boundary that lets some solutes through and holds others back exists as a property of the self-assembled amphiphile bilayer and changes when the amphiphiles are changed.

claims.statement: Mansy et al. encapsulate a fluorescently labelled ten-nucleotide DNA in vesicles self-assembled from single-chain amphiphiles, remove what is outside by size exclusion and follow what remains. About 100 percent of the oligonucleotide stays associated with the vesicles over the 24-hour window, for every membrane composition tested, while small solutes of the same preparation cross the boundary. claims.statement: Nott et al. form membraneless droplets by phase separation of the disordered N-terminal region of Ddx4 and add labelled 32-base DNA, single-stranded or double-stranded, at 1 micromolar with a DNA-free sample as the baseline. Confocal emission measured inside and outside the droplets shows the single-stranded DNA concentrated in the droplet interior while the double-stranded DNA is largely excluded, giving partition coefficients and free energies of opposite sign. This is evidence for Biomolecular Condensates and Coacervate Phase Separation → Encapsulation of Polymers and Catalysts in Protocells in the arising role: a compartment formed by phase separation, with no membrane at all, can take up and hold a polymer selectively, which is the confinement step this arising names.

claims.statement: Zhu and Szostak feed large multilamellar oleate vesicles with five equivalents of oleate micelles. The membrane area grows about 3.7-fold in 25 minutes by the dye-dilution assay, the initially spherical vesicles turn into long thread-like vesicles, and modest shear, measured as a critical shear rate of 15 per second, divides them into multiple daughter vesicles that remain multilamellar and retain their contents; a second feed grows them again and the cycle repeats. Without added micelles the vesicles stay spherical and gentle agitation does not divide them. This is evidence for Amphiphile Self-Assembly into Bilayers and Vesicles → Coupled Growth–Division Cycles of Protocellular Compartments in the arising role: the growth and division cycle is a cycle of the self-assembled amphiphile compartment itself, and it does not occur when no amphiphile is supplied to that compartment.

claims.statement: In the reconstituted proteoliposomes of Berhanu et al. the lipid boundary is what holds the pumped protons: illumination lowers the external proton concentration only while the light is on, the difference relaxes when it stops because protons leak back, and raising membrane fluidity accelerates that leak while adding 30 percent cholesterol reduces it by 30 percent. Adding the uncoupler FCCP, which makes the same membrane permeable to protons, abolishes both the measured gradient and the ATP that the enclosed synthase would otherwise make, in the vesicles and inside giant vesicles alike. This is evidence for Selective Permeability in Protocellular Boundaries → Chemiosmotic Energy Transduction in Proto-Membranes in the arising role: energy transduction across a primitive boundary exists only while that boundary is selectively impermeable to the ion being moved, and it disappears when the boundary is made leaky.
claims.scope: Cause 3.44 > 3.47 (arising): one lipid-vesicle system with a light-driven pump and an ATP synthase; it shows transduction failing when proton permeability is raised, not a graded relation between permeability and output.

claims.statement: Chen, Roberts and Szostak encapsulate transfer RNA at 83 mg/ml, about 0.26 M in nucleotides, in fatty-acid vesicles and mix them with isotonic vesicles of the same membrane composition. The vesicles holding the RNA gain about 21 percent of membrane area while the isotonic ones lose about 23 percent, with fitted rates near 0.1 per minute, and the same transfer is seen with sucrose as the internal solute, whereas mixing vesicles of equal osmolarity, or vesicles with buffer alone, produces no pronounced change. This is evidence for Encapsulation of Polymers and Catalysts in Protocells → Protocellular Selection as a Population-Level Effect in the arising role: differential persistence and growth among compartments arises from what each compartment encloses, so that compartments holding polymer take membrane from those that do not.
claims.scope: Cause 3.45 > 3.48 (arising): two populations of fatty-acid vesicles differing in an encapsulated osmolyte, followed by membrane-area labels; it shows population-level differential growth driven by encapsulated polymer, not replication, inheritance or a change of genotype frequency.

claims.statement: Standfuss et al. remove the charged counterion that the protein provides to the retinal Schiff base by the mutation E113Q, in a stabilized rhodopsin reconstituted into lipid membranes. The pigment still binds 11-cis retinal and is still photoactivated, but its absorption moves from 500 nm to about 382 nm because the Schiff base is deprotonated; lowering the pH to 5.0 and adding 100 mM NaCl, so that a chloride ion takes the counterion role, shifts it back to a protonated form absorbing at about 493 nm. Both forms reach the active Meta II state on illumination. This is evidence for Protein-Structured Hydration and Ionic Microenvironments → Photopigment Photon Absorption and Isomerization in the modulation role: the protein-held charge and the ions around it do not decide whether the pigment absorbs a photon and isomerizes, but set where in the spectrum it absorbs and whether its Schiff base is protonated.
claims.scope: Cause 3.31 > 3.49 (modulation): one engineered, disulfide-stabilized rhodopsin in reconstituted membranes; it shows the ionic microenvironment tuning absorption while photoactivation persists, and does not measure quantum yields.

claims.statement: Kim et al. disrupted the c-maf gene in mice: from E12 the posterior cells of the lens vesicle fail to elongate into lens fibres, leaving a small, hollow lens cavity and no formed lens, and in adult mutant eyes the gamma-crystallin genes and betaA3/A1-crystallin are dramatically reduced while alphaA- and alphaB-crystallin are normal; the mutants are microphthalmic, but the cornea is well separated from the lens and the neural retina forms grossly normally. This is evidence for Organogenesis and Functional Differentiation → Eye Optical Interface in the arising role: without the functional differentiation of lens fibres the refractive lens of the optical interface does not form, although the other eye tissues do.
claims.scope: Cause 5.1 > 5.18 (arising): one germline transcription-factor knockout in mice read by histology from E12 to five weeks and by crystallin RT-PCR; it shows the lens component of the optical interface not forming without lens-fibre differentiation, not the dependence of the cornea or pupil, and no optical measurement is made.

claims.statement: Ashery-Padan et al. deleted Pax6 from the eye surface ectoderm of mouse embryos between E9 and E9.5, after lens induction: Sox2 is still up-regulated in the specified ectoderm, but the ectoderm neither thickens nor invaginates into a lens placode, Six3, Prox1 and alphaA-crystallin are not detected and no lens structures form, while the optic vesicle invaginates a day late into two or three separate folds that each differentiate into a laminated neuroretina. This is evidence for Tissue Morphogenesis and Pattern Formation → Eye Optical Interface in the arising role: without lens-placode morphogenesis the lens of the optical interface does not form, and the eye's single-retina pattern is lost with it.

claims.statement: In mice lacking the lens-fibre gap-junction protein Cx50, lenses are normal at E16.5 and dye coupling persists through Cx46 and Cx43, but lens growth lags after birth (lens mass 56% of control from P7, adult eyes 32% and lenses 46% lighter) and the lenses show an irregular, diffuse nuclear opacity at P14, when the eye opens, and zonular pulverulent cataracts by six months (White et al.). In lenses with N-cadherin deleted from the lens-vesicle stage, the apical tips of secondary fibre cells fail to migrate along the epithelium, the fibres do not elongate beyond the equator, primary fibres become disorganized and lens height and area are reduced by E18.5, while betaB-crystallin is expressed normally (Logan et al.). This is evidence for Intercellular Contacts and Prototissue Coordination → Eye Optical Interface in the arising role: the ordered, transparent lens of the optical interface does not form normally without these cell-cell junction components.
claims.scope: Cause 4.7 > 5.18 (arising): two single-protein junction knockouts in mouse lens; each removes one contact component while other contacts persist, and each yields a lens that forms smaller, disordered or opaque rather than no optical interface; focusing and image quality are not measured.

claims.statement: In Megf10-null mice, starburst amacrine cells are present at normal density, reach their normal layers and have normal dendrites, but their somata lose mosaic spacing: the exclusion zone shrinks to about one soma diameter and the packing factor and Voronoi regularity index fall to the values of random arrays, a disorganization stated to be evident by P0, while Vglut3 and tyrosine-hydroxylase amacrine mosaics and bistratified direction-selective ganglion-cell mosaics stay regular; horizontal-cell mosaics approach random arrangement only when Megf10 and Megf11 are both deleted, and misexpressed MEGF10 repels starburst and horizontal cells but not starburst cells lacking Megf10 (Kay et al.). This is evidence for Intercellular Contacts and Prototissue Coordination → Retinal Sampling Geometry and Ordered Visual Mapping in the arising role: the regular mosaics of these two cell types do not form without homotypic contact-mediated repulsion between neighbouring cells.

claims.statement: In Megf10-null retinas, whose starburst amacrine somata are randomly spaced and whose starburst arbors make inner-plexiform-layer errors, multielectrode-array recordings find robustly direction-selective On-Off ganglion cells in the same proportion as in wild type (74 of 551 against 80 of 609 recorded ganglion cells) with preferred directions along the cardinal axes; their tuning is broader and weaker, mainly through more null-direction spiking, and their On and Off preferred directions are less aligned (Ray et al.). This is evidence for Retinal Sampling Geometry and Ordered Visual Mapping → Retinal Circuit Preprocessing in the modulation role: direction-selective preprocessing forms without the regular starburst mosaic and lamination, which set the precision of its tuning.

claims.statement: In isolated macaque retina, enriching the pH-buffering capacity with 20 mM HEPES, which attenuates the pH-dependent feedback from horizontal cells to cones, completely and reversibly abolishes the receptive-field surround of midget ganglion cells and their L versus M cone opponency: L and M cone spike responses and excitatory conductances come into phase, and surround antagonism and opponency return after washout (Crook et al.). This is evidence for Cellular Signaling and Communication → Retinal Circuit Preprocessing in the arising role: center-surround antagonism in this pathway does not occur without the horizontal-cell feedback signal.

claims.statement: In flat-mounted mouse retina with AMPA/kainate, NMDA and GABA/glycine receptors blocked, injecting the excitatory and inhibitory conductances that the rod bipolar circuit supplies to On, Off transient and Off sustained ganglion cells reproduces the pattern of their light-evoked spikes; in Off cells the light-evoked pattern is recovered only when both conductances vary together, and conductances that vary from trial to trial as measured recover most of the light-evoked timing variability that fixed conductances lack (Murphy and Rieke). With synaptic transmission blocked by a separate antagonist mixture the retina is insensitive to light, On ganglion cells hyperpolarize and stop firing, and Off cells keep only an intrinsic, stimulus-independent firing (Margolis and Detwiler). This is evidence for Retinal Circuit Preprocessing → Retinal Ganglion Spike Encoding in the arising role: ganglion spike trains encode what the circuit delivers, and light-driven encoding does not occur without that input.
claims.scope: Cause 5.20 > 5.21 (arising): conductance replay and receptor blockade in mouse retina in vitro; it shows the pattern, timing and precision of light-evoked spike trains of three ganglion-cell types coming from circuit input, while spike generation itself is intrinsic to the ganglion cell.

claims.statement: In isolated mouse retina with synaptic transmission blocked, 0.1 micromolar TTX abolishes the fast spikes of On, Off transient and Off sustained ganglion cells and then their subthreshold oscillations; Off cells, resting near -55 mV inside the activation range of a TTX-sensitive persistent Na+ current, fire spontaneously, whereas On cells, resting near -65 mV at the current's activation threshold, stop firing, and hyperpolarizing current silences the spontaneous firing of Off cells (Margolis and Detwiler). This is evidence for Cellular Membrane Potential and Electrochemical Gradients → Retinal Ganglion Spike Encoding in the arising role: ganglion-cell spikes do not occur without the voltage-gated Na+ current, and the membrane potential relative to its activation decides whether they are generated.

claims.statement: Childs et al. kill p16Ink4a-positive cells in atherosclerosis-prone Ldlr-null mice carrying the p16-3MR transgene. Senescent cells are present in lesions but not in adjacent normal vasculature; clearing them during 88 days of high-fat feeding lowers plaque burden by about 60 percent, and three days of clearance in established 12-day fatty streaks sharply reduces lesional transcripts of the secreted factors Il1alpha, Tnfalpha, Mmp3 and Mmp13 together with the monocyte-recruitment factors Mcp1 and Vcam1. In established plaques, clearance over 100 days reduces inflammatory cytokine and monocyte-recruitment expression and the metalloproteases Mmp3, Mmp12 and Mmp13 on either diet, preserves fibrous cap and collagen, and reduces monocyte attachment to plaque-adjacent endothelium, while sorted p16-positive plaque cells are themselves enriched for Il1alpha, Mmp12, Mmp13 and Mcp1. This is evidence for Senescence-Associated Secretory Phenotype → Tissue Inflammatory Microenvironments in the arising role.

claims.statement: Horai et al. delete all isoforms of the secreted interleukin-1 receptor antagonist, the endogenous inhibitor that holds basal IL-1 signaling in check. On a BALB/cA background every knockout is arthritic by 13 weeks while no wild-type or heterozygous littermate becomes arthritic, and histology shows joint-restricted synovial and periarticular inflammation with pannus, neutrophil and lymphocyte invasion and articular erosion, with no other histopathological abnormality. Joint transcripts of IL-1beta, IL-6, TNF-alpha, COX-2 and both IL-1 receptors are raised in arthritic joints and already elevated in non-arthritic joints at 4 and at 10 to 12 weeks, which the source reads as the low IL-1 present under normal conditions inducing inflammatory genes once the antagonist is gone. This is evidence for Basal Cytokine Production and Cytokine Signaling Baseline → Tissue Inflammatory Microenvironments in the arising role.
claims.scope: Cause 4.25 > 5.22 (arising): germline deletion of the IL-1 receptor antagonist with littermate controls on two genetic backgrounds; it shows that a shift of the basal cytokine-signaling set point brings a spatially restricted inflammatory tissue context into existence where littermates have none, and it does not show that the shifted baseline suffices, since mutants on a C57BL/6J background stay disease-free at 16 weeks

claims.statement: Khan et al. remove collagen VI, the matrix component most enriched in adipose tissue, in leptin-deficient ob/ob mice with littermate controls. The null adipose tissue is less dense and less structured by electron microscopy and holds larger adipocytes although total collagen by Sirius red staining and hydroxyproline content is unchanged. In this looser matrix the local inflammatory niches are reduced: crown-like structures, which the source describes as necrotic adipocytes surrounded by activated macrophages, and TUNEL-positive adipocytes are fewer, spliced Xbp1 is strongly reduced, adipose F4/80 transcripts fall significantly in mesenteric fat together with MCP-1 and SAA3, and after a lipopolysaccharide challenge collagen-VI-null mice show lower circulating IL-6 and MCP-1 and lower adipose IL-6 and TNF-alpha. This is evidence for Organization of the Extracellular Matrix → Tissue Inflammatory Microenvironments in the arising role.
claims.scope: Cause 5.4 > 5.22 (arising): germline deletion of one adipose extracellular-matrix component in an obese mouse background with littermate controls; it shows that the organization of the matrix conditions where and how strongly the local inflammatory niches of adipose tissue form, and it does not abolish adipose inflammation or separate the matrix change from the accompanying metabolic improvement

claims.statement: Old specific-pathogen-free mice, whose colonic paracellular permeability and circulating muramyl dipeptide both rise with age, carry peribronchiolar cellular infiltrates and raised IL-6 in the lung in the absence of stimulation or overt infection, whereas age-matched germ-free mice, which have no detectable circulating muramyl dipeptide and no age-related rise in colonic permeability, show no increased leukocyte infiltration and no raised lung IL-6 relative to young germ-free or young wild-type mice. This is evidence for Gut Barrier Dysfunction and Microbial-Component Translocation → Tissue Inflammatory Microenvironments in the arising role: the localized inflammatory tissue context of the aged lung does not form when microbial components do not cross the gut barrier.
claims.scope: Cause 5.23 > 5.22 (arising): lifelong germ-free housing compared with specific-pathogen-free housing in young and old mice, with colonic 51Cr-EDTA flux, a Nod2-dependent plasma muramyl-dipeptide bioassay, blinded lung infiltrate area and lung IL-6 as readouts; it shows that a distant tissue inflammatory focus requires gut-derived microbial exposure, and not that matrix organization, transport limits or immune residency within that focus depend on the barrier.

citations.note: Support is restricted to the recorded preparation, read extent and observable.

limitations: Germ-free housing removes the microbiota altogether, so barrier failure and microbial-component translocation are withdrawn together and cannot be separated in this preparation.

claims.statement: In mouse zymosan peritonitis, giving the cyclooxygenase-2 inhibitor NS-398 at 100 micrograms thirty minutes before challenge increased exudate leukocytes by about 22 percent and polymorphonuclear cells by about 41 percent at 24 hours and reduced zymosan amounts reaching lymph nodes and spleen by more than 50 percent, the lipoxygenase inhibitor baicalein gave similar results, and the authors describe this as a resolution-deficit phenotype that blocks phagocytic removal of the microbial challenge; adding 300 nanograms of resolvin E1, protectin D1 or an aspirin-triggered lipoxin analogue together with the inhibitor markedly reduced exudate leukocytes and increased zymosan amounts in lymphatics. This is evidence for Inflammation Resolution Capacity → Tissue Inflammatory Microenvironments in the modulation role: the local inflammatory context still forms when pro-resolving capacity is blocked, but its cellular composition, duration and clearance traffic change.
claims.scope: Cause 5.26 > 5.22 (modulation): pharmacological blockade of pro-resolving mediator biosynthesis with mediator add-back in a self-limited peritoneal exudate; it shows that resolution capacity sets the magnitude and persistence of a local inflammatory context, not that the context requires it in order to form.

citations.note: Support is restricted to the recorded preparation, read extent and observable.

limitations: Enzyme inhibitors at 100 micrograms block both pro-inflammatory and pro-resolving products of the same pathways, so the deficit is not specific to the pro-resolving arm.
A single zymosan-induced peritoneal exudate over 24 hours stands for a tissue inflammatory microenvironment; chronic, matrix-organized microenvironments were not studied.
The mediator rescue is pharmacological add-back at 300 nanograms rather than restoration of endogenous synthesis.
Read through the publisher's PubMed Central article page; the figures themselves and the supplementary table carrying the lipoxygenase-inhibitor numbers were not inspected.

claims.statement: Han et al. delete Jnk1 and Jnk2 together in the myeloid lineage and feed mice a high-fat diet. Knockout and control mice become equally obese, but only controls accumulate adipose tissue macrophages, and the accumulation of F4/80-positive CD11c-positive CD206-negative M1 macrophages is prevented in the knockout while CD11c-negative CD206-positive M2 numbers are unchanged. Adipose expression of Cd68 and F4/80 and of the M1-associated genes Cd11c, Il1beta, Il6, Nos2 and Tnfalpha is decreased while the M2-associated genes Arg1, Il10, Mgl1, Mgl2, Mrc1 and Mrc2 are increased, with the same pattern in liver, and diet-induced chemokine expression is largely suppressed without a selective defect in CCR2 or CCR5, which the source reads as an intrinsic polarization defect rather than inefficient recruitment; isolated knockout macrophages show reduced interferon-gamma-induced CD11c and M1 cytokine genes with M2 differentiation intact. This is evidence for Macrophage Polarization and Local Myeloid Regulatory Bias → Tissue Inflammatory Microenvironments in the arising role.

claims.statement: Two junction-targeted mouse preparations open the intestinal barrier. Laukoetter et al. delete the tight-junction adhesion molecule JAM-A: colons keep normal epithelial architecture but gain many more small lymphoid aggregates, 30 against 7, and large isolated lymphoid follicles, 5 against 0, with more LY-6G-positive neutrophils and significantly higher colonic myeloperoxidase activity, while serum FITC-dextran after gavage rises markedly, colonic FITC-dextran flux rises from 0.25 to 2 micrograms per hour per square centimetre and transepithelial resistance falls. claims.statement: Vereecke et al. delete the ubiquitin-editing enzyme A20, which terminates NF-kappaB signaling and restrains TNF-induced apoptosis, specifically in intestinal epithelial cells. The knockouts develop normally with no spontaneous intestinal inflammation, but a normally sublethal TNF dose makes them hypothermic and diarrhoeic within 2 hours and kills all of them between 5 and 9 hours while every control survives, with higher serum IL-6 and MCP-1, extensive epithelial destruction and near-complete loss of crypt-villus structure, massive TUNEL staining of villus epithelium and raised intestinal caspase activity, and liver damage although the liver expresses normal A20. Two weeks of broad-spectrum antibiotics completely protect the knockouts from TNF lethality and completely prevent the liver damage while epithelial destruction persists, which the source reads as commensal bacteria infiltrating through the destroyed barrier and initiating the systemic response. This is evidence for Cellular Homeostasis and Stress Response → Gut Barrier Dysfunction and Microbial-Component Translocation in the arising role.

claims.statement: Summa et al. disrupt the organism's circadian regulation in two independent ways and measure intestinal permeability. Clock delta-19 mutants excrete about twice the sucralose of wild-type littermates, 2.07 against 0.96 percent of the oral dose, with no change in sucrose, mannitol or lactulose, which the source reads as a colon-specific defect; wild-type mice held under three months of weekly 12-hour light-dark phase shifts likewise excrete more sucralose than non-shifted mice, 0.91 against 0.54 percent. claims.statement: Treating 18-month-old perforin-deficient mice with the senolytic ABT-737 at 25 mg per kg for two consecutive days each month over two months reduced senescent-cell burden and lowered the top serum cytokines, including some of the most elevated proteins in old perforin-deficient serum, while white blood counts, spleen weight, tissue immune infiltration and fibrotic area all fell and tissue transcriptomes showed general repression of immune response and cytokine production with senescence-associated secretory-phenotype gene scores driven back towards those of young mice. claims.statement: In mouse blastocysts lacking Fgf4, single inner-cell-mass cells profiled from E3.25 to E4.5 show arrested differentiation of both the primitive-endoderm and the epiblast lineage, primitive-endoderm markers staying at the wild-type E3.25 level and E4.5 mutant profiles remaining distinct from wild-type epiblast. In engineered L929 cells whose contact signaling through synNotch receptors induces E-cadherin and fluorescent markers, blocking synNotch signaling with DAPT gives no increase in cell types in the three-layer circuit, and adding DAPT to preformed structures totally disrupts the distinct cell types and layers within 3 days. This is evidence for Cellular Signaling and Communication → Cell Differentiation and Specialization in the arising role: distinct differentiated states do not form without intercellular signaling, and in the synthetic system they also do not persist without it; by the priority rule arising dominates maintenance.
claims.scope: Cause 4.3 > 4.5 (arising): FGF4 loss in mouse preimplantation embryos and pharmacological block of an engineered contact-signaling circuit; it shows formation, and in the synthetic system persistence, of distinct cell states depending on signaling, not differentiation in general.

citations.note: Support is restricted to the recorded preparation, read extent and observable.

citations.note: Support is restricted to the recorded preparation, read extent and observable.

limitations: The Fgf4-null profiles come from few embryos (one embryo each at E3.5 and E4.5) and are cross-sectional expression snapshots, not lineage tracing.
The synthetic cell types are reporter-defined expression states in an engineered fibroblast line, and DAPT inhibits gamma-secretase broadly.
Persistence of natural differentiated states without signaling is not tested here.

claims.statement: Mouse beta cells with RIP-Cre deletion of the maintenance DNA methyltransferase Dnmt1 form normal islets at birth and in young mice, whose beta-cell DNA methylation is not yet reduced; with age, as dividing beta cells passively lose methylation, the mutants show reduced methylation, more glucagon-expressing and fewer insulin-expressing islet cells and abnormal glucose tolerance, and lineage tracing shows glucagon-expressing cells derived from cells that had transcribed insulin, their number rising dramatically by 8 months. The alpha-cell determinant Arx is methylated and repressed in beta cells and unmethylated in a subset of lineage-labelled Dnmt1-deficient cells, and Dnmt1 knockdown in Min6 cells progressively demethylates Arx with cell duplications. This is evidence for Epigenetic Regulation and Chromatin Modification → Cell Differentiation and Specialization in the maintenance role: the beta-cell state is established, but is not maintained through cell division without propagation of DNA methylation.
claims.scope: Cause 3.19 > 4.5 (maintenance): conditional deletion with lineage tracing in mouse beta cells and cell-line knockdowns; it shows maintenance of one differentiated identity by propagated DNA methylation, not the establishment of differentiation.

claims.statement: Clonal mouse D1 mesenchymal stem cells encapsulated in RGD-coupled alginate gels and cultured for 7 days in medium with osteogenic supplements differentiate predominantly adipogenically at an initial modulus of about 9 kPa at every stress-relaxation timescale tested, with less adipogenesis in rapidly relaxing gels, and show no adipogenesis at about 17 kPa, where osteogenic differentiation rises significantly with faster stress relaxation (Spearman p < 0.0001) and an interconnected mineralized, collagen-1-rich matrix forms at 14 days only in rapidly relaxing gels; at lower RGD density the osteogenic effect is diminished. This is evidence for Organizing Influence of the Extracellular Matrix on Cell Phenotype → Cell Differentiation and Specialization in the modulation role: the matrix's mechanical properties shift which lineage the cells adopt and how far, while differentiation occurs in every matrix tested.
claims.scope: Cause 5.15 > 4.5 (modulation): synthetic alginate matrices of defined initial modulus, stress relaxation and adhesion-ligand density for one stromal stem-cell line; it shows the matrix changing differentiation outcome, not differentiation without a matrix or the action of native tissue matrix.

claims.statement: In yeast whose Hog1 MAP kinase is replaced by an analog-sensitive allele, inhibiting Hog1 kinase activity with 1-NM-PP1 before a 0.4 M NaCl shock eliminates post-shock volume recovery, keeps nuclear Hog1 from returning to its pre-stimulus level and prevents the shock-induced increase in glycerol synthesis, while the Hog1-independent transient reduction of glycerol leakage remains; cells with wild-type Hog1 adapt perfectly in the presence of the inhibitor, and untreated cells restore volume growth and nuclear Hog1 together about 25 min after the step. This is evidence for Cellular Signaling and Communication → Cellular Homeostasis and Stress Response in the maintenance role: the cell's osmotic homeostasis is not restored after a perturbation without the kinase signaling of the osmostress pathway.
claims.scope: Cause 4.3 > 4.6 (maintenance): chemical-genetic inhibition of one MAP kinase in yeast lacking the Sho1 branch, under step hyperosmotic shocks; it shows volume and glycerol homeostasis after perturbation depending on signaling, not every homeostatic variable.

claims.statement: In wild-type Saccharomyces cerevisiae the plasma-membrane H+-ATPase holds cytosolic pH nearly constant when the external pH is titrated, whereas in the pma1-007 hypomorph, with about 50 percent of plasma-membrane ATPase level and activity, acidifying the medium from pH 5.0 to 2.0 lowers cytosolic pH from 7.0 to 6.2 and progressively lowers growth, the growth rate falling exactly as predicted from the wild-type relation between cytosolic pH and growth rate, with nutrient abundance unaffected. This is evidence for Regulation of pH and Ionic Balance → Cellular Homeostasis and Stress Response in the maintenance role: when proton-pumping pH regulation is weakened, the cell no longer holds its internal pH under an external acid load, and its growth falls with it.
claims.scope: Cause 3.28 > 4.6 (maintenance): a hypomorphic proton-pump allele in yeast under controlled external acidification; it shows persistence of internal pH and growth depending on pH-regulation capacity, not the effect of removing pH regulation entirely.

citations.locator: Results on pHc-growth-rate relationships and PMA1 perturbation; Materials and methods: pHluorin fluorescence and pH calibration
citations.note: Support is restricted to the recorded preparation, read extent and observable.

limitations: A hypomorph, not a deletion: PMA1 activity is reduced by about half, and the wild-type external-pH titration is in an additional file that was not read.
Growth rate stands in for viable internal conditions; ions other than protons are not measured.

claims.statement: Yeast lacking the constitutive cytosolic Hsp70 genes SSA1 and SSA2, which stay viable through Hsf1-induced SSA3 and SSA4, grow severely impaired at 30 C and are inviable at 37 C in spot assays; cells lacking all four SSA genes but expressing two copies of SSA2 from the Hsf1-independent TEF1 promoter grow like wild type at 30 C, only slightly less at 37 C, and dissolve heat-induced Hsp104-marked protein aggregates with wild-type kinetics after a shift to 39 C, although Hsf1 then fails to deactivate. This is evidence for Chaperones and Protein Quality Control Mechanisms → Cellular Homeostasis and Stress Response in the maintenance role: viable growth under thermal stress and restoration of proteostasis after heat shock are not maintained without sufficient Hsp70 chaperone capacity.
claims.scope: Cause 3.20 > 4.6 (maintenance): deletion and promoter-swap strains of the cytosolic Hsp70 family in budding yeast with growth and aggregate-clearance readouts; it shows the chaperone supporting heat-stress survival and proteostasis, not all of cellular homeostasis.

claims.statement: siRNA knockdown of the glutathione peroxidase GPX4 (about 20-fold mRNA decrease) in HT-1080 fibrosarcoma cells causes cell death with accumulation of lipid reactive oxygen species; the death is suppressed by the iron chelator deferoxamine, the MEK inhibitor U0126 and vitamin E, which do not suppress death from a control siRNA pool against essential genes, and siGPX4 kills HRAS-V12-expressing BJeLR and DRD fibroblasts but not BJeH and BJeHLT cells. Glutathione depletion by erastin is required for its lethality, as glutathione or N-acetylcysteine prevents erastin-induced death. This is evidence for Redox Systems and Regulation of Oxidation–Reduction Balance → Cellular Homeostasis and Stress Response in the maintenance role: the cell's viable state does not persist when its glutathione-dependent reduction of lipid peroxides is removed, and an added antioxidant restores it.
claims.scope: Cause 3.25 > 4.6 (maintenance): RNAi and glutathione depletion in cultured cancer and engineered fibroblast lines with inhibitor rescue; it shows viability depending on one redox system in a context-dependent way, consistent with the enabling necessity, not homeostasis in normal tissue.

citations.note: Support is restricted to the recorded preparation, read extent and observable.

claims.statement: In murine RAW264.7 macrophages and human alveolar macrophages, 100 ng/ml LPS for 16 h induces autophagy (61.8 percent of human alveolar macrophages with autophagosomes against 10.3 percent of untreated cells) without a significant effect on viability; TLR4 siRNA completely abrogates and dominant-negative TLR4 markedly inhibits the LPS-induced autophagy, TRIF siRNA completely prevents it, MyD88 inhibition has no effect, and class III PI3-kinase inhibition blocks it; the induced autophagy raises the fraction of Mycobacterium tuberculosis bacilli in autophagosomes from 11 to 79 percent. This is evidence for Innate Immune Pattern Recognition and Damage-Associated Inflammatory Signaling → Cellular Homeostasis and Stress Response in the modulation role: pattern-recognition signaling raises a protective autophagic response that is present at a basal level without it.
claims.scope: Cause 4.23 > 4.6 (modulation): a bacterial ligand acting through TLR4 and TRIF in cultured macrophages, with receptor and adaptor knockdowns; it shows pattern recognition changing the level of a homeostatic process, not homeostasis depending on it.

claims.statement: In mouse embryonic fibroblasts and HEK293 cells, glucose starvation activates the autophagy-initiating kinase Ulk1 through AMPK, which phosphorylates Ser317 and Ser777, while active mTORC1 phosphorylates Ser757 and disrupts the Ulk1–AMPK interaction, an effect reversed by rapamycin. Ulk1-/- fibroblasts are defective in autophagy and undergo marked apoptosis under glucose starvation; re-expressing wild-type Ulk1 rescues both, whereas Ulk1 lacking the AMPK sites (S317/777A) gives significantly compromised starvation-induced LC3 lipidation, GFP-LC3 puncta and autophagosome formation and protects less against starvation-induced apoptosis. This is evidence for mTOR/Nutrient-Sensing Control of Autophagy and Senescence → Cellular Homeostasis and Stress Response in the modulation role: removing the nutrient-sensing input to Ulk1 weakens the starvation-induced autophagic and protective response without abolishing it.
claims.scope: Cause 4.31 > 4.6 (modulation): Ulk1 knockout and phosphosite-mutant reconstitution in mouse fibroblasts under glucose starvation, with kinase and interaction assays; it shows nutrient-sensing control changing the strength of a protective stress response, not homeostasis depending on it under nutrient-rich conditions.

claims.statement: In aggregates of engineered mouse L929 fibroblasts, synNotch signaling from CD19 sender cells induces E-cadherin in receiver cells, which then sort into a tight core; when synNotch signaling is blocked with DAPT from the start, E-cadherin is not induced and no sorting into layers occurs, and when DAPT is added to preformed three-layer structures the layered structure and the distinct cell types are totally disrupted within 3 days, the original cells becoming randomly organized. This is evidence for Cellular Signaling and Communication → Intercellular Contacts and Prototissue Coordination in the arising role: the cadherin-based layered organization does not form without signaling, and the same signaling is also needed to keep it.
claims.scope: Cause 4.3 > 4.7 (arising): an engineered synNotch-to-cadherin circuit in L929 fibroblast aggregates; signaling is required for the first formation of the sorted structure and also maintains it, so by the priority rule arising is the dominant role; the dependency is built into the circuit, and natural cadherin contacts are not tested.

claims.statement: In aggregates of engineered L929 fibroblasts, reciprocal synNotch signaling converts two starting genotypes into three phenotypic cell types, E-cadherin-high GFP core cells, E-cadherin-low mCherry middle cells and E-cadherin-negative blue outer cells, which sort into three layers in about 90 percent of 28 replicate wells; when this fate divergence is blocked with DAPT there is no increase in cell types and no sorting into layers, and when the fates diverge without cadherin outputs the marker-expressing cell types remain randomly mixed. This is evidence for Cell Differentiation and Specialization → Intercellular Contacts and Prototissue Coordination in the modulation role: the cells assemble with or without divergent cell states, and the differentiated adhesion states change how their contacts are arranged.
claims.scope: Cause 4.5 > 4.7 (modulation): a synthetic fate-bifurcation circuit whose differentiated states differ in cadherin level, in L929 fibroblast aggregates; it shows differentiated states ordering contacts into layers, not natural differentiation or the formation of contacts themselves.

claims.statement: In single-copy lac UV5 promoter-lacZ constructs in Escherichia coli, Lac repressor bound to a weak promoter-proximal O2 operator alone gives a leaky 2-3-fold IPTG-reversible repression; adding a strong auxiliary Osym operator in phase upstream (65 bp) or downstream (67 bp), so that the tetrameric repressor bridges both operators in a DNA loop, raises the repression ratio to 99 and 68, 33- and 23-fold above O2 alone, whereas out-of-phase or too-short spacings give little or no loop-dependent enhancement and no repression remains when O2 is disrupted; the authors attribute the enhancement to the loop raising the local repressor concentration at O2. This is evidence for Cooperativity in Proteins and Complexes → Genetic Regulation and Gene Expression in the modulation role: inducible repression forms without the two-operator cooperation, which raises its gain by more than an order of magnitude.
claims.scope: Cause 3.5 > 4.8 (modulation): engineered lac promoters with one or two operators on a single-copy episome; it removes the loop-mediated cooperation between two operators, not the repressor's subunit coupling or allosteric induction, so it does not test regulation without any cooperativity.

claims.statement: In budding yeasts gene expression forms and persists without RNAi, while RNAi lowers selected transcripts: Saccharomyces cerevisiae lacks recognizable Dicer, Argonaute and RNA-dependent RNA polymerase genes and siRNA-like small RNAs; Saccharomyces castellii Δdcr1 and Δago1 mutants, which lose or reduce siRNAs, are viable with no obvious growth disadvantage and show modest transcriptome changes apart from more than 7-fold higher consensus Y' mRNA and more than 4-fold higher palindromic Ty-fragment transcripts; and introducing S. castellii Dcr1 and Ago1 into S. cerevisiae silences a GFP reporter (more than 100-fold lower mRNA with a hairpin trigger), an endogenous URA3 gene and Ty1 retrotransposon protein, mRNA and transposition. This is evidence for RNA Interference and Non-Coding RNAs → Genetic Regulation and Gene Expression in the modulation role: removing RNAi leaves gene expression in place, and RNAi changes the expression level of its targets.
claims.scope: Cause 3.23 > 4.8 (modulation): RNAi gene deletions in S. castellii and reconstitution of RNAi in S. cerevisiae; it removes or adds the Dicer-Argonaute pathway, not every regulatory non-coding RNA, and measures transcript, reporter and transposon levels rather than whole regulatory programmes.

claims.statement: In mouse 3134 cells kept in hormone-free charcoal-stripped serum, eight 20 min pulses of 100 nM corticosterone separated by 40 min washouts make nascent transcripts of GR-regulated genes rise during each pulse and fall to very low levels during each washout, whereas constant corticosterone drives continuous release and higher mature Per1, Mt2 and Fkbp5 RNA and Fkbp5 protein; in adrenalectomized rats, whose plasma corticosterone is undetectable, hourly intravenous corticosterone pulses each produce a transient wave of liver GR activation, GR association with Per1 regulatory regions and Per1 nascent transcription. This is evidence for Neuroendocrine Influence on Gene Expression → Genetic Regulation and Gene Expression in the modulation role: gene expression proceeds without the hormone, and the pattern of glucocorticoid exposure changes the timing and level of transcription of its target genes.
claims.scope: Cause 5.16 > 4.8 (modulation): pulsed against constant corticosterone in an engineered mouse cell line and corticosterone pulses in adrenalectomized rats; it shows the adrenal hormone pattern changing transcription of GR target genes, not neural control of hormone release.

claims.statement: In adult mouse dentate gyrus, a preparation over 90 percent dentate granule neurons, ATAC-seq 1 h after synchronous neuronal activation by electroconvulsive stimulation finds 11,438 gained-open and 1,739 gained-closed chromatin regions against the basal state, enriched at active enhancers, and RNA-seq finds 849 upregulated and 409 downregulated genes; genes associated with gained-open regions overlap the upregulated set (P = 9.7e-54) and genes associated with gained-closed regions the downregulated set (P = 6.8e-4). This is evidence for Neural-State-Dependent Epigenetic and Transcriptional Modulation → Genetic Regulation and Gene Expression in the modulation role: the neurons express their genes in the basal state, and a change of neural activity state reshapes chromatin accessibility and the expression programme.

claims.statement: In a Saccharomyces cerevisiae strain whose only histone H3 gene is under GAL1 control, 3 h of repression in dextrose halves H3 protein, disrupts regular nucleosome arrays in gene bodies and lowers the occupancy of about 2,000 of about 60,000 mapped nucleosomes, chiefly at promoters; RNA-seq against wild type in dextrose detects 2,453 de-repressed and 753 decreased genes, and reduced-occupancy nucleosomes are over-represented in the promoters of genes with increased expression. This is evidence for Nucleosomal Chromatin Packaging and DNA Accessibility → Genetic Regulation and Gene Expression in the modulation role: transcription continues when nucleosome packaging is reduced, and promoter nucleosome loss changes which genes are repressed.

claims.statement: In Drosophila S2 cells, 20-hydroxyecdysone induces the E74 gene, and on re-exposure 24 h later E74 mRNA accumulates faster and to higher levels (transcriptional memory). When the elongation inhibitor flavopiridol is present before and during the first induction, no E74 transcriptional activity is observed; after washout the cells still mount a robust memory response, as they do after the TFIIH inhibitor triptolide, the memory index falling only 20-30 percent for E74, E23 and E75 against a substantial loss on Nup98 depletion. This is evidence for DNA-Directed RNA Synthesis (Transcription) → Genetic Regulation and Gene Expression in the arising role: hormone-induced expression does not form when transcription is blocked, whereas the memory state that sets later expression is established independently of transcription.

This is evidence for Enzymatic Lipid Biosynthesis and Membrane Growth → Endocytosis and Exocytosis in the arising role: endocytic internalization does not take place without ongoing enzymatic sphingoid-base synthesis.

claims.statement: Eigenbrod et al. find that mesothelial cells deficient in MyD88 secrete no CXCL1 in response to necrotic macrophage extracts or liver homogenate, while TRIF, RICK, caspase-1, ASC and TLR2/TLR4 are dispensable, and that cells lacking IL-1R produce little or no CXCL1 and show abolished or greatly impaired NF-kappaB and MAP kinase activation, although the same mutant cells respond normally to the Nod1 agonist KF1B; recombinant IL-1 receptor antagonist blocks the response of wild-type cells. claims.scope: Cause 4.3 > 4.23 (arising): germline receptor and adaptor deletions in mouse primary mesothelial cells challenged with necrotic-cell extracts; it shows that the damage-associated response does not form without IL-1R/MyD88 signalling, and does not test whether an already running response decays when signalling is withdrawn.

limitations: Mouse primary mesothelial cells and a 6-hour stimulation; the receptor-antagonist arm is pharmacological.
IL-1R and MyD88 are one branch of cellular signalling, so the result supports the parent arising only through that branch.
CXCL1 and IL-6 stand for the inflammatory output; the broader damage-sensing repertoire is not measured.
Because the deletions are constitutive, the evidence cannot separate a formation requirement from a later persistence requirement, which is exactly why the recorded maintenance role is not borne out.
Single study, one laboratory.

claims.statement: Davalos et al. find that X-irradiation, replicative exhaustion, p16INK4a overexpression and oncogenic RAS each cause a striking loss of intracellular HMGB1 from human fibroblasts and its appearance in the medium within about a day, in viable cells with no rise in lactate dehydrogenase release and not after a 0.5 Gy dose that damages without causing senescence; the secreted protein is in the oxidised, cytokine-inducing form, and reducing TLR4 mRNA by about 50 percent with shRNA, or inhibiting TLR4 signalling with CLI-95, significantly reduces IL-6 secretion by the senescent cells, while RAGE-blocking antibodies do not. citations.note: Support is restricted to the recorded preparation, read extent and observable.

HMGB1 acts both intracellularly and extracellularly in this system, so its manipulation is not a single-signal perturbation.
The senescence inducers include irradiation and oncogene activation, which have inflammatory effects of their own.
Single study.

claims.statement: Thevaranjan et al. find that intestinal permeability rises with age in mice and that circulating muramyl dipeptide, measured with a NOD2-NF-kappaB reporter bioassay, is significantly higher in the plasma of old wild-type mice, whereas germ-free mice have no detectable circulating MDP and no age-related increase in paracellular permeability; old germ-free mice lack the raised circulating IL-6 and the peribronchiolar infiltrates of old conventional mice, and their whole blood and bone-marrow-derived macrophages do not show the higher baseline and LPS-induced IL-6 seen in old specific-pathogen-free mice. The innate readout is IL-6 production and tissue infiltration rather than a direct measure of pattern-recognition receptor engagement in a defined cell.
The comparison is cross-sectional between age groups and housing conditions, not an intervention within an animal.
The source carries a 2018 correction concerning simultaneous datasets, a pathology scale and a corrected FITC-dextran concentration, recorded in the graph's reading of it.

claims.statement: Bauernfeind et al. find that resting macrophages, and macrophages given ATP or LPS alone, form no ASC pyroptosomes and cleave no caspase-1; only cells first primed for 4 hours through a transcriptionally active signalling receptor and then given an NLRP3 activator respond. Priming raises Nlrp3 but not Asc mRNA in an NF-kappaB-dependent manner, and macrophages stably overexpressing NLRP3 respond to nigericin or ATP with no prior priming. This is evidence for Innate Immune Pattern Recognition and Damage-Associated Inflammatory Signaling → Inflammasome Activation and IL-1-family Signaling in the arising role: inflammasome assembly does not occur at all until pattern-recognition and cytokine receptors have licensed it by raising NLRP3 expression.

Readouts are caspase-1 cleavage and ASC pyroptosome counts; mature IL-1beta release is not quantified in the panels read.
Single study, although its conclusion rests on several independent receptor and adaptor knockouts.

claims.statement: Munoz-Planillo et al. find that raising extracellular potassium to 30-45 mM blocks NLRP3 inflammasome activation by every agonist tested, that a fall of intracellular potassium to about 70-80 percent precedes and accompanies IL-1beta release, and that incubation in potassium-free medium alone activates NLRP3 within 30 minutes with no agonist; the same manipulation does not block AIM2 activation by transfected poly(dA-dT), which causes no potassium efflux, and caspase-1 activation by LPS alone in Nlrp3 R258W macrophages is neither accompanied by potassium efflux nor inhibited by 45 mM potassium. Homeostasis is manipulated as extracellular ionic composition, which is one dimension of the parent arising rather than its whole regime.
Potassium-free medium is a strong non-physiological perturbation, and the authors note that severe hypo-osmolarity also carries cytotoxicity.
Sodium influx modulates the threshold for some agonists, so the gate is not a single-variable one.
Single study, although it tests nine agonists and several genotypes.

claims.statement: Nakahira et al. find that the mitochondria-targeted antioxidant Mito-TEMPO inhibits IL-1beta and IL-18 secretion dose-dependently in LPS- and ATP-stimulated macrophages without affecting TNF secretion, has a negligible effect on secretion through AIM2 with poly(dA:dT), and abrogates the raised caspase-1 activation of autophagy-protein-deficient cells, while the complex I inhibitor rotenone strongly enhances caspase-1 activation and cytosolic mitochondrial DNA release. Mito-TEMPO reduces output rather than abolishing it, consistent with modulation but not quantified against a dose-response of the pathway.

claims.statement: Nakahira et al. find that peritoneal and bone-marrow-derived macrophages from Map1lc3b-deficient and Becn1-heterozygous mice, given LPS and ATP, show more cleaved caspase-1 and cleaved IL-1beta and secrete more IL-1beta and IL-18 than littermate controls, while TNF secretion, LPS-induced NF-kappaB activation and cathepsin B secretion are unchanged and the caspase-1 inhibitor z-YVAD-FMK suppresses the excess; the deficient cells accumulate damaged mitochondria, make more mitochondrial superoxide at baseline and release about twice as much mitochondrial DNA into the cytosol, and endotoxemic Map1lc3b-deficient mice have significantly higher serum IL-1beta and IL-18 with comparable TNF. claims.statement: Youm et al. find that ablation of Nlrp3 lowers the age-associated rise in caspase-1 activation in adipose tissue and significantly reduces the age-related increase in adipose Il1b expression, and that the age-related increase in circulating IL-18 is significantly reduced in Nlrp3-deficient mice and totally abrogated in Asc-deficient mice but unaffected in caspase-11 mutants, while the loss of Nlrp3 and Asc does not affect the age-related increase in IL-6. Single study.

claims.statement: Gough et al. find that the STAT1-inducing activity of fibroblast-conditioned medium is entirely blocked by type I interferon neutralising antibodies at concentrations capable of neutralising about 5 IU/mL IFN-beta and almost ablated by a blocking antibody against IFNAR1, that RNAi knockdown of IFN-beta in wild-type donor cells significantly reduces the STAT1-inducing activity of their medium, and that wild-type fibroblasts cultured with anti-IFNAR1 progressively lose STAT1 alpha/beta protein over 24, 72 and 96 hours against an equally loaded 96-hour immunoglobulin control. citations.note: Support is restricted to the recorded preparation, read extent and observable.

The 96-hour anti-IFNAR1 time course is a single immunoblot with a tubulin loading control and no quantification, and the Results text does not describe this panel.
Antibody blockade is incomplete inhibition rather than removal, and conditioned-medium transfer adds a paracrine component.
Single study.

claims.statement: Rodier et al. find that a 10 Gy dose increases IL-6 and IL-8 secretion by human fibroblasts five- to sixfold within 2-4 days and to replicatively senescent levels within 3-5 days, whereas a 0.5 Gy dose that causes transient damage leaves IL-6 secretion at control levels; as cells approach replicative senescence, persistent damage foci accumulate and IL-6 secretion rises in parallel, expressing telomerase lowers both, and cells driven into senescence by p16INK4a overexpression display few persistent foci and secrete little IL-6 while expressing other senescence markers. This is evidence for Cellular Senescence as a Stress Outcome → Basal Cytokine Production and Cytokine Signaling Baseline in the modulation role: the senescent state carries a persistently raised cytokine output relative to presenescent cells of the same strain, and the size of that shift tracks persistent damage signalling rather than the arrest itself.

Senescence is induced by irradiation or replicative exhaustion, each with effects beyond the senescent state itself.
Single study.

claims.statement: Davalos et al. find that depleting HMGB1 in senescent human fibroblasts with either of two shRNAs reduces IL-6 and MMP-3 secretion by more than 90 percent, that an HMGB1-blocking antibody reduces IL-6 secretion two- to threefold at 4 and 8 micrograms per millilitre while a lower dose and the control antibody do not, and that reducing TLR4 by shRNA or inhibiting TLR4 signalling with CLI-95 significantly reduces IL-6 secretion by the same cells; recombinant HMGB1 drives NF-kappaB translocation and restores IL-6 secretion in HMGB1-depleted cells. HMGB1 has opposing intracellular and extracellular effects in this system, so shRNA depletion removes both at once; the blocking antibody isolates the extracellular arm but gives only a two- to threefold reduction.
IL-6 and MMP-3 stand for the cytokine baseline, and TLR4 is reduced by about 50 percent rather than deleted.
Only one SASP component is manipulated out of a complex secretory program.
Single study.

claims.statement: Thevaranjan et al. find that germ-free mice do not display the age-related rise in circulating IL-6 seen in conventional mice, show no age-related increase in colonic paracellular permeability and have no detectable circulating muramyl dipeptide, and that their whole blood and bone-marrow-derived macrophages show no age-related increase in baseline or LPS-induced IL-6; colonising germ-free mice by co-housing shows that microbiota sourced from old mice significantly increase paracellular permeability and that young recipients given old microbiota have higher plasma TNF than those given young microbiota. The source carries a 2018 correction concerning simultaneous datasets, a pathology scale and a corrected FITC-dextran concentration, recorded in the graph's reading of it.
Both study contexts come from a single publication and laboratory.

claims.statement: Primary MEFs grown in atmospheric 20 percent oxygen senesced after 8–10 population doublings, but in physiological 3 percent oxygen they showed no senescence over more than 60 doublings while keeping p53- and Rb-dependent growth control; 3 percent cultures shifted to 20 percent at PD8 or PD13 senesced after 5–6 further doublings, low oxygen delayed without abolishing the senescence of repair-deficient Balb/c MEFs, and Ku80−/− MEFs senesced rapidly at either tension. claims.statement: In TIG3-TERT human fibroblasts, shRNA depletion of the PRC2 components EZH2 or SUZ12 decreased H3K27me3 and displaced BMI1 and CBX8 from the INK4A promoter and, like BMI1 depletion, activated INK4A transcription and caused senescence detected by SA-β-galactosidase; conversely, ectopic BMI1 bound the INK4A promoter and repressed it, and in fibroblasts approaching senescence EZH2 and H3K27me3 were lost from the locus as INK4A rose. claims.statement: Cambridge et al. synchronized replication and division in an E. coli dnaC28(Ts) initiation mutant by a 42 C block and release to 28 C: in untreated cultures 45-50 percent of cells had Z rings by 120 minutes and cell number doubled by 150-180 minutes, whereas hydroxyurea or nalidixic acid added after replication resumed blocked replication, suppressed Z-ring formation below background and held cell number approximately constant while mass and cell length kept increasing; the block occurred in a deltasulA strain and in SOS-noninducible deltaslmA cells, and none of 449 hydroxyurea-treated deltamin cells formed a Z ring over a compact nucleoid. The authors propose that a compact, incompletely replicated nucleoid at the mid-cell division site inhibits Z-ring formation independently of SOS, SlmA and MinC. This is evidence for Template-Directed Replication of Nucleic Acids → Cell Division and Cellular Reproduction in the arising role: when chromosome replication stops partway, the division machinery does not assemble and the cell does not divide.

claims.statement: Walter et al. found that in E. coli whose respiration was blocked by azide or oxygen depletion, flagellar rotation of tethered cells was nearly zero at high azide until proteorhodopsin pumping under green light restored it to the speed of cells with unimpaired respiration, whereas cells lacking proteorhodopsin did not respond to green light; in low-oxygen cultures the protonophore CCCP eliminated all bacterial motility, which 50 seconds of green illumination did not restore. This is evidence for Cellular Membrane Potential and Electrochemical Gradients → Cell Motility and Directed Migration in the arising role: flagellar motility appears with the transmembrane proton-motive force and is absent when that gradient is dissipated, even with the pump running.

claims.statement: Yam et al. found that about 45 percent of stationary, radially symmetric fish epidermal keratocytes spontaneously broke symmetry and initiated persistent polarized motility within 30 minutes of a shift from 20 to 30 C, whereas inhibiting myosin II with blebbistatin before the shift decreased this fraction to 10 percent, as did the Rho kinase inhibitor Y-27632 (P < 0.0001); microtubule depolymerization with nocodazole and inhibition of PI 3-kinase or myosin light chain kinase had no effect, the myosin phosphatase inhibitor calyculin A raised initiation to 100 percent, and the drugs had little effect on the steady-state speed of keratocytes that were already moving. This is evidence for Intracellular Transport and Cytoskeletal Systems → Cell Motility and Directed Migration in the arising role: the onset of crawling motility requires Rho kinase-dependent actomyosin contraction, which is dispensable once movement is established.

claims.statement: Walter et al. found that inhibiting E. coli respiration lowered the proton-motive force read from flagellar rotation, to 50 percent of its original value at 55 mM azide, with rotation nearly zero at high azide, and that cells with respiration inhibited by azide or oxygen depletion swam slowly until green-light pumping by proteorhodopsin restored rotation to the speed of cells with unimpaired respiration; on removal of the green light they slowed to their previous velocity, and cells lacking proteorhodopsin did not respond. Respiration is replaceable by a heterologous light-driven pump, so the necessity holds for energy conversion as a whole, not for respiration in particular.
The proton-motive force is inferred from motor speed.

claims.statement: Wu et al. characterized Dictyostelium cells lacking the G protein β subunit: in small-population and agar-cutting assays over wide ranges of cAMP and folic acid (10^-8 to 10^-3 M) and with bacterial extracts and urine, gβ− cells never displayed a detectable chemotaxis response in multiple trials, and unlike wild-type cells they did not extend pseudopods towards cAMP released from a micropipette, while in these tests their motility appeared similar to that of wild-type cells and time-lapse videos suggested that Gβ is not required for motility; the abstract reports that they also lacked GTP-regulated high-affinity chemoattractant binding and chemoattractant-stimulated adenylyl and guanylyl cyclase activity. claims.statement: In CD11b-DTR mice recovering from 12 weeks of carbon-tetrachloride liver injury, diphtheria-toxin depletion of scar-associated macrophages during the first week of recovery stopped the structural reorganization of the scar: sirius-red material fell by 85 per cent in control mice after recovery but persisted with depletion, rising from 1 per cent of the biopsy to more than 3 per cent; the perisinusoidal fibrosis score stayed at 1.9 against 1.0 in recovering controls and 2.5 at peak fibrosis; collagen III was 50 per cent higher; and elastin, which declined in recovering controls, showed no reduction. claims.statement: In mouse M1 intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells recorded with fast synaptic transmission blocked, loose-patch recordings show that the intrinsic melanopsin photoresponse is what modulates the cells' spike output, a flash raising the firing rate above its spontaneous 2.3 Hz at a threshold of about 1.9 by 10^5 photons per square micrometre, close to the intensity for a single-photon response. Deleting the signalling enzyme PLCbeta4 reduces that photoresponse to at most 1 per cent of wild type, and deleting both TRPC6 and TRPC7 leaves the cells not intrinsically photosensitive, while in both cases the cells still fire impulses normally to injected current. This is evidence for Cellular Signaling and Communication as a condition for Retinal Ganglion Spike Encoding in the arising role: the graded signal that these ganglion cells convert into spikes is generated by the intracellular signalling cascade, which the spike-generating machinery alone does not supply.

claims.statement: Tenascin-C-null mice given 3 per cent dextran sodium sulphate still develop the barrier-failure regime: the middle and distal colon ulcerate with loss of EpCAM staining and abrogated crypt architecture, and the disease activity index rises as in wild type. The deletion nonetheless changes the regime, with significantly less colon shortening, less body-weight loss, a significantly lower distal-colon histopathology score, areas of intact EpCAM-positive epithelium with preserved crypts found only in the null mice, and less severe distal lesions still after 17 days of recovery. This is evidence that Organization of the Extracellular Matrix acts on Gut Barrier Dysfunction and Microbial-Component Translocation in the modulation role with contextual rather than necessary necessity: removing a matrix component alters how severe the barrier failure becomes while the failure still forms.

A single study.

claims.statement: Raising pro-resolving efferocytosis capacity pharmacologically in mice with dextran-sodium-sulphate colitis attenuated the barrier-failure regime: columbamine reduced body-weight loss, colon shortening, disease activity index, spleen weight and colonic myeloperoxidase activity, improved colon histology and dramatically reduced apoptotic cells in the colon, while the colitis itself persisted. claims.statement: Schistosome infection and caecal-ligation-and-puncture sepsis each raised thymic IL-33 and produced thymic involution with a disturbed medullary-to-cortical thymic-epithelial-cell ratio, and naive T cells that lost CD5 expression and proliferated poorly. claims.statement: Almaatouq et al. randomized online groups of 12 to networks in which members chose up to three peers to follow after each of 20 estimation rounds, with no performance feedback, feedback on their own performance or feedback on all members' performance: the correlation between a member's number of followers and cumulative performance was 0.62 with full feedback against 0.3 and 0.2 with own or no feedback, and with feedback the follow networks evolved from fully distributed into centralized structures that amplified well-informed members, decentralized after an information shock and re-adapted; dynamic networks also produced 17% lower individual error than static networks of the same degree. claims.statement: In anonymous public-goods groups of four re-formed every round, contributions declined over six rounds without punishment (by 1.08 of 20 units per round, P<0.001) but stayed constant when one randomly designated member per group could punish, just as when all members could punish (O'Gorman et al.); in 50 Ugandan farmer cooperatives, a monitor with sanctioning power raised contributions by 15.0% when chosen by lottery and by 25.4% when elected, already before any sanction, relative to a six-round baseline without a monitor in which contributions did not decline (Baldassarri and Grossman). This is evidence for Political and Governance Structures → Cooperation and Conflict in Large-Scale Societies in the maintenance role with an enabling rather than necessary dependency: a centralized enforcement office keeps cooperation among anonymous strangers from decaying and raises it in natural groups, but peer sanctions sustain it equally and members of a cooperative kept cooperating without a central authority.

claims.statement: Romano et al. had 3,236 adults from stratified online panels in 17 countries make one-shot trust-game decisions with partners from their own country, from another of the 16 countries or of unknown nationality: across societies, participants sent more to compatriots than to foreigners and strangers (b=0.19, P<0.001), expected more from them (b=0.29, P=0.002) and returned more to them (b=0.95, P=0.001), while still trusting and reciprocating with outgroup partners and strangers; this ingroup favouritism varied little between countries. claims.statement: Slaughter et al. followed 40,078 posts on X for which Community Notes were proposed in March-June 2023 and compared the 6,757 posts whose crowd-rated fact-checking note was displayed with bias-corrected synthetic controls built from posts whose notes never reached helpful status: once a note was attached, growth in reposts fell by 46.1% and in likes by 44.1% (replies 21.9%, views 13.5%), repost cascades grew less deep and less viral at equal growth in size but not less broad, and notes attached within 12 hours cut repost growth by 49.6% against 6.2% for notes attached after 47 hours. claims.statement: Twitter kept a randomly chosen control group of accounts on reverse-chronological Home timelines when it introduced personalized ranking in 2016; comparing linger impressions between this control group and a treatment sample, Huszár et al. found that the ranking raised the reach of every studied party's tweets above the chronological baseline, in some cases by more than 200%, amplified the mainstream right significantly more than the mainstream left in six of seven countries (Canada Liberals 43% against Conservatives 167%, United Kingdom Labour 112% against Conservatives 176%), amplified individual legislators from below 0% to 400%, and, by AllSides ratings, amplified partisan more than Center news sources. claims.statement: Guilbeault et al. asked 2,400 conservative and liberal online participants to forecast Arctic sea ice from a NASA graph whose final point runs against the long-term trend: at baseline 60.8% of conservatives and 73.9% of liberals read the trend correctly; in bipartisan networks that showed the neighbours' average estimate without partisan cues, trend accuracy rose by 16.6 percentage points and the partisan difference disappeared, conservatives reaching 88.3% against 62.9% in control, whereas with party logos displayed improvement did not exceed that of isolated controls and liberals stayed 13.7 points ahead, and with the neighbours' political identities displayed learning was reduced and a 12.4-point gap remained. This is evidence for Social Identity and Group Belonging → Mass Cognitive Distortion Regimes in the modulation role: making partisan identity salient preserves a party-aligned misreading of scientific data that social learning otherwise removes.
claims.scope: Cause 7.19 > 7.23 (modulation): randomized online networks of 40 people interpreting one graph; it shows identity cues changing the persistence of a group-aligned error, not the formation of the distortion or its societal scale.

claims.statement: In Mäs and Flache's laboratory experiment, groups of eight students interacted by computer, first with same-type partners and then with other-type partners.
