citations.note: Support is restricted to the recorded preparation, read extent and observable.

limitations: Mice, one calcium indicator and two brain regions, with three to eight animals per pharmacological condition.
DSP4 is a systemic neurotoxin whose selectivity for noradrenergic axons is pharmacological rather than genetic.
Astrocytic calcium is a proxy for astrocytic regulation of circuit conditions, which was not itself measured.
Locomotion is the behavioural driver, so arousal and movement are not separated.
Figure captions were read but figures were not inspected and the procedures were not read.

claims.statement: Roth et al. exposed infant rats for 30 minutes daily on postnatal days 1 to 7 either to a mother stressed by limited nesting resources in an unfamiliar environment, who treated the pups abusively, or to a non-stressed cross-fostering mother with abundant resources, with home-cage littermates as a further control. Adults that had been maltreated had significantly suppressed BDNF messenger RNA in the prefrontal cortex relative to both control groups, while the hippocampal change was shared with cross-fostered controls and so not specific to maltreatment. Maltreatment produced a significant increase in methylated BDNF exon IX DNA at postnatal days 8, 30 and 90 and, in adults, at exon IV as well, confirmed by bisulfite sequencing across twelve exon IV CpG sites and by methylated-DNA immunoprecipitation, whereas Reelin expression and promoter methylation were unchanged. Seven days of intracerebroventricular infusion of the DNA methylation inhibitor zebularine in adults lowered exon IV methylation and restored both exon IV and total BDNF messenger RNA. This is evidence for Societal Feedback on Individual Neurodynamics to Neural-State-Dependent Epigenetic and Transcriptional Modulation in the modulation role: an experimentally imposed social caregiving environment sets a durable chromatin and transcriptional state in the brain, and a pharmacological reversal of that chromatin mark restores the transcript.
claims.scope: Cause 7.20 > 6.14 (modulation): a controlled rodent model of adverse early caregiving with cross-fostered and home-cage controls, one gene with a control gene, and a methylation-inhibitor rescue in adults; it shows that a social environment durably modulates epigenetic and transcriptional state, not that social organisation is required for such modulation.

citations.note: Support is restricted to the recorded preparation, read extent and observable.

limitations: Rats, one week of early adversity, one gene with a single control gene.
Methylation and expression are tissue averages over cell types in the dissected prefrontal cortex.
Zebularine is infused into the ventricle and its mechanism in non-dividing neurons is not established; baseline methylation differed between vehicle-treated cohorts.
The read passages contain no behavioural outcome, so the claim concerns molecular state only.
A rodent caregiving manipulation stands in for the social organisation of the parent arising.

claims.statement: Hodes et al. measured interleukin-6 release from lipopolysaccharide-stimulated leukocytes before any stress and then exposed mice to repeated social defeat. Leukocytes from animals that later proved behaviourally susceptible had released more interleukin-6 before the stress than those from animals that proved resilient (F(1,36) equal to 15, p less than 0.001). Replacing the haematopoietic compartment with interleukin-6-deficient cells, by irradiating mice with the head shielded in lead and reconstituting them with knockout bone marrow, made them as resilient as interleukin-6 knockout animals, with a significant main effect of the deletion (F(1,43) equal to 9.18, p less than 0.01), and the knockout chimeras were also more resilient in the witness version of the stress; peripheral blockade with an interleukin-6 monoclonal antibody, but not an IgG antibody or saline, prevented the development of social avoidance (F(3,72) equal to 7.14, p less than 0.01). This is evidence for Basal Cytokine Production and Cytokine Signaling Baseline to Neuro-Immune Interactions in the modulation role: the pre-stress capacity of peripheral leukocytes to release a cytokine sets how neural and behavioural state responds to a social challenge, and removing that peripheral source changes the outcome.
claims.scope: Cause 4.25 > 6.15 (modulation): a bone-marrow chimera knockout and a peripheral antibody blockade in mice, with social interaction after repeated social defeat as the read-out and a pre-stress leukocyte assay as the predictor; it shows that the peripheral cytokine baseline modulates the neuro-immune response to stress, not that it is required for neuro-immune coupling.

citations.note: Support is restricted to the recorded preparation, read extent and observable.

Irradiation and reconstitution have systemic effects of their own, although the head was shielded.
One cytokine is manipulated and the neural pathway through which it acts is not measured in the read passages.
The pre-stress leukocyte measurement is correlational; only the knockout and antibody arms are interventions.
A published correction to this paper, read here, changes one author's name only.

claims.statement: Ogrodnik et al. cleared p16Ink4a-positive senescent cells from aged INK-ATTAC mice, either pharmacogenetically with AP20187 or pharmacologically with dasatinib and quercetin, and compared them with vehicle-treated aged and young mice. Of 29 detectable brain cytokines, ten differed between young and old, and the age-associated cytokine profile was significantly alleviated by AP20187 (p equal to 0.026) though not by dasatinib and quercetin (p equal to 0.15). Hippocampal interleukin-1 alpha messenger RNA foci, an upstream regulator of the senescence secretome, rose with age in CA3 (p less than 0.0001) and were significantly reduced by dasatinib and quercetin (p equal to 0.0278), microglial soma size in CA3 increased with age and was significantly reduced by both treatments, and the number of CD3-positive T cells around the lateral ventricle was raised in aged vehicle-treated mice and reduced by both. This is evidence for Senescence-Associated Secretory Phenotype to Neuro-Immune Interactions in the modulation role: removing the cells that emit the secretory phenotype changes the brain's inflammatory milieu, microglial activation and lymphocyte infiltration, while neuro-immune coupling itself persists.
claims.scope: Cause 4.27 > 6.15 (modulation): whole-body pharmacogenetic and pharmacological clearance of senescent cells in aged mice with young and vehicle-treated comparisons, measured as brain cytokines, hippocampal transcripts, microglial soma size and T-cell counts; it shows that the secretory phenotype modulates brain immune state, not that it is required for neuro-immune interaction.

citations.locator: Abstract and Results: Clearance of senescent cells reduces hippocampal microglial activation, age-related brain inflammation, and infiltration of immune cells; Figure 4 caption
citations.note: Support is restricted to the recorded preparation, read extent and observable.

limitations: Aged mice with four to ten animals per group and two clearance strategies whose effects on individual measures differ.
Clearance is whole-body, so brain changes may be secondary to peripheral clearance.
No individual cytokine reached significance; the cytokine result rests on the two-way analysis of the age-associated profile.
Microglial activation is inferred from soma size and inflammation from cytokine and transcript levels, with no neural activity measured.
The cognitive and sequencing sections and the methods were not read.

claims.statement: Lecrux et al. measured whisker-evoked cerebral blood flow by laser-Doppler flowmetry together with local field potentials in anaesthetised rats while changing cholinergic tone in both directions. Acutely raising acetylcholine with the cholinesterase inhibitor physostigmine significantly potentiated the evoked blood-flow response, and this potentiation was reduced by more than 75 percent by the muscarinic antagonist scopolamine (p less than 0.01). Chronic deprivation had the opposite effect: a 192-IgG-saporin lesion of the basal forebrain cholinergic neurons removed about 70 percent of cortical cholinergic fibres (p less than 0.001) and reduced the whisker-evoked blood-flow response by 40.7 percent (p less than 0.001), with evoked field potentials reduced across cortical layers and a potent reduction of band-limited power. The authors conclude that acetylcholine is not only a facilitator but a prerequisite for the full expression of sensory-evoked neurovascular coupling. This is evidence for Global Neurotransmitter Modulation to Neurovascular Coupling in the modulation role: a diffuse neuromodulatory state sets the gain of the vascular response to activity in both directions, while the coupling persists.
claims.scope: Cause 6.7 > 6.16 (modulation): immunotoxin lesion of the basal forebrain cholinergic system and acute cholinesterase inhibition with muscarinic blockade in anaesthetised rats, with laser-Doppler blood flow and local field potentials during whisker stimulation; it shows that one neuromodulatory system scales the evoked response, not that neurovascular coupling requires it.

citations.note: Support is restricted to the recorded preparation, read extent and observable.

The immunotoxin lesion is chronic, so compensation cannot be excluded.
Evoked neuronal responses also fell after depletion, so the vascular change is not purely a coupling change.
Only the cholinergic system was manipulated among the diffuse neuromodulators, and the figures were not inspected.

claims.statement: Reinhart and Nguyen delivered 25 minutes of high-definition transcranial alternating-current stimulation to frontal and temporal sites of adults aged 60 to 76, tuned to each person's own theta frequency and applied in phase across the two sites. Accuracy on a visual working-memory task rose significantly relative to sham without a change in response bias or mean reaction time, the gain appeared within about 12 minutes and persisted through 50 minutes after stimulation, and older adults became statistically indistinguishable from younger adults at baseline (stimulation-by-time interaction F(8,656) equal to 16.707, p less than 0.01). In a second cohort the tuned frontotemporal montage again raised accuracy while non-tuned 8 Hz stimulation and frontal-only or temporal-only tuned montages did not differ from sham at any time bin, and in younger adults antiphase stimulation designed to desynchronize the same circuit rapidly induced working-memory deficits. This is evidence for Brain Oscillations and Rhythms to Working Memory and Executive Functions in the modulation role: changing the phase relation and frequency of a rhythm across two regions changes working-memory performance in either direction while the capacity itself persists.
claims.scope: Cause 6.2 > 6.18 (modulation): non-invasive alternating-current stimulation in humans with sham, frequency-control, montage-control and phase-reversal conditions and accuracy on one visual working-memory task as the read-out; it shows that the rhythm's phase relation modulates performance, not that working memory requires the rhythm.

citations.locator: Abstract and Results: HD-tACS improves working memory in older adults in a stable and enduring manner; HD-tACS improvement requires precise spatiospectral targeting of the brain; Changing HD-tACS phase angle provides bidirectional control of working memory performance in younger adults
citations.note: Support is restricted to the recorded preparation, read extent and observable.

limitations: Transcranial stimulation acts diffusely and the stimulated anatomy is inferred rather than measured.
One visual working-memory task with accuracy as the outcome, not a neural measure of maintenance.
Modest and differing sample sizes across the four experiments.
Working memory persisted in every condition, so the evidence concerns its regime.
The coupling and synchronization analyses and the methods were not read.

claims.statement: Ben-Ami Bartal et al. tested rats daily for twelve days with a cagemate trapped in a restrainer only the free rat could open. Opening latency fell across days in uninjected, saline-treated and nadolol-treated animals (all p less than 0.001) but not in rats given either dose of the benzodiazepine anxiolytic midazolam, so the anxiolytic removed the evidence of learning to help, and the decay differed significantly between groups (chi-squared(4) equal to 12.0, p equal to 0.02). The plateau latency on days 10 to 12 was significantly longer for high-dose midazolam than for uninjected (p equal to 0.01) or nadolol-treated rats (p equal to 0.04), and high-dose animals averaged 1.0 plus or minus 0.5 openings over twelve days against 5.7 plus or minus 1.2 in uninjected rats. Two controls bound the interpretation: nadolol, a beta-adrenergic antagonist that does not cross the blood-brain barrier, left helping intact, and with chocolate instead of a cagemate the midazolam-treated rats learned to open while saline-treated rats did not. This is evidence for Emotional and Affective Processing to Neural Mechanisms of Social Recognition and Empathy in the modulation role: pharmacologically dampening the central affective response abolishes the socially directed behaviour while the same animals still learn to open the restrainer for a non-social reward.
claims.scope: Cause 6.6 > 6.20 (modulation): systemic benzodiazepine administration in rats with a peripherally restricted antagonist and a non-social reward as controls, and door-opening latency as the read-out; it shows that the affective response modulates prosocial behaviour, not that social recognition itself depends on affect.

citations.locator: Abstract and Results: Blocking Distress in Free Rats Tested with a Trapped Cagemate; Blocking Distress in Free Rats Tested with a Chocolate-Containing Restrainer; Figures 1, 2 and 5 captions and Tables 1-2
citations.note: Support is restricted to the recorded preparation, read extent and observable.

limitations: Rats and one prosocial paradigm with door-opening latency as the only measure.
Midazolam acts broadly on GABA-A receptors, so the affective reading rests on the nadolol and chocolate controls rather than on a localised manipulation.
Within every group a substantial subpopulation never opened consistently.
Social recognition itself was not measured, and the methods and remaining analyses were not read.

claims.statement: Sincich et al. recorded extracellularly in the lateral geniculate nucleus of six anaesthetised, paralysed macaques with amplification sufficient to resolve, in 37 neurons, the synaptic potentials driven by a single retinal ganglion cell together with the relay cell's own spikes, while the receptive-field centre was stimulated with a naturalistic luminance sequence varying at 80 Hz. Between 94.6 and 99.7 percent of the geniculate spikes were driven by retinal excitatory postsynaptic potentials and the neurons rarely fired without an identifiable potential from a retinal ganglion cell, while the probability that a retinal spike produced a geniculate spike averaged 46 plus or minus 16 percent. The neurons needed to be primed within 40 ms by a preceding potential in order to fire, so potentials close in time had to summate for transmission to occur, and this facilitation was followed by depression. This is evidence for Retinal Ganglion Spike Encoding to Thalamic Visual Relay and Gain Control in the arising role: the relayed spike train is made of retinal spikes, which almost never fails to be the case, and the relay's gain is set by their timing.
claims.scope: Cause 5.21 > 6.22 (arising): paired measurement of retinal synaptic potentials and relay spikes in the macaque lateral geniculate nucleus under naturalistic luminance stimulation; it establishes the near-complete origin of relay spikes in retinal spikes and the summation requirement, without removing or silencing the retina.

citations.locator: Results: Identification of retinal input to LGN neurons and EPSP efficacy and summation requirement of LGN action potentials
citations.note: Support is restricted to the recorded preparation, read extent and observable.

citations.locator: Materials and Methods: animals, anesthesia and neuromuscular blockade, extracellular recording and visual stimulus
citations.note: Support is restricted to the recorded preparation, read extent and observable.

limitations: Six anaesthetised and paralysed macaques and the 37 neurons in which a retinal potential could be resolved.
The dependence is measured rather than produced by a removal of retinal input.
One naturalistic stimulus in the receptive-field centre; the burst mode and other stimuli lie outside the read passages.
Extracellular synaptic potentials identify the dominant retinal driver, so weaker converging inputs may be missed.

claims.statement: Two primary experiments show that a feature of the cortical map depends on retinal preprocessing. Hillier et al. ablated starburst amacrine cells in adult mice by injecting diphtheria toxin into both eyes of ChAT-Cre by LSL-DTR animals, admitting only experiments with complete starburst loss in both retinas and showing that the toxin does not reach cortical Cre-expressing cells; retinal direction-selective responses fell by 93 percent and direction-selective ganglion-cell terminals in the lateral geniculate nucleus disappeared, while ON-OFF and orientation-selective proportions and the pupil reflex were unchanged. In the cortex, the significant overrepresentation of posterior-motion-preferring direction-selective cells fell from 26.8 percent in toxin-injected wild-type controls to 6.2 percent (p equal to 3.7 times 10 to the minus 11), with a complementary rise in dorsal preference and an unchanged overall proportion of direction-selective cells. Huberman et al. blocked all spontaneous retinal activity in both eyes of ferrets from postnatal day 1 to 10 with epibatidine, with saline controls, and found in adulthood an overwhelming lack of eye-specific segregation of thalamocortical terminations in layer 4 and binocular receptive fields enlarged from 41.00 plus or minus 6.95 to 1514.69 plus or minus 206.64 square degrees (p less than 0.00001), while monocular receptive fields were normal. This is evidence for Retinal Circuit Preprocessing to Primary Visual Cortex Feature Maps in the maintenance role: an adult ablation inside the retinal circuit removes a formed property of the cortical map, and a developmental blockade of retinal output leaves the map unsegregated.
claims.scope: Cause 5.20 > 6.23 (maintenance): adult diphtheria-toxin ablation of one retinal interneuron class in mice with cortical calcium imaging, and neonatal pharmacological blockade of retinal activity in ferrets with adult anatomical and receptive-field read-outs; together they show that cortical map properties depend on retinal preprocessing both for persistence and for formation, in two species and for two different map features.

Calcium imaging and labelled terminations are indirect read-outs, and figures were not inspected here.

claims.statement: Gregoriou et al. removed the entire lateral prefrontal cortex of one hemisphere in two macaques by aspiration, verified the extent by magnetic resonance imaging and transected the corpus callosum and anterior commissure so that only the other hemisphere could still receive prefrontal feedback, then recorded V4 neurons in both hemispheres during a colour-cued orientation-discrimination task. Visual selectivity for the stimuli in the receptive field did not differ between hemispheres, but attentional enhancement did: 71 percent of neurons in the intact hemisphere showed significant enhancement and the population response rose 25 percent with attention, against 55 percent of neurons and 15 percent in the lesion-affected hemisphere, with the median attention index falling from 0.11 to 0.06 (p less than 0.001). Attentional effects also began later without prefrontal cortex, with median latencies of 199 against 161 ms, a difference that held when only neurons with attentional effects of similar size were compared. This is evidence for Cognitive Processing and Decision Making to Predictive and Top-Down Attentional Modulation of Visual Processing in the modulation role: removing the prefrontal substrate of task control reduces and delays the top-down modulation of visual responses while that modulation, and visual selectivity, persist.
claims.scope: Cause 6.3 > 6.24 (modulation): unilateral aspiration of lateral prefrontal cortex with commissural transection in two macaques, using the intact hemisphere as the within-animal control and V4 firing rates during a cued attention task as the read-out; it shows that prefrontal cortex is one source of top-down modulation, not that attentional modulation requires it.

claims.statement: Zhou et al. injected muscimol into the ventro-lateral pulvinar of macaques at sites representing the lower contralateral quadrant containing the recorded V4 receptive fields, while one of the three task stimuli lay in the ipsilateral hemifield as a within-session control. Accuracy in the attention-demanding condition fell from 74.3 to 10.8 percent in the affected quadrant, with no significant change at the ipsilateral location and only a small change in the upper contralateral field. In V4, visually evoked responses fell by 59.7 percent and the attention modulation index from 0.106 to 0.053, a 50 percent reduction which the authors state did not eliminate either the evoked response or the effect of attention; gamma coherence within V4 fell 39 percent and its attentional enhancement 49.6 percent, V4-inferotemporal gamma coherence fell 35 percent, and power below 20 Hz rose, while lateral geniculate and inferotemporal responses were unchanged. This is evidence for Thalamic Visual Relay and Gain Control to Predictive and Top-Down Attentional Modulation of Visual Processing in the modulation role: deactivating the thalamic node halves the attentional modulation of cortical responses and synchrony while that modulation persists, so the dependency is a change of regime rather than a condition of first admissibility.
claims.scope: Cause 6.22 > 6.24 (modulation): reversible muscimol deactivation of the ventro-lateral pulvinar in macaques with ipsilateral, lateral geniculate and inferotemporal controls, read out as V4 firing rates, attention indices and coherence; it shows a halving of attentional modulation, not its abolition, and does not bear on the formation of top-down modulation.

claims.statement: Mensch et al. expressed tetanus neurotoxin in zebrafish to abrogate synaptic vesicle release in vivo, confirming reduced synaptic activity with electrophysiology and normal gross development. Myelinated axons fell by 39 percent (67 plus or minus 9 control against 41 plus or minus 9) with a matching increase in unmyelinated axons above 0.3 micrometres, while the number, size and distribution of those axons were unchanged. Myelinating oligodendrocytes fell by only 10 percent, whereas myelin sheaths per oligodendrocyte fell by 30 percent (11.9 plus or minus 3.1 against 8.2 plus or minus 2.9) with unchanged sheath length, unchanged retractions and an unchanged period of sheath formation. Chimeras showed the effect is axonal: toxin-expressing oligodendrocytes in a control environment made a normal 12 plus or minus 2.7 sheaths while control oligodendrocytes in a toxin-expressing animal made 8.6 plus or minus 3.3, and toxin in single reticulospinal neurons gave 40 percent fewer sheaths along their own axons. Raising activity with pentylenetetrazole increased sheaths per oligodendrocyte by about 40 percent, an increase entirely eliminated by co-expressing the toxin. This is evidence for Nervous System and Physiological Coordination of Organs to Activity-Dependent Myelination and Conduction Tuning in the arising role: the activity-dependent component of myelination does not form when vesicular release from the nervous system's neurons is blocked, and the effect is produced from the axonal side.
claims.scope: Cause 5.7 > 6.27 (arising): tetanus-toxin block of synaptic vesicle release in zebrafish spinal cord, with genetic chimeras, single-neuron expression and a pentylenetetrazole gain-of-function as controls, measured as myelinated axon counts and sheaths per oligodendrocyte; it shows the dependence of myelination on neuronal vesicular release during the first days of myelination, and does not measure conduction.

Mouse physiology and a Nestin-lineage Bax intervention constrain parts of the route; macaque histology has no matched functional assay. Rat training changes retained birth labels without isolating survival or testing newborn-cell necessity. These findings do not establish general cognitive necessity, unique neuron-count mediation or a causal human memory-preservation mechanism. Earlier autoradiographic nulls likewise do not establish that stable neuron populations are necessary for memory.

entities.description: For a nonzero target displacement, Wang et al. define anticipation index as gaze-to-current-target distance at target onset divided by previous-to-current-target distance. This ratio is not the percentage of anticipatory movements and is not generally bounded above by one.

entities.name: Nucleon valence quantum numbers
entities.description: In the declared strong-interaction nucleon sectors, net flavor means quarks minus antiquarks: proton (N_u,N_d)=(2,1), neutron (1,2), with zero other net flavors. With B=sum_f N_f/3 and Q/e=sum_f q_f*N_f, these labels give B=1 and charges +1 and 0. Adding a same-flavor quark-antiquark pair or gluons preserves these additive labels without preserving total basis-particle count.

entities.name: Fundamental color-singlet tensor
entities.description: For three fundamental SU(3) color indices, the normalized antisymmetric tensor epsilon_abc/sqrt(6) is invariant because U_ai*U_bj*U_ck*epsilon_ijk=det(U)*epsilon_abc and det(U)=1. A nontrivial center element acts as z or z^2 on one or two fundamental factors, excluding a singlet there. Three is therefore a restricted representation-theoretic minimum, not a measured particle population or sufficient formation condition.

entities.name: Coherent vacuum oscillation phase
entities.description: In the coherent ultrarelativistic vacuum approximation with hbar=c=1, A_alpha-to-beta=sum_i U_beta,i exp[-i m_i^2 L/(2E)] U_alpha,i* and P=|A|^2. Antineutrinos replace U by U*. Relative phases use Delta m^2 L/(2E); the effective two-flavor survival probability is 1-sin^2(2 theta) sin^2[Delta m^2 L/(4E)]. A common mass-squared shift changes only a common phase.

entities.name: Reactor antineutrino coincidence readout
entities.description: KamLAND identifies electron-antineutrino candidates through inverse beta decay, antinu_e+p->e-plus+n. The prompt positron kinetic plus annihilation signal is followed by neutron-capture light, normally a 2.2 MeV gamma from hydrogen. The approximate relation E_antineutrino=E_prompt+T_neutron+0.8 MeV uses neutron recoil kinetic energy and a rounded kinematic offset; energy response and delayed-coincidence selection remain explicit.

entities.name: Coherent neutrino propagation in matter
entities.description: For flavor amplitudes f, i*df/dx=H_f(x)*f with H_f=U diag(m_i^2) U-dagger/(2E)+diag(V_e(x),0,0), after removing a common identity term. For neutrinos V_e=sqrt(2)*G_F*n_e(x); for antineutrinos U is complex-conjugated and V_e changes sign. For neutrinos in neutral ordinary matter the active-sector neutral-current contribution is -G_F*n_n(x)/sqrt(2) times the identity and changes only a common phase; its sign also reverses for antineutrinos before removal.

openObligations: Use a closed unitary three-active-neutrino model with standard weak interactions, hbar=c=1 and fixed positive energy in the ultrarelativistic coherent forward-scattering approximation. The prescribed medium is electrically neutral, unpolarized and locally isotropic, with nonrelativistic electrons, protons and neutrons and no appreciable muon/tau population. Incoherent scattering, absorption, neutrino-neutrino refraction, sterile states and nonstandard interactions require different models.

The vector f contains flavor amplitudes, with the already declared U_alpha,i convention. The review writes its basic evolution equation in the vacuum mass basis; multiplication by the constant U gives the stated flavor-basis Hamiltonian. For antineutrinos both U becomes U* and the charged-current potential changes sign. A merely diagonal potential cannot in general be discarded; the neutral-current term is removable here because it is common to all three active flavors.

Vacuum masses, the mixing matrix, energy and the medium density profile are supplied inputs. Matter-dependent eigenvalues are effective propagation parameters, not newly generated vacuum masses. This model does not determine absolute mass, Dirac/Majorana nature, an origin mechanism or a temporal emergence order.

A variable density generally gives noncommuting Hamiltonians at different positions. Its evolution requires the ordered solution with initial conditions; one cannot substitute a single constant-density vacuum phase or assume adiabaticity from an instantaneous mixing angle. No actual solar/Earth profile, scattering experiment, oscillation fit or matter evolution is numerically reproduced here.

entities.name: Instantaneous matter mixing and adiabatic boundary
entities.description: In the declared two-flavor approximation set A=2E*(V_e-V_x) and Delta_m=sqrt[(Delta*cos(2 theta)-A)^2+(Delta*sin(2 theta))^2]. The eigenvalue gap is Delta_m/(2E), with cos(2 theta_m)=(Delta*cos(2 theta)-A)/Delta_m and sin(2 theta_m)=Delta*sin(2 theta)/Delta_m. Nonzero mixing is maximal at A=Delta*cos(2 theta). An instantaneous eigenbasis has the additional connection -i*R-dagger*dR/dx; adiabatic following is an approximation that neglects its inter-state coupling relative to the gap.

entities.name: Conditional transverse two-body mass
entities.description: For two effectively massless physical daughter four-momenta from a two-body decay, define mT^2 = 2 pT1 pT2 (1-cos(deltaPhi)); the exact parent invariant mass then obeys M >= mT. Replacing these quantities by reconstructed electron and missing transverse vectors defines an estimator under a single-invisible-daughter assignment. Response errors can make that estimator exceed the true mass, so the exact inequality is not an eventwise detector guarantee. The transverse recoil is the magnitude of the daughter transverse-vector sum; mT is not a fully reconstructed invariant mass.

entities.name: Single-doublet Higgs background and tree masses
entities.description: Write rho=phi-dagger*phi and V=mu2*rho+(lambda_P^2/2)*rho^2 with mu2<0 and lambda_P>0. In unitary gauge choose phi=(0,(v+H)/sqrt(2)), v^2=-2*mu2/lambda_P^2. The tree-level relations are M_H^2=lambda_P^2*v^2, M_W=g*v/2, M_Z=sqrt(g^2+gprime^2)*v/2 and M_photon=0.

sourceCoordinates.locator: Section 10.1, page 2, Equations 10.1 and 10.3-10.5: declared Higgs-doublet potential, unitary-gauge background and tree-level gauge/scalar masses

openObligations: This is the minimal single-doublet model at tree level with supplied mu2<0, lambda_P>0 and positive gauge couplings, in units hbar=c=1. lambda_P denotes the PDG parameter whose square enters the quartic term; it is not the background lambda_W used in the historical Weinberg1967 convention.

The chosen doublet orientation and unitary-gauge coordinates are model conventions. The scalar background is distinct from the propagating H excitation; would-be Goldstone components supply longitudinal vector polarizations rather than additional physical particles. A gauge choice or scalar minimum is not an independently measured spatial medium, an additional particle population or a causal maintenance process.

The specified classical potential has a nonzero minimum and positive radial curvature. This does not establish absolute stability of the interacting quantum vacuum, a cosmological transition history or continuous physical regeneration. Radiative corrections, renormalization prescription and possible extra fields require separate treatment; these tree-level parameters are not silently equated with fitted resonance masses.
Field assignments, gauge couplings and model parameters are premises of this construction. They do not derive chirality or a general stability/formation law for later composite matter.

entities.name: Charged-fermion mass and Higgs coupling convention
entities.description: For each supplied charged-fermion mass m_i in the declared mass basis, the tree-level term is -m_i*psi-bar_i*psi_i-(m_i/v)*H*psi-bar_i*psi_i. Defining y_i=sqrt(2)*m_i/v gives m_i=y_i*v/sqrt(2) and the one-Higgs coefficient y_i/sqrt(2)=m_i/v. This reparametrizes independent mass/Yukawa inputs; it does not calculate their numerical hierarchy.

entities.name: Weak vector fields and fermion currents
entities.description: In the declared broken-phase Standard Model, W-plus and W-minus are spin-one fields of electric charge +e and -e; Z is neutral and spin one. With J_W^mu=sum_l nu-bar_l*gamma^mu*(1-gamma5)*l+sum_ij u-bar_i*gamma^mu*(1-gamma5)*V_ij*d_j, L_CC=-g/(2*sqrt(2))*(W-plus_mu*J_W^mu+h.c.). The tree neutral term is L_NC=-g/(2*cos(theta_W))*Z_mu*sum_f f-bar*gamma^mu*(gV_f-gA_f*gamma5)*f, where gV_f=T3_f-2*Q_f*sin(theta_W)^2 and gA_f=T3_f; T3_f is the isospin of the left-handed partner. Thus the stated quark charged current contains CKM mixing, while the tree Z current is flavor diagonal in this minimal mass basis.

sourceCoordinates.locator: Section 10.1, pages 1-3, Equations 10.2-10.3 and 10.6-10.7: weak vector-field charges/polarizations, charged and neutral currents and the stated quark mixing basis

Massive vector fields have three physical polarizations in the stated broken-phase description. The absence of a tree-level flavor-changing Z vertex does not exclude loop-induced flavor-changing neutral processes or nonminimal interactions.

W/Z denote unstable resonance species or field excitations in these descriptions, not stable asymptotic carrier units, bounded objects with persistent classical tracks or an observed field-formation sequence. Generic arising or maintenance necessity is not admitted.

entities.name: Low-energy massive weak exchange
entities.description: For the leading scalar denominator of a massive weak propagator, 1/(q^2-M_V^2)=-M_V^(-2)*[1+O(q^2/M_V^2)] when |q^2| is much smaller than M_V^2. With the declared charged-current normalization this yields the tree relation G_F/sqrt(2)=g^2/(8*M_W^2)=1/(2*v^2) for a local four-fermion approximation. Charged and neutral weak amplitudes retain their different currents; the contact description is distinct from a resonant production and decay process.

entities.name: Confinement criteria and their domains
entities.description: Confinement is specified relative to a theory and observable. In an unscreened pure-gauge theory, asymptotic fundamental Wilson-loop area behavior defines a static string-tension criterion. With dynamical quarks, the reviewed Euclidean static-source spectra instead include mixing and screening by color-singlet meson pairs. The QCD interpretation of hadronic final states is a separate phenomenological statement, not an equivalent finite-loop test or a proof that separation energy grows without bound.

openObligations: A criterion must declare the gauge theory, dynamical matter, state or temperature regime, operator, separation/time limits and regulator. Pure-gauge fundamental Wilson-loop area law, screened static-source energies with dynamical quarks and phenomenological color-singlet final states are not interchangeable definitions.

The area-law criterion takes large contours and static-source limits in an unscreened theory. Wilson strong-coupling surfaces and Creutz finite SU(2) loops do not prove continuum SU(3) confinement with physical quark masses. Their finite-volume, finite-loop and extrapolation restrictions remain explicit.

Pair creation in the reviewed dynamical-quark calculations permits color-singlet static-light or static-strange channels. The screened ground-state energy need not grow indefinitely with separation. A metastable string branch, an operator overlap and the true ground state are different quantities; Euclidean mixing energies do not measure real-time hadronization rates.

The selected nonperturbative formulation, including a chosen lattice action and operator basis, is not an observed universal organization stage. The renormalization prescription and scale are not physical elapsed time or a demonstrated temporal maintenance cause. The non-Abelian gluon sector within QCD is not an independently measured universal maintenance arrow.
Classification as a regime-level pattern is descriptive, not a verified universal phase sequence or material carrier.
A universal downward constraint from confinement remains excluded. No intervention, closed effective dynamics or universal generating rule is established by the static-source results.

Electrical fractional-charge bounds constrain a declared material or particle search. Electric charge is not color charge; a null result cannot establish absence of all free colored objects. In particular, the CMS fractional-charge benchmark explicitly uses color-singlet particles.

Color-singlet tensor algebra is a representation constraint, not a dynamical formation proof. Asymptotic freedom concerns ultraviolet running and does not prove the infrared criterion. The high-temperature phase diagram, physical-point continuum completion and a mathematical all-channel confinement theorem are outside this admission.

No universal nuclear or atomic stability follows from the definition or the selected hadron results. Nuclear binding, decay channels and electromagnetic atomic binding require distinct systems and inputs; the existing deuteron beta threshold excludes one specified bare-nucleus breakup channel, not all decays, nuclei or atomic states.

entities.name: Adiabatic solar survival and source averaging
entities.description: For the declared two-flavor solar model, adiabatic propagation to a vacuum endpoint and sufficient relative-phase averaging give P_ee(E,r)=cos^2(theta_m,p)*cos^2(theta)+sin^2(theta_m,p)*sin^2(theta)=[1+cos(2 theta_m,p)*cos(2 theta)]/2, with theta_m,p evaluated at production position r. The averaged survival is <P_ee>_s=integral dE w_s(E) integral d^3r f_s(r|E) P_ee(E,r). For a specified electron-flavor charged-current response, w_s is proportional to the unoscillated differential neutrino number flux dPhi_s/dE at the detector times its cross section and detection efficiency, with any selected-bin response included and the finite nonzero normalization divided out. Here dPhi_s/dE counts neutrinos per unit area, time and neutrino energy; the transported energy flux E*dPhi_s/dE would introduce an extra energy factor and is not the event weight.

For elastic scattering or neutral-current channels, the corresponding flavor-dependent response must be folded explicitly; a single electron-flavor charged-current weight is not a universal event-rate formula.

entities.name: Neutrino oscillation propagation scope
entities.description: In the declared coherent ultrarelativistic vacuum model, flavor-sensitive preparation and readout are related by interference between distinct mass propagation components. Their relative phases change transition probabilities as L/E varies; a probability is not a continuously measured sequence of flavor jumps. Oscillation is a conditional propagation phenomenon, not an additional bounded object or a universal property of every neutrino state.

A single vacuum mass eigenstate acquires only a phase in its internal state; its flavor-readout probabilities |U_alpha,i|^2 do not oscillate. These are not statements that vacuum mass states remain instantaneous eigenstates in arbitrary varying matter, or that packet position is stationary.

Leptonic charged-current flavor labels specify preparation/readout; mass differences and mixing specify model inputs. They do not establish an arising chronology or the claim that flavor identity can never be dynamically autonomous. No causal maintenance or downward constraint is inferred from these definition dependencies.

Within this oscillation model, mass-squared differences constrain differences only. They do not determine the absolute mass scale, require every individual mass to be nonzero, select Dirac versus Majorana character or supply a unique mass-generation extension. Mass origin remains a separate scope.

Continuous weak scattering or repeated projective collapse is not the coherent phase mechanism. A specified source, medium and detector determine which probability or weighted response is appropriate; transport and cosmological claims need additional inputs.

entities.name: Astrophysical and cosmological transport boundary

This graph admits the propagation implication and explicitly excludes quantitative astrophysical transport and cosmological predictions from this reconstruction.

The reported period-averaged survival and historical two-flavor rate-and-shape fit use response and background models; the 180 km display baseline is not a single experimental baseline. Shape-only, KamLAND-only and solar-combined fits are distinct, and the solar combination adds a CPT assumption.

SNO reports a joint electron versus combined muon-plus-tau active-flux inference under its B8-shape and weak-response assumptions. This is not a measured oscillation phase, separate muon/tau identification or unique proof of adiabatic MSW conversion. Subtracting channel-flux centers does not reproduce its covariance, joint result or significance; the SK-added and shape-relaxed analyses remain separate.

Super-Kamiokande uses atmospheric flux, zenith distributions and detector/kinematic proxies with a historical two-flavor fit. The 1998 disappearance analysis does not directly identify tau appearance or distinguish its tau interpretation from the stated sterile alternative. Its L/E cross-check reuses the sample and does not resolve an oscillation dip.

OPERA reconstructs tau candidates in a primarily muon-neutrino beam using channel-dependent efficiencies and backgrounds. Its calibrated channel-combination significance, signal strength and full-mixing mass-squared compatibility reuse the same candidate sample. Dividing five candidates by an interaction total does not produce an oscillation probability, and the Fisher-product statistic is not the calibrated tail probability.

Historical effective two-flavor parameters, confidence constructions and adopted external inputs retain their publication-specific meanings; no current three-flavor global fit is inferred. These results do not establish absolute neutrino masses, every individual mass to be nonzero, Dirac/Majorana character, a unique mass-generation mechanism or quantitative astrophysical/cosmological transport.

entities.name: Static-source plaquette density contrast
entities.description:
For a smeared traced Wilson source W(R,T) and an unsmeared normalized plaquette P_mu_nu=(1/2)Tr[ordered elementary plaquette link product], define C_mu_nu=/-

. The reference is the vacuum plaquette expectation. In the large-T projection and leading plaquette matching, E_R,i=(2 beta/a^4) C_i4 and B_R,i=-(2 beta/a^4) C_jk, with |epsilon_ijk|=1. These denote differences of color-contracted squared components between the static-source ground state and vacuum. Sum spatial components to define energy contrast epsilon_R=(E_R+B_R)/2 and action contrast sigma_R=(E_R-B_R)/2.

openObligations: This record synthesizes the reported primary numerical analysis and its methodological conclusion. It is neither a new measured energy nor an independent simulation; the two preprints describe the same work and are not pooled confirmations.

A negative finite-volume energy shift relative to two nucleons is not by itself an infinite-volume bound-state determination. Residual/gap intervals can contain an eigenvalue without establishing its ground-state index or excluding additional levels outside the interval. The source tables distinguish statistical confidence from assumption-dependent spectral windows.

The asymmetric-correlator diagnostics show changing left/right state overlaps over accessible Euclidean times. They question the eigenstate interpretation of apparently stable estimators without proving that every such energy estimate is wrong or that a bound state cannot exist.

The reported synthetic small-gap examples use chosen spectra, overlaps and a noise model related to the lattice data. Their statistically similar bound/scattering outputs illustrate an inverse-problem ambiguity; they are not additional QCD measurements or a unique reconstruction of the true spectrum.

Neither the single-volume 2026 analysis nor the conditional 2013 interpretation establishes continuum physical-mass nuclear binding, all nuclei, atomic binding, a real-time formation rate or permanent matter stability.

openObligations: A renormalized quark mass needs a prescription and scale. The new flavor-symmetric calculation specifies one action-dependent bare mass; it does not determine an MSbar mass or its response derivative. Flavor SU(3), with degenerate up, down and strange masses, is distinct from the SU(3) color gauge symmetry of QCD.

Controlled quark-mass sensitivity requires a defined input variation or derivative and a declaration of what is held fixed, including the gauge coupling or QCD scale, cutoff, strange/sea masses and unit calibration. A comparison with physical nuclear data alone is not such a controlled calculation. An input hadron mass used to set the scale cannot simultaneously count as an independent prediction.

Hadron masses, nuclear binding differences, bulk density, compressibility and astrophysical matter are different observables. No reviewed many-body equation of state, composition, thermodynamic state, pressure response or astrophysical inference is supplied here. Direct quark-to-density/compressibility edges and a demonstrated uninterrupted chain to macroscopic materials are excluded, without asserting that the underlying physical influence is zero.

A later material model must declare how it treats electromagnetic, electronic and environmental inputs as well as its nuclear interactions and calibration. Neither a QCD-only two-nucleon spectrum nor a hadron mass table specifies atomic bonding, material phase or mechanical response.

The quark and nucleon inputs supply field/parameter and nucleon concepts, not experimentally established arising or maintenance interventions. Color, flavor, baryon number and sample count are distinct quantities.

entities.name: Canonical scalar cosmological background
entities.description: In hbar=c=1 units with signature (+---) and the curvature convention of Mukhanov Equation 1, take S=integral d^4x sqrt(-g)[-M_pl^2 R_4/2 + g^{mu nu} partial_mu phi partial_nu phi/2 - V(phi)], with reduced M_pl^2=(8 pi G)^(-1). The spatially flat background is ds^2=dt^2-a(t)^2 dx^2, dt=a d_eta. For homogeneous phi(t), H=dot(a)/a obeys 3 M_pl^2 H^2=dot(phi)^2/2+V, dot(H)=-dot(phi)^2/(2 M_pl^2), and ddot(phi)+3H dot(phi)+V_,phi=0. For H>0, epsilon_H=-dot(H)/H^2; epsilon_H<1 defines accelerated expansion and a decreasing comoving Hubble radius (aH)^(-1).

entities.name: Canonical gauge-invariant curvature mode
entities.description: For scalar perturbations with spatial metric g_ij=-a^2[(1-2psi)delta_ij+2 partial_i partial_j E], define Hcal=a'/a=aH, Q=delta(phi)+(phi'/Hcal)psi, v=aQ, z=a phi'/Hcal=a dot(phi)/H, and R=psi+Hcal delta(phi)/phi'=v/z. Primes denote conformal-time derivatives. On an interval with H and dot(phi) nonzero, eliminating the linear lapse/shift constraints gives S2=(1/2)integral d_eta d^3x[(v')^2-(grad v)^2+(z''/z)v^2], up to boundary terms. A Fourier mode satisfies u_k''+[k^2-z''/z]u_k=0; its canonical momentum is pi_v=v'.

entities.name: Conditional primordial curvature spectrum
entities.description: Choose vhat(eta,x)=integral d^3k/(2pi)^3 [a_k u_k(eta) exp(i k.x)+h.c.], [a_k,a_q^dagger]=(2pi)^3 delta^3(k-q), a_k|0>=0, and u_k u_k*'-u_k* u_k'=i. In an early adiabatic regime with omega_k^2=k^2-z''/z>0, |omega_k'/omega_k^2|<<1 and k^2>>|z''/z|, choose u_k approximately exp(-ik eta)/sqrt(2k). With R(x)=integral d^3k/(2pi)^3 R_k exp(i k.x), define <R_k R_q>=(2pi)^3 delta^3(k+q)(2pi^2/k^3) P_R(k), so P_R=k^3|u_k/z|^2/(2pi^2). For the selected initial state and a slow-roll attractor with epsilon_H<<1 and |dot(epsilon_H)/(H epsilon_H)|<<1, the late growing-mode power is approximately [H^2/(8pi^2 epsilon_H M_pl^2)] evaluated at k=aH.

entities.name: Conditional long-wavelength curvature evolution
entities.description: Substituting v=zR in the canonical mode equation gives (z^2 R_k')'+k^2 z^2 R_k=0. At k=0 its two solutions are R=C1+C2 integral d_eta/z^2. For finite modes whose gradient term is negligible, this is a long-wavelength approximation on the regular single-field interval. R is approximately conserved only when the second contribution and gradient corrections are negligible. An attractor with a decaying second solution admits that limit; single-field dynamics or k/(aH)<<1 alone does not select it.

entities.name: Equal-time Gaussian cosmological-mode statistics
entities.description: For the reviewed free real massless scalar on prescribed spatially flat FRW, set y=a phi and p=y'- (a'/a)y. Quadratic evolution of the supplied Gaussian vacuum preserves a Gaussian state. For one discrete nonzero Fourier pair k,-k, its independent complex amplitude y=y1+i y2 has equal-time density P(y1,y2)=exp[-|y|^2/|f_k|^2]/(pi |f_k|^2), with mean zero and <|y|^2>=|f_k|^2. This represents the commuting equal-time field-amplitude statistics; it does not by itself determine a classical trajectory or establish a quantum origin from an observed power spectrum.

entities.name: Dominant-mode stochastic classical approximation
entities.description: In the reviewed large-squeezing, dominant-mode regime, neglect the subleading decaying solution and choose a time-independent phase so the retained f_k is real. The field can then be represented as y(k,eta) approximately f_k(eta)e(k), with time-independent Gaussian e, <e(k)e*(k')>=delta^3(k-k') and e(-k)=e*(k). Where |f_k|>0, with F=Im(conj(f_k) g_k) and g_k=i[f_k'-(a'/a)f_k], the limiting phase-space distribution is concentrated near p=(F/|f_k|^2)y. Random amplitudes then follow the specified classical mode evolution; this stronger approximation requires more than the equal-time Gaussian marginal.

The source describes omitting the tiny decaying component as phase-space coarse graining that smooths the narrow momentum combination while retaining the leading amplitude. A claim about environment-induced decoherence requires an interaction, subsystem and coarse-graining prescription. Small environmental effects need not appreciably change the dominant amplitude, but no universal environmental channel, rate or entropy is supplied here; entropy can depend on the omitted component.

The paired-mode correlations and the persistence of a dominant solution are not a stable population of virtual particles. Gaussianity, a quasi-isotropic mode or a compatible observed spectrum alone does not uniquely demonstrate the assumed initial vacuum or quantum origin. No CMB likelihood, cosmological parameter estimate or universal cross-scale formation law is certified by these definitions.

entities.name: Planck base-model primordial inference
entities.description: The selected analysis assumes spatially flat base LambdaCDM with purely adiabatic scalar P_R(k)=A_s*(k/k_*)^(n_s-1), k_*=0.05 Mpc^-1. CAMB (August 2017) maps this prescribed initial spectrum and the adopted background, matter and thermal history to lensed CMB spectra; CosmoMC (July 2018) samples the six-parameter posterior. The base parameters are baryon and cold-dark-matter densities, theta_MC, tau, ln(10^10 A_s) and n_s, with flat base priors; the amplitude prior is 1.61 < ln(10^10 A_s) < 3.91. The adopted neutrino model has two massless states and one 0.06 eV state, BBN-predicted helium and the stated tanh reionization history. The likelihood multiplies Commander low-T, SimAll low-E and high-multipole Plik, exploring the allowed nuisance parameters jointly.

entities.name: Three-active-neutrino mixing parameterization
entities.description: In a supplied closed unitary three-active-neutrino model, define U=R23 R13(delta) R12 P. Each real ij rotation acts on its plane with block [[cij,sij],[-sij,cij]] and as identity on the remaining direction, with cij=cos(thetaij) and sij=sin(thetaij); the 1-3 block is [[c13,s13 exp(-i delta)],[-s13 exp(i delta),c13]]. For generic three-mass mixing, charged-lepton and Dirac-neutrino rephasings leave three angles and one Dirac phase, with P=I. In the Majorana alternative use P=diag(exp(i eta1),exp(i eta2),1); these two extra column phases cancel from ordinary mass-induced flavor-oscillation probabilities.

entities.name: Oscillation mass identifiability
entities.description: In the leading coherent ultrarelativistic vacuum model with hbar=c=1, hold U, L and E fixed. Replacing every m_i^2 by m_i^2+kappa multiplies A_alpha-to-beta by exp[-i kappa L/(2E)], leaving P=|A|^2 unchanged. This holds for shifts preserving m_i^2+kappa>=0 and (m_i^2+kappa)/E^2<<1. For three nonnegative squared masses, Delta21=m_2^2-m_1^2 and Delta31=m_3^2-m_1^2 both nonzero and unequal imply three pairwise distinct values; at most one can be zero, so at least two masses are nonzero.

entities.name: Declared Standard Model sector decomposition
entities.description: Adopt the local gauge algebra su(3)c plus su(2)L plus u(1)Y, conventionally written SU(3)c x SU(2)L x U(1)Y, with Q=T3+Y. For each of three generations, the pre-Higgs-background chiral assignments are Q_L=(u_L,dprime_L)~(3,2,1/6), u_R~(3,1,2/3), d_R~(3,1,-1/3), L_L=(nu_L,l_L)~(1,2,-1/2) and l_R~(1,1,-1). The single complex Higgs scalar is phi~(1,2,1/2). Each tuple gives the color representation, weak representation and declared hypercharge: 3 means the color fundamental, 2 the weak doublet and 1 a singlet. The gauge potentials are G_mu^a (a=1,...,8), W_mu^i (i=1,2,3) and B_mu, with couplings gs, g and gprime. This is a chosen interacting field specification; the scalar is a boson without being a gauge vector mediator.

Right-handed entries denote right-handed fermion fields, not their left-handed charge conjugates; dprime is a weak-interaction basis component.

Choose D_mu=partial_mu+i*gs*t^a*G_mu^a+i*g*T^i*W_mu^i+i*gprime*Y*B_mu, with generators in the representation of the field and zero action for a trivial factor. The 8+3+1 vector-potential species count follows from the chosen generator dimensions; it is neither a total physical-polarization count nor an observed particle population. With a supplied single-doublet background in the usual unitary-gauge tree convention, thetaW=arctan(gprime/g), A_mu=B_mu*cos(thetaW)+W_mu^3*sin(thetaW), Z_mu=-B_mu*sin(thetaW)+W_mu^3*cos(thetaW), and W_mu^plus/minus=(W_mu^1 minus/plus i*W_mu^2)/sqrt(2). This minimal renormalizable field content contains no nu_R. The local algebra, representations, chirality, three-generation repetition and coupling parameters are adopted model premises. entities.description: In the specified free Maxwell theory, fix an inertial frame, hbar=c=1 and nonzero momentum p. Its complex polarization vector is e(p)=E(p)c(p), so p dot e=0 and e_dagger e=1. Here e is a polarization amplitude, not the mean electric field, which vanishes in this one-photon number state. A passive real O(p) in SO(2) gives E'=E O, c'=O^T c and f'=O^T f in the transformed mode convention; transforming creation operators consistently preserves e and the one-photon state. An active polarization comparison instead fixes the basis and apparatus while varying relative coefficients. Both transverse modes have the same free frequency |p|; this model supplies no polarization-dependent propagation splitting or preferred vacuum axis.

entities.name: Specified primordial nuclear reaction network
entities.description: In the selected homogeneous hot-expanding model, weak neutron/proton interconversion, expansion and thermodynamics set a reaction history for free nucleons and light nuclei. Abundances may be expressed per baryon as Y_i=n_i/n_b; a nuclear species balance has dilution dn_i/dt+3*H*n_i and a sum of reaction production and destruction terms. The deuterium photodissociation bottleneck delays effective light-nucleus assembly; nuclear reactions then produce deuterium, helium-3 and helium-4 and mass-seven species including beryllium-7, which later feeds lithium-7. These model equations require a supplied cosmological background, baryon density, weak rates, neutron lifetime and thermonuclear cross sections.

entities.name: Constrained bulk equilibrium, coexistence and phase-rule conditions
entities.description: In the selected hydrostatic bulk thermodynamic framework, equilibrium criteria use allowed variations under explicit constraints: entropy is maximal at fixed total energy, or energy is minimal at fixed entropy. Write A=U-T*S and G=U-T*S+p*V; the relevant potential and stability comparison depend on what is held fixed. For phases in freely exchanging contact without gravity, electrical effects, solid distortion or capillary tension, equilibrium requires equal temperature, pressure and the potential of each freely exchangeable independently variable component. In this setting the intensive degrees of freedom obey f=C+2-N_ph, where C counts independent components and N_ph counts coexisting phases, not specimens.

entities.name: State- and boundary-specific piezoelectric tensor convention
entities.description: For the declared isothermal uniform bulk linear response, the proper piezoelectric stress tensor is e_ijk=(partial D_i/partial strain_jk) at fixed E,T, equivalently -(partial stress_jk/partial E_i) at fixed strain,T. Its SI units are C/m^2. The piezoelectric strain tensor d relates strain to electric field at fixed stress,T or displacement D to stress at fixed E,T, with units m/V, equivalently C/N. Converting between e and d requires elastic compliance and matching tensor/shear conventions; they are not interchangeable numerical coefficients.

Momentum is still transferred to the bound body; its whole-body translational recoil energy is negligibly small on the stated spectral scale. This zero-phonon channel is a fraction of events, not absence of binding vibrations, zero momentum transfer or a rule that every emitted gamma ray is resonant.

entities.name: Declared linear homogeneous optical-propagation model
entities.description: In the selected homogeneous isotropic linear medium, use the convention E(z,t)=Re[E0(omega)*exp(i*k(omega)*z-i*omega*t)] with k(omega)=omega*sqrt(epsilon(omega)*mu(omega)) in absolute SI constitutive units. Writing k=k_real+i*k_imag gives amplitude attenuation exp(-k_imag*z) and phase accumulation k_real*z. For the passive forward branch, k_imag>=0; the corresponding fixed-medium intensity attenuation coefficient is alpha_int=2*k_imag in m^-1. Nonlinear real propagation phase across a pulse bandwidth can produce dispersive waveform deformation, whereas a real phase linear in frequency supplies a delay. A wave number proportional to frequency at fixed speed is not by itself dispersive deformation. These phase effects are distinct from imaginary-part attenuation.

The harmonic convention is exp(i*k*z-i*omega*t). With the passive forward branch Im(k)>=0, amplitude decays as exp(-Im(k)*z), while intensity has the factor 2 in its exponent. The absolute SI epsilon and mu in k=omega*sqrt(epsilon*mu) are not unqualified relative constants.

entities.description: Engineer N-end-rule-tagged E. coli DHFR/cpLys38, selected C-terminally tagged cpLys38, lysine-less unstructured-tail additions, terminal His6 and linear Ub4 variants as defined in Figures 2-5. cpLys38 joins the old termini with six glycines and starts at former Lys38/ends at Asn37. The source interprets these conditions through aggregation prevention. Its broad passive-cage conclusion is retained as conditional, not a proof that all chaperonins are passive or that no client can experience an active conformational effect.

Figure 1B compares refolding Rubisco plus BSA with native Rubisco plus BSA and BSA alone in solution; it does not directly measure a matched light-scattering reduction inside GroEL/SR1.

Figure 1 C source inference permits reversible intermediate-sized association plus growth of persistent void-volume material. The data do not show that every aggregate dissolves or that all solution aggregation is reversible.

Original folding assistance and aggregation management are qualified to the declared activity/proxy readouts. entities.name: Supercooled BPTI water-relaxation context
entities.description: The source primary MRD sample is 8.3 mM BPTI in water containing 52 percent 2H and 17 percent 17O at pH* 5.2, dispersed as aqueous droplets in heptane/nonionic-surfactant emulsion. Fits exclude the highest-frequency point as described; no new fit is performed here.

openObligations: Long-Evans rat hippocampus is bulk tissue containing neurons and glia. High/low licking-grooming and arched-back nursing groups are selected extremes of continuous maternal behavior, not universal biological classes.

Cross-fostering changes a postnatal care environment. It does not isolate licking from nursing, nutrition or other maternal effects, directly manipulate an abstract neural state, or establish germline inheritance. Same-class foster controls are other mothers, not untouched biological-mother controls.

General adult-age statements conflict with assay-specific 90-day descriptions. ChIP figures report four animals/group but supplementary fixed-tissue methods specify six. GR protein Figure 5a reports five but Western methods specify six. Clones and technical blot replicates are not independent animals; litter dependence remains relevant.

Exon 1_7 is an alternative first exon of the rat glucocorticoid receptor gene. CpG site 16 at the 5-prime end of the NGFI-A binding region and site 17 at its 3-prime end have different outcomes. Bisulfite cytosine readouts, acetyl-H3K9-associated ChIP, NGFI-A ChIP, GR protein and plasma corticosterone are separate observables.

TSA infusion is a broad pharmacological intervention, not a locus-specific methylation edit or cell-specific neural manipulation. The restraint-stress cohort is separate from the GR-protein cohort. Parallel effects do not identify their causal mediation order.

The published Figure 2-associated t/P pairs (2.1/P<0.001 and 3.1/P<0.0001) are inconsistent with ordinary t tests; exact uncertainty is not reproduced. The 27 July 2004 publisher correction fixes labels, corticosterone units to micrograms/dL and bisulfite PCR annealing to 56 degrees C; the supplement retains conflicting text.

Individual animal source values and clone sequences are unavailable in the reviewed materials. Published findings are not an independent reproduction, and nonsignificant contrasts are not equivalence tests.

Methylation, histone-associated ChIP, factor-associated ChIP, protein immunoreactivity and endocrine responses are different observables. Cross-fostering and broad TSA perturbations do not isolate a unique causal histone/methylation mediator or universal histone code.

Cross-sectional developmental cohorts and adult observations do not establish mitotic or transgenerational chromatin inheritance, continuous persistence in the same cell, lineage stabilization, universal contextual memory or long-range coordinated regulation.

No genome-wide sequence comparison proves absence of all sequence variation. The epigenetic interpretation is bounded by the actual locus assays and environmental/drug contrasts, rather than universal sequence-independent regulation of replication and transcription.

Replication/transcription, protein cooperativity, signalling and hydrogen-bond studies are separate scopes. They are not jointly measured necessary mediators or calibrated contributions to the selected hippocampal outcomes.

openObligations: Adult male 8-10-week C57BL/6-background mice; rapidly dissected bulk dentate gyri enriched in neurons, not purified neurons or single-cell measurements. ECS is induced synchronous activation, not an explicit learning task or a measured sustained cognitive state.

ATAC-seq and RNA-seq use independent samples. GEO GSE82015 lists four wild-type ATAC replicates at E0/E1/E4 and two sh-cFos E1 ATAC replicates; other AAV ATAC groups and RNA groups have three. GSE86367 lists three E24 ATAC and three RNA samples. Replicate labels do not independently verify animal identity or sample independence.

c-Fos knockdown uses one shRNA and overexpression uses AAV2/9 one week before assay. No reviewed rescue with a second sequence excludes all off-target effects. External KCl-neuron ChIP-seq annotations are not matched in vivo c-Fos occupancy measurements.

A 1/4/24-hour comparison across sacrificed cohorts does not demonstrate persistence in the same cell, lifelong memory, inheritance or a universal minimal assembly. RNA abundance is distinct from transcription rate, protein output and behavioral function.

Figure 6c has a 144/114 gene-count conflict. Figure 7c caption says E0/E4/E24, while plot and experimental text specify E0/E1/E4. Supplementary Tables 4-5 contain conflicting headers, nonfinite values or spreadsheet errors. No global quantitative model is calibrated from these data.

The main Methods report no sample-size predetermination, randomization or blinding. Some qPCR primer labels/sequences conflict. Published findings, metadata inspection and source-cell counts are not independent biological replication or sequencing-pipeline reproduction.

Approximately three-month-old male Arc-CreERT2/R26R-eYFP mice on a C57BL/6J background. Training includes a tone paired with footshock in a context; the changed-context comparison alters several environmental cues. It is not a context-only learning protocol or an isolated chromatin intervention.

Basal denotes NeuN+/eYFP- nuclei collected after training, not naive home-cage animals. Early denotes NeuN+/eYFP+ at 1.5-2 hours, Late the tagged population at five days without recall, and Reactivated NeuN+/eYFP+/Arc+ after re-exposure in a different cohort. Marker selection, reporter maturation and a roughly 12-hour labeling window limit cell identity and temporal specificity.

Whole-hippocampus molecular samples pool nuclei across animals and neuronal subtypes. ATAC Methods specify 10,000 nuclei from 8-10 mice per replicate. Table 13 lists three Basal and four Late libraries, while the reporting summary excludes one Basal from 13 and Figure 2a states n=3 per group. The included-library mapping remains unresolved. A library, genomic locus, slice or punctum is not an independent animal. Destructive cohorts are not single-cell longitudinal measurements.

Figure 1f counts are labeled cells per DG slice; the caption refers to hippocampus. Its five versus six mice each contribute six sections, while tests report df=59/57. Extended Data 1e gives n=15 with df=14 without a clear per-group denominator; 1c has n=30 with df=16. Animal-level effects and confidence intervals require source measurements and sample reconciliation.

Hi-C Methods describe two libraries per Basal, Early and Late population, but the reporting summary excludes one Early library. Methods say two animals per sample, whereas reporting specifies four to five. Promoter-capture Hi-C covers four populations and selected promoters. Contact frequencies and inferred A/B compartments are not unique three-dimensional coordinates. Figure 3 specifies a 500-kb Juicer representation, while Methods and software use 50-kb HOMER compartment PCA; their mapping needs explicit reconstruction.

ATAC Figure 2a labels log2 fold-change thresholds, while its caption, Methods and software say fold changes >1.5. RNA Table 8 has undocumented sign reorientation and a near-threshold extra row. The RNA Methods cite an edgeR reference for DESeq2 and the software omits the RNA export code. No sequence analysis, signed gene-specific pathway or edge weight is calibrated.

eIF4E and GRIA1 puncta measure protein immunoreactivity, not translation rate, receptor current or synaptic efficacy. The Results/caption call the measured shaft dendritic, but Figure 5f labels an axon and Methods describe axon surfaces; exact compartment identity and distance units require clarification. Sections and neurites are nested within mice.

Reported group randomization and selected blinded quantification do not resolve all sampling issues. Sequencing sample sizes used observed variability and group differences; ATAC/Hi-C quality exclusions and a plotted ATAC outlier exclusion were not pre-established. Normality was assumed without formal testing. Null tests are not equivalence tests. Separate molecular profiles and behavioral outcomes do not establish a chromatin-to-memory mediation chain or lifelong persistence.

Accessibility and contact-frequency profiles are not direct chromatin-density, unique three-dimensional packing, mechanical force or molecular remodeling trajectories. RNA abundance is not a transcription rate or a direct replication/repair-permissibility measurement.

Separate profiles and populations do not establish that packing causes the expression differences. c-Fos perturbation has multiple possible routes; matching ATAC/RNA effects does not uniquely identify accessibility as their mediator.

Population-level region overlap through sampled windows is not an inherited state, a persistent same-cell trajectory, a universal physical sequence-to-functional-resource transformation or complete spatial control of genomic function.

Epigenetic regulation, nucleic-acid copying, hydrogen bonding and signal pathways are separate scopes. A named chromatin role does not make them necessary causal ancestors or substitute for a matched packaging intervention.

A 1/4/24-hour comparison across sacrificed cohorts does not demonstrate persistence in the same cell, lifelong memory, inheritance or a universal minimal assembly. RNA abundance is distinct from transcription rate, protein output and behavioral function.

Figure 6c has a 144/114 gene-count conflict. Figure 7c caption says E0/E4/E24, while plot and experimental text specify E0/E1/E4. Supplementary Tables 4-5 contain conflicting headers, nonfinite values or spreadsheet errors. No global quantitative model is calibrated from these data.

The main Methods report no sample-size predetermination, randomization or blinding. Some qPCR primer labels/sequences conflict. Published findings, metadata inspection and source-cell counts are not independent biological replication or sequencing-pipeline reproduction.

Approximately three-month-old male Arc-CreERT2/R26R-eYFP mice on a C57BL/6J background. Training includes a tone paired with footshock in a context; the changed-context comparison alters several environmental cues. It is not a context-only learning protocol or an isolated chromatin intervention.

Basal denotes NeuN+/eYFP- nuclei collected after training, not naive home-cage animals. Early denotes NeuN+/eYFP+ at 1.5-2 hours, Late the tagged population at five days without recall, and Reactivated NeuN+/eYFP+/Arc+ after re-exposure in a different cohort. Extended Data 1e gives n=15 with df=14 without a clear per-group denominator; 1c has n=30 with df=16. The source tests folded and methotrexate-stabilized proteins. The assays do not establish that only misfolded proteins are degraded, that native proteins are excluded, or that the proteasome itself decides whether a client is damaged.

No raw autoradiograms, numerical rate fit, binding constant, precise substrate concentration or kinetic uncertainty is reconstructed. Exact engineered tail amino-acid sequences are not printed in the reviewed main Methods, and no universal 20-residue minimum is admitted from data-not-shown observations.

Similar source ubiquitination kinetics for full versus shortened N-end-rule tags constrain reduced tagging as the explanation for the deletion effect. They do not prove equal proteasome-binding occupancy or exact chain topology.

The selected positive scope is accumulating source-assigned ubiquitinated substrate bands under blocked deubiquitination/degradation. Similar net accumulation in two linker constructs is not an isolated ligation rate, exact attachment-site map or proof of identical chain topology.

The genetically encoded linear Ub4 fusion is not a measured post-translational isopeptide-attachment event. Tagging, initiation and degradation have distinct preparations and readouts; no universal modification-to-function causal effect is isolated.

Phosphorylation, acetylation, methylation and glycosylation are not additional reviewed experiments in this scope. No universal timing after completed synthesis, fast reversibility, combinatorial signalling code or regulated network reprogramming is demonstrated.

Cooperativity, enzyme complexes and translation are not measured formation events or universally necessary prerequisites of this supplied-substrate assay. The separate retinal signalling scope does not provide a matched modification pathway.

A reconstructed prevalent/averaged conformation does not prove every particle has an identical genome arrangement or establish the assembly order, folding trajectory, historical origin or free-energy minimum.

The asymmetric contact distribution motivated possible assembly models in the source. Figure 2c is a proposed model; neither its stages nor a two-step pathway were directly measured by this static structural experiment.

The source comparisons to prior maps, model fits and RNA predictions are not separately acquired primary experiments here. Raw particles, deposited maps, supplements and complete resolution uncertainty were not independently reanalyzed.
The admitted observations concern MS2 bacteriophage. Other viral systems require separate evidence.

The three preparations are separate publications and separate contexts. Cell-free assembly dynamics, a reconstructed mature-particle structure and isolated-receptor association cannot be silently joined into one measured lifecycle.

No selected observation establishes proteolytic maturation, acquisition of infectious competence, complete genome delivery across a cellular boundary, productive intracellular replication, propagation or host-expression reprogramming.

A protein named maturation protein is a component label, not observation of the maturation process. A completed capsid or genome-containing structure is not a measured assembly trajectory; an optical assembly trajectory is not an infectious-competence assay.

No physical-instance admission is made. Structural stoichiometry, specimen count or image-particle count is not an emergence minimum or carrier-equivalence rule.
