entities.name: Ddx4 thermal demixing context
entities.description: Source Figure 3D supplied purified Ddx4N1 N-terminal disordered protein (residues 1-236), 202 micromolar, 200 mM NaCl, pH 8. The same source sample is imaged through cooling from 50 to 22 degrees C and reheating, with repeated cycles. The figure demonstration uses 4 degrees C/min; the separate SI cloud-point sampling defaults to 2 degrees C/min. Retain onset/disappearance hysteresis and operational image/turbidity detection; no universal equilibrium transition is inferred.

sourceCoordinates.locator: Published pages 938-940, Figure 3A-D and Results Ddx4 Disordered Regions Reversibly Form Structures In Vitro; Supplemental Figure S4 page 5 and Section S6 pages 21-25: construct distinction, thermal demixing, image-variance transition detection and conditional phase-diagram model

Published pages 936-947, complete primary main text, all seven figures/captions and main Experimental Procedures/References: prepared constructs, cellular versus in vitro scope, hypotheses and limits of generalization

openObligations: Read the complete published primary article pages 936-947, complete PMC main HTML and all seven main figures/captions. The author-lab PDF has a graphical cover plus twelve published pages. Read selected actual 29-page publisher supplement: title page, Figure S4 page 5, Figure S7 pages 10-11, Section S2 relevant in vitro/FRAP pages 14-16, Section S6 pages 21-25, and Section S8 pages 27-28. Other SI preparation/statistical/genome-analysis pages, full sequence details, raw data and movies were not completely read.

Ddx4N1 is the supplied isolated disordered N-terminal region (residues 1-236), without the central DEAD-box helicase. Ddx4YFP replaces that helicase with YFP, and cellular/full-length constructs differ. In vitro terminal-region phase separation is not a demonstration of native germ-granule function, helicase catalysis or a universal folded-protein prerequisite.

Thermal Figure 3D reports 202 micromolar Ddx4N1, 200 mM NaCl and pH 8, with cooling/heating and same-sample repeats. Its 4 degrees C/min demonstration differs from the 2 degrees C/min default cloud-point sampling in SI Section S6. Cooling appearance and reheating disappearance differ; an operational image/turbidity threshold is not independently established equilibrium criticality or a universal minimum molecule count.

Cloud-point data and Flory-Huggins/screened-Coulomb fits are separate from direct images. Assumptions about polymer volume fraction, water, effective interaction constants and electrostatic screening underlie fitted enthalpy/entropy, charge spacing and dielectric values. No new direct molecular force, solvent structure, dielectric or calorimetric measurement is admitted.

FRAP main Figure 3C describes a 60:1 Ddx4N1:Ddx4YFP mixture; SI pages 15-16 instead list pre-dilution concentrations 292.5 micromolar Ddx4N1 and 8.1 micromolar each YFP construct and free CFP, with hanging-drop equilibration. No exact common composition or ratio is silently selected. The qualitative recovery trace is admitted, with no new precise diffusion coefficient.

FRAP recovery depends on bleach geometry, imaging, diffusion/exchange assumptions and the fluorescent tracer. It supports mobility in the reported droplet preparation, not all constituent dynamics, DNA transport kinetics, viscosity, universal liquid character or proof that every condensate/coacervate has the same mechanism.

The partition experiment uses source-defined 32-base single-stranded or 32-base-paired double-stranded fluorescent DNA at equal nominal fluorophore concentration in a separate Ddx4N1 preparation. Background-subtracted emission per region volume is a concentration/partition proxy; equal quantum yield/dye behavior across phases and free-energy calibration are not independently verified.

The source defines its partition coefficient as outside/inside, not the inverse. The main Results paragraph names atto657N whereas Figure 7 and Experimental Procedures name Atto647N. No numerical partition/free-energy value, unlabeled-DNA binding constant, universal sequence specificity or corrected dye identity is independently admitted.

Ten inside/ten outside regions in each of three fields of view are sampling regions, not automatically sixty independent preparation replications. SD of emission regions and model-fit SE are different uncertainties. No independent replication or raw-image replay is performed.

Cellular cold/osmotic response, methylated/splice/charge/aromatic variants and genome enrichment were read but are not new admitted assay contexts. Cellular osmotic changes alter volume/concentration and environment together; sequence/general-mechanism hypotheses do not become universal proof for all condensates.

The admitted thermal, FRAP and DNA-partition contexts do not directly resolve fusion or fission dynamics, transfer/exchange rates for every component or one unique intermolecular/solvent mechanism. No direct catalytic reaction modulation, metabolic throughput/benefit, universal reaction sequestration, membrane-like selectivity, gradient maintenance, prebiotic coacervate ancestry or origin-of-life event is measured in the admitted contexts.
Source fits, calibration and raw measurements are not independently reconstructed or reproduced.

openObligations: Read the complete actual primary main article pages 153-165 and complete PMC HTML, all seven figures, all three tables, Methods/References, plus the complete six-page publisher Supporting Information with all four figures and procedures. The university PDF adds a repository cover. Primary supplement identity is verified by ACS figshare DOI 10.1021/acssynbio.7b00265.s001 and file 9445870; original PMC files were unread HTML challenges.

This reconstitution supplies purified mature enzymes and pre-existing phospholipid liposomes; enzymes and substrates are added externally. The source explicitly says this pathway does not support de novo membrane synthesis because PlsB and other components require existing phospholipids/membranes. No first membrane, protein biosynthesis origin, self-reproducing cell or self-made enzyme complement is established.

The selected chemistry context is the three-enzyme PA time course in SI Figure S3. It is distinct from the full eight-enzyme headgroup pathway and the PE/PG endpoint/calibration assays. SI specifies different PlsB/ATP concentrations for that time course than the general main PA procedure; these are retained as different preparations, not silently pooled.

LC-MS records internal-standard-normalized ion counts and source-assigned lipid identities. Species-dependent response, extraction recovery, peak integration and external calibration govern concentration/yield inference. The main text refers to PE/PG standards in Supporting Information, but the retrieved six-page supplement contains no explicit PE/PG calibration curve; no independent absolute-yield or uncertainty reconstruction is made.

Limiting-CoA conversion supports source-specific cofactor recycling, with supplied ATP and substrates. It does not close energy/resource supply, synthesize fatty-acid chains from carbon feedstock, make every phospholipid or show indefinite throughput. Small PA signal without PlsC is source-attributed to possible PlsC contamination of PlsB; omission effects are not treated as perfectly pure single-enzyme controls.

R18 self-quenching is a membrane dye-dilution proxy. In Figure 6 the immediate fluorescence increase follows oleic-acid addition and does not require phospholipid biosynthesis; subsequent PA conversion adds little further fluorescence change. Thus the signal alone cannot isolate synthesis-driven area growth from fatty-acid partition, swelling, fusion or dye redistribution.

The source reports an approximate 25-30 percent expansion from R18 assumptions. No new exact area/volume expansion, vesicle number, leaflet distribution, size distribution or calibrated membrane material balance is independently admitted. Triton-normalized maximal emission is not a direct bilayer surface-area standard.

R18 PA conversion uses 2.7 mM oleic acid and three enzymes. Figure 7 morphology follows a different PG-pathway preparation and a 1.5 mM total fatty-acid feed. These are not matched single-vesicle samples or an interchangeable protocol. Cryo-EM snapshots are not longitudinal lineage/continuous growth tracking.

High-dose material forms stacked multilamellar-like structures that resolve after EDTA. The dosed-feed comparison also lowers magnesium; exact lower magnesium concentration is not resolved in the reviewed main/SI descriptions. Feeding and magnesium are changed together, so an isolated feeding or magnesium causal effect is not established.

The PA-divalent-cation/outer-leaflet imbalance/slow-flip-flop explanation is a source hypothesis. No direct leaflet-resolved synthesis, flip-flop kinetics, cation binding map, complete membrane retention, permeability/selectivity panel, electrochemical gradient or transport activity is measured here.

The title continuous refers to CoA reuse and finite precursor conversion; the conclusion proposes a future continuously controlled feeding system. Finite time courses/endpoints and supplied doses do not demonstrate indefinite membrane production, balanced division, autonomous enzyme renewal or population self-reproduction.
No universal efficiency/robustness benefit, compartmentalized competing metabolism, spontaneous origin sequence, adaptive regulation or required prior metabolic compartment is established.

Optogenetic activation of fast-spiking cells selectively amplifies local gamma in the reported barrel-cortex preparation.
Whisker-evoked responses depend on sensory-input phase relative to the experimentally induced gamma cycle.
LIP microstimulation shifts choices toward the selected response field and changes response times directionally.
LIP silencing shifts free choices away from contralateral targets and increases contralateral saccade endpoint error in the control task.
Retinotopically matched MT silencing impairs motion direction sensitivity; moving the stimulus outside the affected field restores performance in the reported control.
Motion-task choices show an early contraversive bias after LIP suppression, with reported attenuation over trials and sessions.
Changing visual reliability shifts combined height judgments; observed cue weights and thresholds resemble the declared maximum-likelihood predictions.
Assistive and resistive forces change hand-localization bias differently; the study reports no significant corresponding variance difference.
Practice in the imposed force field brings reaching paths toward their baseline shape in the reported task.
Removing the practiced force field produces reaching deviations approximately opposite to initial exposure errors.
Selective BLA terminal activation in CeA increases open-arm and center exploration in the reported high-stress mouse preparation.
Direct BLA somatic activation decreases open-arm exploration in the reported comparison; it is not interchangeable with projection activation.
Selective BLA-to-CeA terminal inhibition reduces open-arm and center exploration in a separate low-stress cohort.
Brief bilateral LC photostimulation promotes EEG/EMG-defined sleep-to-wake transitions in the inactive-period assay.
Hour-long LC photoinhibition reduces active-period wakefulness and wake-episode duration while leaving sleep-to-wake transitions possible.
Picrotoxin exposure changes the culture event-size distribution toward a bimodal form, with recovery after washout.
Hcrt-neuron photostimulation with specified trains shortens post-stimulation wake latency from SWS and REM relative to control mice; the distribution shifts rather than fixing the transition time.
Systemic Hcrt-R1 antagonist pretreatment reduced the 20-Hz stimulation-related shortening of post-stimulation wake latency in the reported comparison.
Activation of nonselective cells during the normal-contrast Go stimulus disrupts the measured Go ensemble and reduces task performance.
Activation of selected pattern-completion cells during low-contrast Go stimulation increases ensemble reliability and hit-minus-false-choice task performance.
In the selected WT-background TWISP preparation, AVJR activation produced increased downstream AVDR calcium activity (Randi et al. 2023, Figure 1).
In the selected WT-background TWISP preparation, AVER activation produced increased downstream AVAR calcium activity (Randi et al. 2023, Figure 1).
In the selected WT-background TWISP preparation, SAADL activation produced decreased downstream OLLR calcium activity (Randi et al. 2023, Figure 1).
Partial two-photon ablation of hindbrain radial astrocytes reduced time in futility-induced passivity in selected larval zebrafish; it did not abolish all passive behavior.
Light activation of gfap-driven Opto-alpha1-AR in hindbrain radial astrocytes reduced fictive swim power relative to controls.
Capsaicin treatment of fish expressing rat TRPV1 sparsely in radial astrocytes increased passive time in closed loop; transgene-negative and saline controls did not show the same effect.
Optogenetic NE-MO activation increased L-MO radial astrocyte calcium fluorescence in the selected larval fish preparation.
NE-MO activation reduced fictive swimming in fish with intact radial astrocytes, following a possible brief increase in swim vigor. The glia-ablated condition is a separate null result.

Cyclazosin treatment reduced the L-MO radial astrocyte calcium response evoked by NE-MO stimulation. Pharmacology supports alpha1B receptor involvement without proving exclusive astrocyte-specific action.

After closed loop was replaced by probabilistic swim-triggered visual feedback, mean radial astrocyte calcium rose faster with less reliable feedback. This readout supports temporal integration without identifying a unique algorithm.

In the DG slice imaging assay, astrocyte VGLUT1 deletion reduced CNO-evoked glutamate-sensor responses. Responses were detected in a subset of tested astrocytes; exact population proportions remain unresolved.

Theta-burst LTP was lower in DG synaptic fields near recombined VGLUT1-deficient astrocytes than in neighboring unrecombined fields. Figure 3 source data contains 16 paired normalized measurements; this does not establish universal astrocyte necessity for LTP.

Kir4.1 cKO passive astrocytes had smaller Ba2+-sensitive inward-current magnitudes during the stated Schaffer stimulation protocol than controls. This is an electrical uptake proxy, not a direct extracellular potassium measurement.

Kir4.1 cKO passive astrocytes had smaller TBOA-sensitive inward-current magnitudes in the presence of Ba2+ than controls. The developmental intervention and subtraction assay do not isolate a unique molecular mechanism of clearance.

Posttetanic potentiation over 0-2 min and short-term potentiation over 0-15 min were greater in Kir4.1 cKO slices than controls. The study does not uniquely assign this effect to potassium handling rather than glutamate handling or developmental changes.

MCT4 antisense treatment reduced inhibitory-avoidance retention latency at 24 h and 7 days relative to scrambled controls. Acquisition latency was not significantly changed. The behavioral result does not directly measure astrocyte-to-neuron lactate flux.

L-lactate rescued the reported MCT4-ODN-associated retention deficit at the tested 24 h and 7 day endpoints. Rescue supports a lactate-related contribution without uniquely establishing an exclusive fuel pathway.
MCT2 antisense reduced inhibitory-avoidance retention latency at 24 h and 7 days relative to scrambled controls. This regional knockdown is not a cell-restricted neuronal intervention.

The deprived optic nerve and tract had more CC1-positive mature oligodendrocytes than the respective controls. This endpoint does not establish increased total myelin thickness or a universally stabilizing glial property.

Myelin internodes generated during deprivation were reported shorter than open-eye controls. Text and caption disagree on the deprived median, so no exact median or quantitative geometry rule is assigned.

Deprived optic nerves had lower CAP-derived conduction velocity and broader length-normalized CAP responses than paired controls. The experiment changes visual experience, not only myelin internode length.

Microglia contained more labeled RGC input from the TTX-treated eye than from the vehicle eye in the selected P5 dLGN regions. This supports activity-dependent selection without identifying the exact synapse-tagging sequence.

Microglia contained more labeled input from the vehicle eye than from the forskolin-treated eye. The measured comparison concerns relative input engulfment within the sampled dLGN, not all neural activity or all glial cells.
P5 microglia in CR3/CD11b knockout mice engulfed less labeled RGC input than WT littermate controls. Engulfment persisted, so CR3 is not established as the sole route of input removal.
P5 microglia in C3 knockout mice engulfed less labeled RGC input than WT littermate controls. The developmental knockout does not isolate microglial C3 production or an exclusive complement pathway.

Ipsilateral and contralateral RGC projection territories overlapped more in CR3 knockout dLGN at P10 and P30. This is an anatomical refinement endpoint, not a direct measurement of synaptic transmission.

Juxtaposed VGlut2/GluR1 puncta and total VGlut2-positive puncta were more densely represented in CR3 knockout dLGN. These structural markers do not directly measure electrical efficacy or prove a unique engulfment mechanism.

After a targeted capillary lesion, nearby microglial processes switched toward the injured site and accumulated around it. This measures a local morphological response, not demonstrated neuronal protection.

In the neonatal microglial culture assay, ARL67156 treatment reduced measured medium adenosine after ATP exposure relative to the vehicle condition. This is a pharmacological culture contrast, not a cell-exclusive adult mechanism.

In the neonatal microglial culture assay, APCP treatment reduced measured medium adenosine after ATP exposure relative to the vehicle condition. This is a pharmacological culture contrast, not a cell-exclusive adult mechanism.

PLX5622-treated mice showed increased distance-dependent correlations and thresholded synchrony of striatal calcium events at baseline relative to controls. Correlated activity is the measured outcome; it does not identify direct neuronal connections.

Striatal dialysate adenosine was lower in the PLX5622 group than in controls in the anesthetized microdialysis assay. The source workbook supplies five independent mouse rows per group in ng/mL and a separate nM conversion.

The CD39-deletion cohort had lower striatal adenosine-assay fluorescence after D1 agonist than controls. Figure 4h source data are relative fluorescence units, not extracellular adenosine concentrations.
After D1 agonist challenge, Figure 4i source counts report seizures in 9/11 CD39-deletion mice and 1/11 controls. This is a challenge-specific incidence comparison.

CPA co-treatment reduced the reported D1-challenge seizure incidence in the CD39-deletion preparation: 1/9 co-treated mice versus 9/11 in the D1-only cohort. The co-treated control cohort had 0/5 seizures.
Figure 4f source counts report seizures in 9/11 P2ry12 knockout mice versus 3/13 controls after D1 agonist. The genotype contrast is not a cell-selective perturbation of microglial sensing.
Figure 4k source counts report seizures in 5/6 Adora1 flox/Drd1a-Cre mice versus 2/12 controls after D1 agonist. This receptor deletion differs from microglial CD39 deletion.
The Figure 4m D1-only cohort had seizures in 8/9 Il34 flox/Drd1a-Cre mice versus 2/11 controls. Neuronal ligand deletion with reduced microglia is not a direct, acute microglial ablation.

Figure 4m source counts show no seizures in 10 co-treated Il34-deletion mice or 11 co-treated controls, versus 8/9 and 2/11 in their respective D1-only cohorts. The caption and workbook give inconsistent co-treatment sample counts; the stated counts are the workbook values.

CNO exposure in the hM3Dq thalamocortical preparation increased microglial fluorescence near labeled cortical boutons relative to control conditions. This is a morphological proximity readout, not direct synaptic inhibition.
CNO exposure in the hM3Dq thalamocortical preparation reduced microglial process-tip velocity while bouton proximity increased. Lower tip velocity and directed recruitment are different measurements.

One hour after ECS, bulk dentate ATAC-seq identified gained-open and gained-closed regions relative to sham. Supplementary Table 4 lists 11,438 gained-open and 1,739 gained-closed regions under the publication analysis; these are genomic region counts, not neuron counts.

Independent dentate RNA-seq samples showed increased and decreased transcript abundance one hour after ECS relative to sham. This is an RNA-abundance response, not a direct measurement of transcription rate, protein production or learning.

Across independent post-ECS cohorts, the published region lists retain 4,175 early gained-open and 484 gained-closed regions at four hours, and 597/22 respectively across one, four and 24 hours. The shared genomic regions define a sampled window; most early changes are not retained through every sampled timepoint.

AAV c-Fos shRNA attenuated ECS-associated chromatin opening at regions annotated with c-Fos binding sites compared with control shRNA. This supports a contribution to the induction response under this perturbation.

c-Fos shRNA attenuated induction of RNA for genes associated with the selected activity-responsive regions compared with control shRNA. Parallel accessibility and RNA effects do not uniquely establish that accessibility mediates the RNA response.

AAV c-Fos overexpression without ECS partially mimicked activity-associated opening at c-Fos-associated regions compared with EYFP control. It does not establish sufficiency for all activity-dependent chromatin changes.

Without ECS, c-Fos overexpression increased RNA abundance for genes associated with c-Fos-induced chromatin opening. Similar distributions of selected expression changes do not establish molecular or functional equivalence to ECS.

After cross-fostering within 12 hours of birth, adult hippocampal bisulfite readouts at the 5-prime NGFI-A-site CpG (site 16) followed foster-mother care class. The comparison supports a postnatal environmental contribution rather than an effect fixed solely by biological-mother class.

In adult offspring of low-care mothers, repeated intracerebroventricular TSA increased acetyl-H3K9-associated ChIP signal at the GR exon 1_7 promoter relative to vehicle. The signal is a bulk chromatin assay, not single-cell accessibility or DNA methylation.

Repeated TSA increased NGFI-A-associated ChIP signal at the GR exon 1_7 promoter in adult low-care offspring relative to vehicle. This effect does not independently identify which chromatin modification caused the binding change.

TSA reduced the hippocampal bisulfite methylation readout at NGFI-A-site CpG 16 in adult low-care offspring relative to vehicle. The broad drug intervention does not establish locus-specific demethylation as the unique mediator of later outcomes.

TSA reduced the CpG site-17 bisulfite readout in both high- and low-care offspring. Maternal-care class and cross-fostering did not show that site-17 effect, so TSA does not exactly recreate the maternal-care methylation pattern.

TSA increased hippocampal GR protein immunoreactivity normalized to alpha-tubulin in adult low-care offspring relative to vehicle. This is a protein readout, separate from promoter methylation, RNA abundance and the restraint-stress cohort.

In a separate adult low-care offspring cohort, TSA reduced the plasma corticosterone response associated with a 20-minute restraint challenge relative to vehicle. Samples extended to 90 minutes after restraint onset; this is an endocrine response, not direct evidence of subjective stress or a unique neural mechanism.

Five days after conditioning, exposure to the changed environment B yielded fewer Arc+/eYFP+ labeled cells per DG slice than re-exposure to training environment A. This is an effect of the environmental comparison on a marker readout, not a selective intervention establishing that the labeled cells cause memory.

The changed-context A-B group showed less freezing than the A-A group in the five-day re-exposure assay. Freezing is a behavioral readout under a multi-cue protocol; its covariance with neuronal labels does not establish a molecular mediator.

Peripheral LPS produced more cNST FOS-positive neurons than saline at two hours in the specified counting region. The marker response does not establish DBH-specific firing or identify the peripheral mediator.

The main 0.5 mg/kg LPS challenge increased bulk Vglut2-cre cNST calcium-response area relative to the preceding saline session. Fixed session order and a population fluorescence measurement limit causal and cellular interpretation.

The separately vagotomized group showed lower LPS-evoked cNST calcium-response area than intact animals. The published figure reports an approximately 80% reduction with residual signal; it does not demonstrate complete elimination of every immune-to-brain route.

Under LPS challenge, hM4Di inhibition of the LPS-TRAPed cNST population increased circulating IL-6 and IL-1beta and reduced IL-10 relative to CNO-treated mCherry controls. This is a three-analyte blood profile, not an immune-cell-specific production assay.

Under LPS challenge, hM3Dq activation of the LPS-TRAPed cNST population reduced circulating IL-6 and IL-1beta and increased IL-10 relative to CNO-treated mCherry controls. These effects do not identify the descending efferent pathway.
Dbh-cre cNST hM3Dq activation reduced circulating IL-6, IL-1beta and TNF and increased IL-10 after LPS. The four-analyte endpoint does not demonstrate that norepinephrine is the required mediator.

Trpa1-cre nodose hM3Dq activation reduced circulating IL-6 and IL-1beta and increased IL-10 after LPS relative to mCherry controls. The intervention targets a neuronal population, not the TRPA1 channel protein alone.

Calca-cre nodose hM3Dq activation reduced circulating IL-6 and IL-1beta after LPS. IL-10 did not differ significantly and is represented separately; this population does not inherit the TRPA1-associated three-analyte profile.

In the high-dose LPS assay, the Trpa1-cre nodose activation group had greater survival than mCherry controls through the plotted nine-day window. This endpoint concerns endotoxaemia, not clearance of a live infection.

In the separate high-dose LPS assay, Dbh-cre cNST activation improved survival relative to mCherry controls through the plotted nine-day window. This does not establish treatment efficacy against bacterial infection or an interchangeable nodose protocol.

Sustained Trpa1-cre nodose hM3Dq activation during oral Salmonella infection increased bacterial colony counts per gram in spleen and mesenteric lymph nodes relative to mCherry controls. Lower inflammation cannot be generalized to improved host defense.

Intraperitoneal TNF or IL-1beta and IL-10 evoked calcium responses in different observed nodose neurons during the short recording trials. The response classifier and sampled cells define the claim; direct neuronal cytokine-receptor binding is not established.

Extraintestinal cytokine perfusion evoked repeatable calcium responses in sampled nodose neurons. Repeated responses in this preparation support stimulus sensitivity but do not establish direct receptor binding or a complete immune feedback loop.

Constitutive Tek-Cre Kcnj2 deletion removed the measured barium-sensitive inward-rectifier current in isolated capillary endothelial cells relative to wild type. The record identifies Kir2.1, not a general glial potassium-uptake process.
Focal capillary 10 mM potassium dilated the attached upstream arteriole ex vivo. Barium treatment and endothelial-targeted Kcnj2 deletion suppressed this response in the specified comparisons.

Focal capillary 10 mM potassium hyperpolarized upstream arteriolar smooth muscle in the isolated CaPA recording. This is a direct voltage measurement at the sampled upstream cell, not along every intervening endothelial contact.

Separating the capillary tree from its feed arteriole removed the upstream dilatory response to capillary 10 mM potassium, while direct arteriolar potassium still evoked dilation. Continuity is supported; a particular connexin is not identified.

Focal capillary 10 mM potassium increased peak RBC flux in wild-type mice. The response was attenuated in endothelial-targeted Kcnj2 knockout and barium-treated wild-type groups; flux counts RBC passages per second.

Focal capillary 10 mM potassium increased RBC velocity in the wild-type comparison; no significant increase was detected in the knockout or barium-treated comparisons. Velocity was measured in the peak-flux bin and is distinct from flux.
Capillary 10 mM potassium increased upstream feed-arteriole diameter in the in vivo paired comparison. This does not imply that the stimulated capillary itself dilated.

Cortical 15 mM potassium increased relative perfusion, with a smaller response after endothelial-targeted Kcnj2 deletion. Surface barium further reduced responses; this cortical exposure is distinct from focal capillary injection.

Whisker stimulation evoked a smaller relative cortical perfusion response after endothelial-targeted Kcnj2 deletion, with residual responses present. Barium reduced responses further and is not restricted to capillary endothelium.

Focal capillary potassium still increased RBC flux under cortical tetrodotoxin, while whisker-evoked flux was suppressed in the separate control comparison. Ejected potassium bypasses the physiological release step.

GTPgammaS reduced residual ATP and NAV-2729 increased it relative to their separate vehicle controls in the supplemented microvessel lysate assay. The inverse readout supports altered kinase activity, not direct endothelial membrane PIP2 measurement.

Pipette NAV-2729 caused a time-dependent reduction of capillary endothelial Kir currents relative to vehicle. Bath diC16-PIP2 present before recording preserved much of the current during NAV exposure; it was not a sequential rescue after current loss in the same cell.

Capillary endothelial cells from inducible Arf6 knockdown mice had lower barium-sensitive Kir current density than littermate controls. Partial endothelial knockdown is distinct from complete or capillary-restricted deletion.

Bath diC16-PIP2 increased the measured Kir current in capillary endothelial cells from Arf6 knockdown mice relative to untreated knockdown cells. The result supports a supplementation effect without direct measurement of endogenous lipid concentration.

NAV-2729 reduced upstream arteriole dilation to focal capillary potassium in the ex vivo preparation relative to vehicle. Diameter is the observed endpoint; conducted voltage is inferred rather than directly recorded in this assay.

Cortical NAV-2729 reduced whisker-evoked relative perfusion. Concurrent intravenous diC16-PIP2 preserved a larger response relative to NAV alone, but did not restore the higher vehicle-treated response. Groups and pre/post comparisons remain distinct.

Arf6 knockdown mice had lower untreated whisker-evoked perfusion responses than littermate controls in the reported comparison. Subsequent barium reduced both responses, with a smaller reported barium-sensitive fraction in knockdown mice; no exact fraction is calibrated.

Intravenous diC16-PIP2 increased the whisker-evoked perfusion response in Arf6 knockdown mice in a separate cohort. The nonsignificant treated-genotype contrast does not establish complete equivalence or restoration of every vascular function.

Arterial endothelial Gja4/Gja5 deletion increased apparent input resistance and decreased apparent capacitance in the aortic whole-cell assay. These coupled-network measurements do not establish brain endothelial conduction velocity.

Neurobiotin loaded through a patch pipette reached fewer neighboring aortic endothelial cells after arterial Gja4/Gja5 deletion. Residual multicell fills occurred; the result is not complete elimination in every measurement.

Retinal large-artery serotonin fills were restricted to single probe cells in the sampled connexin mutants. Spreading events in controls depended on favorable loading and were observed in only two of four mice.

Pial arterial diameter responses to focal visual stimulation were smaller and more spatially restricted in arterial connexin mutants. This two-photon endpoint retains a separate local diving-arteriole null.

The widefield HbT-related arterial response to focal visual stimulation showed reduced spatial extent in connexin mutants. The optical response and its fitted decay are not calibrated blood flow or a graph edge length.

ChRmine stimulation produced smaller, more spatially restricted arterial HbT-related responses in connexin mutants. Distance is measured from opsin expression, and the zero-laser trials can retain vascular responses.

The response-onset-versus-distance calculation yielded slower arterial propagation in connexin mutants. This velocity is derived from optical vasomotion trajectories; it is neither RBC velocity nor directly measured electrical conduction.

Connexin mutants had longer optical-response time-to-peak in the five reported distance bins extending through 1200-1600 micrometers from ChRmine expression. The 1600-2000-micrometer bin is a separate nonsignificant result.

Full-field visual stimulation evoked a more spatially restricted arterial HbT-related response in connexin mutants. The assay does not directly measure ATP demand, oxygen use or adequacy of metabolic supply.

Connexin mutants had longer optical-response time-to-peak in the three full-field distance bins extending through 400-800 micrometers. The 800-1200-micrometer bin did not show a significant genotype difference.

Somatic current injection evoked action potentials in selected GFP-labeled dentate neurons four to eight weeks after retroviral injection. This demonstrates excitability in a sampled neuron, not its necessary contribution to memory.

Perforant-path stimulation evoked postsynaptic responses in four sampled birth-labeled neurons. Spontaneous input was also observed in six cells. These afferent responses do not establish functional axonal output to the downstream circuit.

Running-housed mice had more BrdU-labeled dentate cells than standard-housed mice in the separate 48-hour assay. BrdU incorporation does not itself count mature neurons or show that learning is necessary for neurogenesis.

Light pulses evoke spikes in selected ChR2-labeled dentate neurons. Opsin expression and age affect capture and latency; this is an imposed activation protocol, not endogenous firing or a universal maturation threshold.

Illumination of labeled granule-cell populations evoked postsynaptic currents in 14 of 107 sampled target cells. This supports functional output in selected slices; the yield is not a connection probability, and the illustrated CA3 pyramidal response includes a polysynaptic inhibitory route.

Kynurenic acid blocked light-evoked postsynaptic responses in eight tested targets. Dependence on glutamatergic transmission can occur upstream of an inhibitory relay, so blockade does not make every recorded response a direct excitatory synapse.

The group-II metabotropic glutamate receptor agonist DCG-IV suppressed light-evoked postsynaptic responses in two experiments, consistent with mossy-fiber involvement. This does not locate every synaptic hop or establish a universal connection strength.

Eight weeks after tamoxifen, NCff mice had more dentate DCX-positive cells and more DCX-positive cells with tertiary dendrites than vehicle controls (three mice per group). This is a marker-population response to the Bax manipulation, not a direct neuron birth-rate measurement.

The day-56 dentate assay found more retained BrdU-labeled cells after the Bax manipulation: reported means 11113 versus 3004 in controls, three mice per group. BrdU was given on days 9-18; only a subset expressed NeuN, so the total is not a count of mature functional neurons.

At eight weeks, the Bax manipulation increased the weak-tetanus dentate field-LTP response without bicuculline (reported treatment P=0.039). This population assay does not identify the contribution of each birthdated neuron or prove a complete cell-number mediation route.

In the nine-day similar-context task, male NCff mice given tamoxifen had higher discrimination ratios than vehicle controls (11 versus nine mice; reported treatment P=0.023). This supports a task-specific behavioral effect; it does not directly measure neural pattern separation or general memory improvement.

In the running-housed comparison, tamoxifen-treated NCff mice showed greater open-field path length, rearing and center exploration than vehicle controls (11 versus ten mice). Changed locomotion prevents an isolated anxiety interpretation and does not establish a human therapeutic effect.

The separately irradiated Bax-floxed cohort had fewer dentate DCX-positive cells than sham controls: reported means 144 versus 3120, three mice per group. This regional intervention does not selectively isolate newborn-neuron function or by itself prove cognitive necessity.

Over four days, reaching-trained adolescent mice had greater spine formation and elimination than controls. Table S1 reports formation 13.3 versus 6.0 percent and elimination 13.7 versus 9.0 percent, with 25 trained and 18 control mice. These are interval-specific morphological responses in sampled dendrites.

Naive adults learning the reaching task had greater four-day formation and elimination than controls: reported formation 7.9 versus 3.7 percent and elimination 9.5 versus 4.0 percent, five trained versus six control mice. The result does not supply an age-independent remodeling rate.

Naive adults learning capellini handling had greater four-day formation and elimination than controls: reported formation 7.8 versus 3.7 percent and elimination 8.2 versus 4.0 percent, five trained versus six control mice. This task is separate from single-seed reaching.

Adults pretrained in adolescent reaching showed increased formation and elimination during a new capellini task compared with general adult controls: 8.7 versus 3.7 percent formation and 9.0 versus 4.0 percent elimination, five versus six mice. This is a compound task-history comparison.

Of spines first seen between days zero and four, 42.3 percent persisted to the reported approximately 120-day follow-up in mice trained for sixteen days, versus 13.5 percent in controls, five mice per group. Survival of this selected new-spine subset supports finite structural persistence, not permanence or memory necessity.

At one week after photothrombosis, the reported six-hour spine-formation percentage was 1.37, versus 0.14 in controls; 4 poststroke mice and six controls. The increase concerns retained new lateral protrusions in the sampled peri-infarct cortex, not continuous weeks-long tracking or neuronal birth.

At 2 weeks after photothrombosis, the reported six-hour spine-formation percentage was 0.93, versus 0.14 in controls; 4 poststroke mice and six controls. The increase concerns retained new lateral protrusions in the sampled peri-infarct cortex, not continuous weeks-long tracking or neuronal birth.

At 6 weeks after photothrombosis, the reported six-hour spine-formation percentage was 0.75, versus 0.14 in controls; 3 poststroke mice and six controls. The increase concerns retained new lateral protrusions in the sampled peri-infarct cortex, not continuous weeks-long tracking or neuronal birth.

At one week, sampled dendrites had lower spine density than controls: reported 1.81 versus 2.23 spines per ten micrometers, four versus six mice. This spatial density is distinct from the increased percentage of new protrusions during the acute six-hour assay.

Six weeks after photothrombosis, fluorescent vascular volume fraction was higher than in controls: reported 7.25 versus 4.36 percent, t(8)=3.14, P<0.01. This volume-occupancy result does not count new vessels or establish a selectively tested angiogenesis mechanism.

At 24 hours after four training days, trace-paired rats had more dentate BrdU-labeled cells than unpaired and naive controls, with six animals per group. BrdU preceded training by one week. The measured endpoint is retained labeled cells, not a separately identified increase in division rate.

The trace-paired group had fewer morphologically pyknotic subgranular profiles than naive and unpaired groups. These are total degenerating profiles, not an identified newborn-neuron survival fraction. The printed ANOVA degrees of freedom and terminal-cohort allocation remain unresolved.

At 24 hours after training, the place group had more dentate BrdU-labeled cells than naive, cue and time-yoked swimming groups, with six animals per group. This is an effect of the specified training comparison on previously labeled cells; a unique survival mechanism was not isolated.

The place-trained group had fewer morphologically pyknotic subgranular profiles than naive, cue and time-yoked swimming groups. Counts of all degenerating profiles do not establish survival of individually tracked newborn neurons, and the exact terminal cohort for this paragraph is unresolved.

PV photostimulation evokes a tonic RGL current that is blocked by bicuculline and enhanced by vigabatrin in the tested slices. This is a GABA-sensitive clamp-current response, not RGL spiking, cell-cycle entry or a measured one-to-one synapse.

Five-day PV activation lowers EdU-positive RGL density, MCM2-positive RGL density and the MCM2-positive fraction relative to no-light sham. The endpoint is suppression of the measured cycle markers, not reduced mature-neuron production measured across the full lineage.

Five-day PV inhibition increases EdU-positive RGL density, MCM2-positive RGL density and the MCM2-positive fraction relative to no-light sham. Increased marker counts do not establish successful maturation, integration or a universal neural-activity requirement.

Conditional gamma2 deletion increases assigned activated clones at two and seven days. At seven days, R+R and R+astrocyte classes increase while the R+intermediate-progenitor comparison is nonsignificant. The class distribution is not a uniform increase in neuronal production.

At thirty days, conditional gamma2 deletion changes the assigned clone composition, including more R+R and no-R clones and fewer single-R and neuronal or multilineage classes. Later lineage effects and unresolved denominators prevent conversion to founder transition probabilities.

The five-day systemic diazepam comparison lowers EdU-positive and MCM2-positive RGL densities and the MCM2-positive fraction. Systemic treatment does not by itself identify a selective RGL receptor mechanism or measure completed neuron production.

Within the isolated housing condition, PV activation lowers EdU-positive density, MCM2-positive density and the MCM2-positive RGL fraction compared with isolated no-light controls. This treatment contrast is distinct from comparing the two housing groups under light.

Under PV light stimulation, isolated mice retain higher EdU-positive RGL density than group-housed mice in Figure 5c, with reported P < 0.05. This residual housing contrast prevents a claim that PV activation abolishes every measured isolation effect.

In 23 French adults, every selected regular category has lower mean error than the irregular baseline, including the first presentation's positions 6-8. The effect concerns these stimulus contrasts under corrective feedback, not recovery of a complete unseen program from one exposure.

In the 24-child Experiment 2 cohort, repeat, repeat+2, two-arcs, two-squares and four-segments sequences have lower mean error than the irregular baseline. This is task-specific success with selected patterns; it does not establish possession of every proposed primitive.

In the separate 23-child Experiment 3 cohort, repeat, repeat+2, two-arcs and four-segments sequences have lower mean error than the irregular baseline. Two complete previews precede each block, followed by the same corrective task.

In the 20-participant Munduruku cohort, all tested regular categories except two-crosses have lower overall error than the irregular baseline. The two-arcs boundary at position 13 is below baseline; two-squares and diagonal-position contrasts remain uneven. The cohort combines adolescents and adults.

In the selected adult sample, recognition repetitions, violation-response time and missed violations increase with assigned sequence complexity, including analyses excluding the irregular template. Published AIC selection also retains the presence of rotation by three steps for recognition and response time, and spatial distance for misses; description cost alone is not a complete behavioral account.

In the subsequent primitive-pair task, every tested geometric rule has shorter reported recognition time and fewer missed violations than the unrelated-pair control. Rotations by three steps are harder on selected measures than some other primitives, contradicting equal behavioral cost as a general assumption for this task.

In the separate 44-adult behavioral experiment, average anticipation index increases with assigned sequence description cost (reported R squared 0.86, P<0.001): simpler templates have less normalized gaze error at target onset. Repeat and alternate patterns show an advantage over irregular from the fourth and seventh locations of the first presentation respectively.

In the 23-person fMRI behavioral sample, all tested template/violation-position conditions have above-chance detection. Across the ten template means, sensitivity decreases with assigned description cost (reported R squared 0.95), while correct-response time increases (R squared 0.85).

The compensation relation is defined on a local deviation δΩ of the admissibility context Ω: the manuscript writes E = C(δΩ), with C the minimal compensation function. This is an argument dependency of an author definition, not a process in which Ω produces compensation or energy.

The oscillatory mode class is introduced as a minimal stable compensatory form: ψ = A e^{i(kx−ωt)} denotes the simplest oscillatory configuration said to preserve admissible compensation. The mode definition uses the compensation notion; equation satisfaction, stability and objecthood remain separate tests.

The assumed hyperbolic frame is argued from five stated admissibility conditions, one of which is compensatory boundedness; definite signatures are rejected as incompatible with compensatory balance between ordered variation and directional localization. The frame's stated assumptions use the compensation notion; this does not force the signature.

The discrete-scale hypothesis is stated as a discrete compensation scale: ℏ is introduced as a marker of discrete compensatory action and of the discreteness of admissible compensation in oscillatory regimes. The hypothesis is defined with the compensation notion; no discrete spectrum follows from that wording.

The discrete-scale relations E = ℏω and p = ℏk are written with the frequency ω and wave number k of the oscillatory mode ψ = A e^{i(kx−ωt)}, and the manuscript lists (k, ω, ℏ) as the parameters within whose bounded range such a mode is said to remain stable. The hypothesis uses the mode parameters; no rule selecting discrete values is supplied.

The field-anisotropy interpretation boundary evaluates the Level-0 anisotropy proposal: it lists what an anisotropy assertion must specify, uses the free real scalar dispersion as an isotropic comparison and admits no anisotropic field regime or directional-admissibility law. Neither record establishes anisotropy, and F12 remains unresolved.

The field-anisotropy boundary evaluates the directional-gradient proposal: it records that no admissibility functional, domain, gradient operator, units, field-observable map or testable anisotropy prediction is supplied, so the gradient name cannot connect Level 0 to a field model. F12 remains unresolved.

The photon polarization scope evaluates the directional-gradient proposal as a polarization-response question: in the free Maxwell model the two transverse polarization modes have the same free frequency and no preferred vacuum axis, and the record states that the directional admissibility gradient has no functional, domain, operator, units or field-response map.

The directional excitation boundary evaluates the transport-bias proposal: it separates dispersion and envelope velocity, damping, localization and decay, treats free-scalar group velocity as no net directed current, and records that the proposal has no admissibility functional, units, field observable or testable drift prediction. F12 remains unresolved.

The isotropic free-scalar dispersion record supplies the formal null against which a proposed directional anisotropy is evaluated: rotation-related wave vectors of equal magnitude have equal energy at fixed mass, and the record states that its inputs neither yield anisotropy nor supply a Level-0 admissibility-gradient mechanism.

The quantum-field framework definition is scoped against a construction from Level 0 and states what a quantum-field target must specify: quantum fields, states and dynamics with chosen fields, symmetries and interactions. That specification is what C-phys-l0-bridge records as missing from the carrier-promotion contract; the bridge evaluates the proposal and derives nothing.

The discrete-scale hypothesis is interpreted with the free real scalar quantization: there, discreteness enters through the canonical commutators as integer occupation of each mode, with energy steps ω_p in ħ = 1 units, while ω_p ranges over continuous momenta unless boundaries are imposed. E = ℏω and p = ℏk therefore do not by themselves make ω or k discrete.

The declared Level-0 case convention ∂²tΨ − ∂²xΨ + m²Ψ = 0 with m² = ω² − k² is the free Klein-Gordon equation of the free real scalar evolution record restricted to one spatial dimension, with the same plane-wave dispersion ω² = k² + m². The identity is mathematical; it does not identify Ψ with a quantum field or m with a measured mass.

The manuscript proposes that the sequential operator ∂t opens the condition for temporal directionality and that time first appears as a directional condition of distinguishability; the physical notion referred to is the time parameter of Hamiltonian evolution in the free scalar record. This records the author's proposed reading; it does not identify the sequential primitive with measured time.

The manuscript proposes that the operator ∂x opens the condition for spatial localization and that spatial interpretation becomes admissible only after localization stabilizes; the physical notion referred to is spatial localization of free-field excitations, which in L1 requires smeared wavepackets moving in flat space. This records the author's proposed reading, not a derivation of space.

The manuscript defines energy at Level 0 as the structural measure of compensatory requirement, E = C(δΩ), and concludes that energy appears as a compensatory measure of admissible deviation; the physical notion referred to is energy as the Hamiltonian of a specified field. This records the author's proposed reading only; C has no specified form to compare.

The manuscript proposes the scalar closure parameter m² as the precursor of what physical theory will later describe as mass, to be reinterpreted only once localized node-like units are admissible; the physical notion referred to is the mass m of the free scalar's particle states, E_p² = p² + m². This records the author's proposed reading; no mass identification is established.

The manuscript proposes that a coherently stabilized resonant node behaves, at the level of admissibility, as a particle-like unit in 1+1 dimensions while not asserting physical particles; the physical notion referred to is the particle of a quantized field, a Fock excitation of definite momentum and mass. This records the author's proposed reading; no CRT instance or particle identification is admitted.

The manuscript names the variational equation of its quadratic action a Klein-Gordon-type form and its operator the hyperbolic d'Alembertian class, while reading both as Level-0 admissibility devices rather than the wave operator of later physics; the physical notion referred to is the free Klein-Gordon field. As written, the source's operator and mass signs do not match that form (F02).

The manuscript proposes ensemble-quanta as the basic carriers of a Level-1 effective field Φ and calls the hierarchy φp → ensemble-quantum → Φ the ontological foundation of the first quantum-field level, while stating that an ensemble-quantum is not a particle or field excitation and that no quantum-field theory is completed; the physical notion referred to is the quantum-field framework.

The partial-lifetime convention tau/B=1/Gamma_channel uses the branching fraction of the inclusive width convention, B_f=Gamma_f/Gamma_tot over a complete channel partition, with tau the inverse total decay rate; in inverse-time units the channel rate is Gamma_f/hbar=B_f/tau. This is a definitional transfer, not evidence that the proton decays or that its channel partition is known.

The ensemble survival record applies the exponential survival law and the mean-lifetime-as-inverse-decay-rate convention of the C001 lifetime record to a stored neutron population; its effective loss rate adds non-decay losses to the beta-decay rate 1/tau_n, so 1/lambda equals the conventional lifetime only after those losses are corrected.

The proton spin-to-cyclotron ratio g_p/2=nu_L/nu_c uses the free cyclotron frequency reconstructed from the three trap eigenfrequencies by the invariance relation declared in the C001 cyclotron-comparison record; the ratio gives the moment in nuclear magnetons but transfers no mass value or trap correction between the experiments.

The Sachs form factors are combinations of the Dirac and Pauli form factors that parametrize the proton's elastic electromagnetic-current response; in the light-front treatment that current is identified at x+=0 with the free quark current weighted by quark charges, the C001 quark electromagnetic current. The MAMI fit determines no quark amplitudes, flavor separation or geometry.

The CLAS neutron response is defined with the same one-photon Sachs decomposition that the C025 record states for the proton, now with GE_n and GM_n and the dipole and magnetic-moment normalization; no MAMI cross section or fit enters the CLAS or Hall A extractions.

The electron anomaly ratio g/2=1+nu_a/nu_c uses the free cyclotron frequency obtained from the trap-modified cyclotron, axial and magnetron frequencies by the invariance relation declared in the C001 cyclotron-comparison record; the relativistic shift and cavity correction remain separate electron-specific terms.

The signed electron-moment normalization -mu/mu_B=g/2 with positive mu_B=e*hbar/(2m) uses the declared charge convention in which e>0 is the positron charge and the electron carries -e; the convention fixes signs and units, not the measured g/2.

The ATLAS common signal strength 1.4+/-0.3 is interpreted with the narrow-resonance rate convention: it scales every SM-predicted signal yield by one factor relative to the fixed-mass SM reference, the special case of equal mu_if across channels; it is not a coupling, width or Yukawa determination.

The ATLAS four-lepton candidate readout is built from same-flavour, opposite-charge lepton pairs whose reconstructed invariant masses m12 and m34 define the selection windows, with the four-lepton invariant mass as the displayed observable; it uses the C001 pair invariant-mass convention on calibrated lepton four-momenta.

ATLAS reads its excess against the SM Higgs hypothesis, the scalar implied by the electroweak symmetry-breaking mechanism, which in the declared single-doublet background is the one neutral physical scalar H whose couplings are fixed once its mass is specified; compatibility does not establish the doublet structure or exclude extended Higgs sectors.

ATLAS identifies the new particle as neutral from its decays to vector-boson pairs of zero net charge; that reading uses the declared charges of the weak vector fields, W+ and W- with +e and -e and a neutral Z, together with the neutral photon, and is not a direct charge measurement of the new state.

The 1969 nu*W2 values are extracted from electron-only cross sections through the one-photon W1/W2 decomposition with the unknown ratio R of longitudinal to transverse virtual-photon absorption; the C001 inclusive response defines that R and the variable x, so the scaling record's transverse dominance is the R=0 choice and omega=1/x.

Borexino reads e- -> nu + gamma as a charge non-conserving decay of the lightest known charged particle; that reading uses the declared lepton assignments, the electron with charge -e and the active neutrino electrically neutral. The bound constrains this one channel and is not a charge or neutrino-flavor measurement.

Borexino frames its search as a test of electric-charge conservation, which it ties to Maxwell's equations and the unbroken U(1) gauge symmetry; the searched final-state photon is the neutral gauge quantum of the declared unbroken electromagnetic U(1) model. The limit is not a photon-charge or photon-mass bound.

The Shalm p-values bound a null hypothesis of local realism, local hidden-variable responses with settings chosen independently of the hidden variables, the model class of the C001 CHSH record. Shalm tests it with a Clauser-Horne-type probability inequality rather than the CHSH correlator S, so the CHSH bound itself is not the tested statistic.

The acquisition context's nonmaximally polarization-entangled pairs are the designed pure state 0.961|H_A H_B>+0.276|V_A V_B> on Alice's and Bob's polarization factors; with both amplitudes nonzero it does not factorize, which is the C001 pure-state entanglement criterion. Entanglement of the designed state is not itself the Bell-test result.

The CMS benchmark couples to the Z through the declared neutral-current convention: with weak isospin zero and charge q, g_A=T3=0 and g_V=T3-2Q*sin^2(theta_W)=-2q*sin^2(theta_W), which fixes its modified Drell-Yan photon/Z signal model. The convention defines the benchmark couplings and is not evidence that such particles exist.

The Lee residual is defined for drop charge in units of e, the magnitude of the electron charge, which is the positive unit of the declared lepton charge convention (electron -e, positron +e); integer multiples of e are the reference from which fractional residuals are measured. No quark or color interpretation follows.

The primordial network's weak-rate normalization is defined with the free-neutron decay rate 1/tau_n, the inverse mean lifetime of the exponential-survival convention. This is a definitional use of the lifetime quantity; it imports no particular storage or beam measurement and makes neutron decay no formation step.

The historical BBN context interprets its adopted neutron-lifetime input against storage ('bottle') determinations, which count surviving neutrons and must correct non-decay losses. The relation records which lifetime definition the source treats as BBN-relevant; no UCNtau value is adopted or compared.

The BBN context contrasts its lifetime input with the beam method, which infers tau from detected proton-producing decays of a monitored beam. Under the source's conditional dark-decay reading, that decay-product count would not be the BBN-relevant total rate; no beam lifetime is adopted.

The network's Born n<->p weak rates are defined in the low-energy four-fermion description: their prefactor is proportional to G_F^2 cos^2(theta_C)(1+3g_A^2). The source then fixes the overall normalization from the free-neutron lifetime rather than from G_F; no electroweak parameter is fitted.

The network's deuterium bottleneck is described through the binding energy of the same n+p<->d+gamma channel whose energy balance (photon energy plus deuteron recoil) the C001 capture record defines. The network uses an approximate 2.2 MeV value; no capture measurement is adopted.

The network's charged-particle thermonuclear rates are parametrized with Coulomb-barrier penetration: Coulomb functions, the Sommerfeld parameter Z1*Z2*e^2/(hbar*v) and an astrophysical S-factor. This uses the like-sign Coulomb repulsion between nuclear charges; it is not a fitted nuclear potential.

interactionCases.title: Screened repulsion and finite null long-range attraction in isolated charged-colloid pairs

Within SOMA this arising is classified as an object because a quark is treated as a distinguishable carrier unit with definite quantum identity, even though isolated free realization is excluded by later confinement structure. This arising establishes the foundational object basis for strong-interaction matter and enables subsequent organization into hadrons, confinement regimes, and nucleonic structure.

arisings.name: Endocytosis and Exocytosis
arisings.summary: Process-level vesicular transport regime enabling regulated uptake, intracellular routing, and release of materials by the cell.
arisings.description: Endocytosis and Exocytosis denote the admissible process-level organization in which membrane dynamics, signaling control, and intracellular routing are integrated into a regulated vesicular transport regime at the cellular level. Within Level 4 this arising is classified as a process because it consists in the ongoing budding, trafficking, targeting, docking, fusion, and release operations through which the cell internalizes external material, redistributes cargo between compartments, and secretes selected molecules. This process transforms the cell boundary from a passive separator into an active programmable interface that modulates material exchange according to cellular context, organelle identity, and signaling state. The arising establishes directional flow, cargo specificity, boundary remodeling, and regulated coupling between cellular state and membrane-mediated transport activity.

arisings.name: DNA Repair Mechanisms and Genome Stability
arisings.summary: Process-level cellular regime detecting, repairing, and preserving genome integrity under ongoing damage and replication stress.
arisings.description: DNA Repair Mechanisms and Genome Stability denote the admissible process-level organization in which molecular repair pathways, regulatory signaling, and controlled gene expression are integrated into a coordinated cellular regime that preserves the integrity of genetic information over time. Within Level 4 this arising is classified as a process because it consists in the ongoing detection of DNA damage, replication errors, and chemical modifications, the selection and activation of appropriate repair pathways, and the coordination of repair with replication, transcription, checkpoint control, and cell-fate responses. Genome stability here is maintained through regulated cellular operations rather than isolated molecular events, including repair, tolerance, arrest, and when necessary transition toward programmed cell death. This arising establishes the cellular-scale maintenance regime through which genetic material remains sufficiently stable for continued viability, inheritance, and controlled function.

arisings.name: Intracellular Transport and Cytoskeletal Systems
arisings.summary: Process-level organization of directed intracellular transport through cytoskeletal structures, motor activity, and regulated spatial routing.
arisings.description: Intracellular Transport and Cytoskeletal Systems denote the admissible process-level organization in which structural polymers, motor proteins, and regulatory signaling are integrated into a coordinated intracellular framework for spatial organization and directed transport. Within Level 4 this arising is classified as a process because it consists in the ongoing assembly, remodeling, routing, and force-coupled movement of vesicles, organelles, macromolecular complexes, and signaling components within the bounded cellular space. The cytoskeletal system functions both as a mechanical scaffold and as a directional transport infrastructure, enabling targeted redistribution of cellular contents, spatial differentiation of functional zones, and dynamic reconfiguration during growth, polarization, and division. This arising establishes the regulated cellular transport regime through which internal positioning, cargo delivery, and structural coordination become reliably admissible.

arisings.name: Cellular Mechanisms of Immune Response
arisings.summary: Process-level cellular defensive regime integrating recognition, signaling, and effector responses against internal and external threats.
arisings.description: Cellular Mechanisms of Immune Response denote the admissible process-level organization in which molecular recognition, intracellular signaling, and controlled effector actions are integrated into a coherent defensive regime at the cellular level. Within Level 4 this arising is classified as a process because it consists in the ongoing detection of non-self, altered-self, or damaged-self patterns, the amplification and routing of danger-related signals, and the execution of targeted defensive responses such as secretion of protective molecules, localized degradation of compromised components, or activation of programmed cell death. This process can operate within single cells and can also extend through immediate coordination with neighboring cells before the emergence of organism-scale immune systems. The arising establishes the regulated cellular defense architecture through which threat-sensitive recognition and response become structurally admissible.

arisings.name: Cellular Regulatory Networks
arisings.summary: Pattern-level integration of signaling, gene expression, and metabolic control into a unified cellular regulatory architecture.
arisings.description: Cellular Regulatory Networks denote the admissible pattern-level organization in which signaling pathways, gene-expression control, metabolic regulation, and feedback constraints become structurally integrated into a unified architecture governing cellular behavior as a whole. Within Level 4 this arising is classified as a pattern because it consists in the stable relational configuration of interacting control nodes, feedback loops, feedforward motifs, conditional switches, and multi-timescale couplings rather than in a single bounded object or one ongoing process alone. Regulation at this level is distributed across network topology, coupling strength, and dynamical state, so cellular control is no longer attributable to isolated pathways or molecules. This arising establishes the global regulatory pattern through which the cell stabilizes internal conditions, switches between functional modes, maintains robustness under perturbation, and adapts to environmental and internal change.

arisings.name: Endosymbiotic Origin of Organelles
arisings.summary: Pattern-level stable integration of formerly autonomous cells into membrane-bound organelles under host cellular control.
arisings.description: Endosymbiotic Origin of Organelles denotes the admissible pattern-level organization in which previously autonomous prokaryotic cells become stably incorporated into a host cell and transformed into persistent internal functional units such as mitochondria and plastids. Within Level 4 this arising is classified as a pattern because it consists in a durable relational configuration of constrained coexistence, metabolic coupling, genetic coordination, regulated inheritance, and hierarchical control between host and endosymbiont-derived subsystems. The arising is therefore not treated as a single historical event but as a reproducible organizational pattern in which partial cellular autonomy is transferred into a higher-level integrated cellular architecture. This pattern establishes internally differentiated energetic and metabolic organelle systems that remain physically bounded yet systemically subordinated to host-level regulation.

arisings.name: Secretory Pathway and Intracellular Protein Sorting
arisings.summary: Process-level cellular routing regime for modification, targeting, and delivery of proteins within and outside the cell.
arisings.description: Secretory Pathway and Intracellular Protein Sorting denote the admissible process-level organization in which vesicular transport, compartmentalization, molecular recognition, and quality-control mechanisms are integrated into a coherent cellular routing regime. Within Level 4 this arising is classified as a process because it consists in the ongoing targeting, modification, packaging, trafficking, sorting, and delivery of newly synthesized proteins toward specific intracellular destinations or toward secretion. This process transforms protein synthesis from a generic production activity into a spatially and functionally structured cellular operation governed by targeting signals, sorting receptors, vesicular pathways, and organelle-specific routing logic. The arising establishes the regulated transport architecture through which protein localization, organelle identity, controlled secretion, and spatial specialization of biochemical function become reliably admissible.

arisings.name: Cellular Sensory Systems and Environmental Adaptation
arisings.summary: Process-level cellular sensing and adaptive reconfiguration in response to changing environmental and internal conditions.
arisings.description: Cellular Sensory Systems and Environmental Adaptation denote the admissible process-level organization in which membrane-associated receptors, intracellular signaling pathways, and regulatory networks are integrated into a coherent regime for detecting environmental and internal conditions and translating them into coordinated cellular responses. Within Level 4 this arising is classified as a process because it consists in the ongoing sensing, amplification, interpretation, and regulatory conversion of cues such as nutrients, toxins, physical parameters, and signaling molecules into adaptive changes in metabolism, gene expression, transport activity, and structural organization. Adaptation at this level is implemented as regulated reconfiguration of cellular processes and priorities rather than as overt behavioral action. This arising establishes the cellular-scale sensing and adaptation regime required for sustained viability and functional optimization under changing constraints.

arisings.name: Cell-State Control of Metabolic Flux
arisings.summary: Property-level distribution of metabolic flux control over substrate and metabolite levels, allosteric effectors and enzyme abundance, so that pathway fluxes follow the cell's nutrient and energetic state.
arisings.description: Cell-State Control of Metabolic Flux denotes the admissible property-level condition in which flux through cellular metabolic pathways is set jointly by substrate and product concentrations, allosteric effectors, covalent modification and enzyme abundance, with control distributed across the network rather than located in single rate-limiting steps. Within Level 4 this arising is classified as a property because flux control is a system-level attribute of the integrated metabolic network and cannot be assigned to any one enzyme. This arising establishes how cellular nutrient, energetic and signalling state is translated into coordinated pathway use, without a causal force beyond the physically realized state variables.

arisings.name: Intracellular Spatial Organization and Organelle Positioning
arisings.summary: Property-level non-random arrangement of organelles and macromolecular assemblies inside the cell, produced by cytoskeletal tracks, motors, anchoring and membrane contact sites.
arisings.description: Intracellular Spatial Organization and Organelle Positioning denotes the admissible property-level condition in which organelles and macromolecular assemblies occupy organelle-specific, non-random positions and contacts within the cell, set by cytoskeletal tracks and their modification state, motor activity, anchoring and membrane contact sites. Within Level 4 this arising is classified as a property because it is a persistent cell-scale arrangement rather than the transport process that produces it. This arising establishes the spatial order through which local concentrations, contacts between organelles and cell polarity become reproducible features of the cell.

arisings.name: Apoptotic Programmed Cell Death
arisings.summary: Process-level regulated self-elimination in which death-receptor or mitochondrial signals switch a cell, after a variable delay, into caspase-driven dismantling.
arisings.description: Apoptotic Programmed Cell Death denotes the admissible process-level regime through which a cell responds to extrinsic death-receptor signals or to intrinsic damage and stress signals by activating a switch-like caspase cascade, with mitochondrial outer-membrane permeabilization where the route requires it, followed by orderly dismantling of its own structure. Within Level 4 this arising is classified as a process because it consists in a temporally ordered sequence of signal integration, variable-delay commitment and execution. The timing of commitment varies from cell to cell and depends on history, and signs of execution are not universally irreversible: removal of the inducer can allow recovery in some preparations. This arising establishes regulated self-elimination as a cellular fate distinct from division, arrest and differentiation, which multicellular organization recruits for development, tissue turnover and removal of damaged or infected cells.

arisings.name: Autophagy and Local Degradation of Subcellular Components
arisings.summary: Process-level cellular recycling regime enabling targeted sequestration, degradation, and reuse of damaged or surplus subcellular components.
arisings.description: Autophagy and Local Degradation of Subcellular Components denote the admissible process-level organization in which cellular signaling, membrane dynamics, and quality-control mechanisms are integrated into a regulated internal recycling regime. Within Level 4 this arising is classified as a process because it consists in the ongoing recognition, sequestration, isolation, degradation, and molecular reuse of damaged proteins, macromolecular complexes, and organelles within the cell. This process reshapes internal composition in response to metabolic demand, stress conditions, and damage accumulation, linking homeostatic maintenance with adaptive resource reallocation. Autophagy is therefore treated as an active cell-level control process rather than a passive decay mechanism. This arising establishes the regulated degradative and recycling architecture through which internal renewal and selective component turnover become structurally admissible.

arisings.name: Cellular Membrane Potential and Electrochemical Gradients
arisings.summary: Property-level transmembrane electrical potential that, together with ion concentration gradients, constitutes the electrochemical driving force (proton- or sodium-motive force) used for transport, energy coupling, signalling and motility.
arisings.description: Cellular Membrane Potential and Electrochemical Gradients denotes the admissible property-level condition in which pump-sustained ion concentration differences, selective membrane permeability and metabolic energy conversion are integrated into a persistent transmembrane electrochemical regime at the cellular level. Within Level 4 this arising is classified as a property because it consists in the stable possession of a transmembrane electrical potential that, together with ion and proton concentration gradients, forms the electrochemical driving force of the cell. This driving force powers secondary active transport, chemiosmotic ATP synthesis and flagellar rotation; the potential itself is a dynamic, condition-dependent state, distinct from the pH gradient and from the full driving force. This arising establishes a system-level electrochemical property through which transport, energy coupling, signalling and motility across the cell boundary are coordinated by the organized state of the cell.

arisings.name: Phototransduction Cascade
arisings.summary: Process-level cellular transduction regime converting a photochemical event into a regulated change of membrane potential.
arisings.description: Phototransduction Cascade denotes the admissible process-level organization in which an initial photochemical event is amplified, temporally shaped, and converted into a regulated change of membrane potential through a coordinated sequence of biochemical and biophysical steps. Within Level 4 this arising is classified as a process because it consists in the ongoing transductive conversion of photon absorption into cellular electrical signaling via photopigment isomerization, G-protein activation, enzymatic amplification, second-messenger modulation, ion-channel regulation, and adaptive feedback. This process implements gain control, noise suppression, temporal integration, and state-dependent adjustment, transforming discrete photon capture into a robust cell-scale electrical output suitable for downstream neural processing. The arising establishes a specialized cellular sensory transduction regime that is more structured than generic ion-channel activity and depends on an integrated multistage cascade architecture.

arisings.name: Innate Immune Pattern Recognition and Damage-Associated Inflammatory Signaling
arisings.summary: Process-level cellular inflammatory regime in which endogenous damage cues and related innate pattern-recognition inputs are detected and translated into regulated inflammatory signaling.
arisings.description: Innate Immune Pattern Recognition and Damage-Associated Inflammatory Signaling denote the admissible process-level organization through which stressed, damaged, or dysregulated cells trigger innate inflammatory activation by exposing or releasing endogenous danger signals and engaging pattern-recognition-dependent signaling pathways. Within Level 4 this arising is classified as a process because it consists in the ongoing detection, discrimination, amplification, thresholding, and regulated propagation of damage-related inflammatory cues through innate sensing architectures and downstream signaling modules. This arising establishes the cellular transition regime through which homeostatic disturbance becomes translated into regulated inflammatory activation and local immune recruitment.
